Fact.Name: Has Form 1099-DIV box 3, 9, or 10 distributions that may need Form 8949
Fact.Description: Complete-safe disclosure trigger for a Form 1099-DIV return-of-capital or liquidation distribution whose basis may be exhausted. When dividendReports reports a positive box 3, 9, or 10 amount, the filer must review the stock's remaining basis and enter any resulting gain through the existing Form 8949 transaction flow. This fact does not compute the basis exhaustion or add a capital gain: the dictionary has no lot or sale date for these holdings, so it is a prompt and route only. Complete false when the dividendReports trigger is unanswered or false.

Fact.Name: Has capital gains or losses
Fact.Description: Whether the filer has capital gains or losses to report on Schedule D. Gate for the Schedule D intake.

Fact.Name: Claims capital gains or losses
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /hasCapitalGainsOrLosses is answered and true (IsComplete pattern, as qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness). A SECOND DISJUNCT arrives with Form 8621: the gate is also true when the return carries at least one Form 8621 fund and that form produces a nonzero capital component (the section 1291 excess-distribution and section 1296 mark-to-market legs, form8621:/form8621LongTermGain or form8621:/form8621ShortTermLoss), so Schedule D applies on that return without the filer answering /hasCapitalGainsOrLosses at all. A THIRD disjunct - /hasForm8949Transactions (an answered, non-empty collection) or an answered line 1a / 8a shortcut row (/scheduleDLine1aRowPresent, /scheduleDLine8aRowPresent) - so entered transactions are no longer discarded by an unanswered or "No" /hasCapitalGainsOrLosses. Measured over the 70 committed fixtures that seed the collection: 7 flip false to true (sd-r35-part1/part2-box-line-totals, the four b18-s351-* cases and income/sdnr-form8949-rows-itemised-not-exempt), each a return with real Form 8949 rows whose line 7 was $0 at base.

Fact.Name: Net short-term capital gain or loss
Fact.Description: The current-year net short-term gain or (loss) covering Schedule D lines 4 and 5 collapsed (Form 8949 detail filer-supplied). Line 7 proper is /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover (this writable plus line 1a plus the computed line-4 legs /scheduleDLine4ShortTermGainFromOtherForms, minus the line-6 carryover); this writable must EXCLUDE the prior-year carryover. May be negative. LINE 1a IS OUT OF THIS FIGURE. Schedule D line 1a (the no-adjustment 1099-B/1099-DA shortcut row) has its own dedicated intake, /writableScheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss, which reaches line 7 through /scheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss. A filer who also folds the same transactions into this writable is counted twice; the direction that matters is a doubled LOSS, which inflates both the IRC 1211(b) $3,000/$1,500 deduction and the carryover into next year. WHAT THIS WRITABLE ACTUALLY HOLDS: line 4, "Short-term gain from Form 6252 and short-term gain or (loss) from Forms 4684, 6781, and 8824" — except the Form 4684 part of line 4, which has its own fact (form4684:/netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD, added into /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend, never into this writable) — and line 5, the K-1 short-term net. A filer or a successor who folded a Form 4684 line-15 short-term net into this figure would count it TWICE; the Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 parts of line 4 have no computed facts of their own and DO still belong here (the print-only /writableScheduleDLine4OtherShortTermGains only puts them on the printed line 4). SCOPED BY U-8949: "lines 4 and 5 collapsed" is what this writable holds when the return itemises NO transaction on /form8949Transactions, which is every return in the corpus. When that collection is non-empty this writable means the NON-ITEMISED REMAINDER of lines 4 and 5, because /netShortTermGainOrLoss ADDS /form8949ShortTermNet (lines 1b, 2 and 3) to /nonForm8949ShortTermRemainder rather than substituting for it. Itemising nothing makes the remainder the whole part, so this is one rule and not two. A filer who itemises a row AND leaves that same row in this figure double-counts and no guard catches it; on a LOSS row that understates tax and inflates both the capital-loss deduction and the carryover, which is the direction that matters. FORM 6252 AND FORM 8824 (2026-09-27): a Form 6252 sale or Form 8824 exchange entered on this return is carried to Schedule D line 4 or 11 by /scheduleDForm6252And8824ShortTermGainOrLoss and /scheduleDForm6252And8824LongTermGainOrLoss; do not include it here as well.

Fact.Name: Net long-term capital gain or loss
Fact.Description: The current-year net long-term gain or (loss) covering Schedule D lines 8b, 9, 10 and 12 collapsed. Line 15 proper is /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover (this writable plus line 8a plus lines 11 and 13, minus the line-14 carryover); this writable must EXCLUDE the prior-year carryover. May be negative. LINE 8a IS OUT OF THIS FIGURE, the same carve-out the short-term twin makes for line 1a. Schedule D line 8a (the no-adjustment 1099-B/1099-DA shortcut row) has its own dedicated intake, /writableScheduleDLine8aGainOrLoss, which reaches line 15 through /scheduleDLine8aGainOrLoss. A filer who also folds the same transactions into this writable is counted twice; a doubled LOSS inflates both the IRC 1211(b) deduction and the carryover into next year. FOUR of the remaining lines this writable might seem to span have their own facts and enter line 15 OUTSIDE this writable: line 11 (gain from Form 4797 Part I, as form4797:/section1231LtcgPortion, plus the Form 4684 line-15 long-term leg, as form4684:/netLongTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD), line 13 (capital gain distributions, as dividendReports:/capitalGainDistributions and form8814:/form8814TotalLine10CapitalGainDistributions) — all three added into /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend — and line 14 (the long-term carryover), subtracted there. Line 11's own text names four sources — "Gain from Form 4797, Part I; long-term gain from Forms 2439 and 6252; and long-term gain or (loss)" / "from Forms 4684, 6781, and 8824" — and only the Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 parts of it are carried by this writable. FORM 2439 BOX 1a IS OUT OF THIS FIGURE TOO. Without this, the same box would be entered here for line 15 and again in /writableScheduleDLine11OtherLongTermGains for the printed line, unreconciled. Box 1a now enters line 15 ONCE, through form2439:/form2439ScheduleDLine11LongTermCapitalGainOrZero, added at /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend the way the Form 4797 and Form 4684 legs are, per notice, VOID and wrong-year notices excluded. A filer with a Form 2439 notice list who also folds box 1a into this writable is counted twice, exactly as with line 8a above; the graph cannot detect it inside a collapsed net, so the exclusion is BY CONSTRUCTION and stated to the application. SCOPED BY U-8949, and this qualifies the line-by-line enumeration above rather than replacing it: that enumeration is what this writable holds when the return itemises NO transaction on /form8949Transactions. When that collection is non-empty this writable means the NON-ITEMISED REMAINDER of lines 8b, 9, 10 and 12 — because /netLongTermGainOrLoss ADDS /form8949LongTermNet (lines 8b, 9 and 10) to /nonForm8949LongTermRemainder. Itemising nothing makes the remainder the whole part. The same unguardable double-count and the same loss-side direction apply as on the short-term twin. The Box D/J, E/K and F/L totals named above are, on a detail return, carried per transaction by /form8949Transactions — the ledger row oos-scheduled-form8949-per-transaction is DISCHARGED by that collection, this writable remaining the fallback intake. FORM 6252 AND FORM 8824 (2026-09-27): a Form 6252 sale or Form 8824 exchange entered on this return is carried to Schedule D line 4 or 11 by /scheduleDForm6252And8824ShortTermGainOrLoss and /scheduleDForm6252And8824LongTermGainOrLoss; do not include it here as well.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 transactions
Fact.Description: The per-transaction Form 8949 detail: one item per row of Part I or Part II. OPTIONAL, and NOT exclusive of the collapsed nets — this collection and /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss / /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss are ADDED, never chosen between, because the collapsed writables carry Schedule D lines the Form 8949 totals never reach (lines 1a, 4, 5 short; 8a, 11 and 12 long). See the block comment above this fact for the printed line-by-line argument. EXHAUSTIVENESS IS NOT ASSUMED AND IS THE FILER'S OBLIGATION, stated here because nothing mechanical can check it: whatever is entered as a transaction here must NOT also be folded into the collapsed writable for the same part, and whatever is NOT entered here must still be. The form itself invites the partial case — line 1a lets a filer leave the no-adjustment 1099-B totals off Form 8949 entirely, so entering only the two rows that need a column (g) adjustment is a normal, correct return, and the rest belongs in the remainder. A filer who itemises some rows AND leaves the whole net in the remainder double-counts, and no guard in this dictionary catches it. THE DIRECTION OF THAT ERROR IS ASYMMETRIC, and one side of it is the one that matters. Double-counting a GAIN row overstates capital gain and therefore overstates tax — adverse, but self-limiting, because the filer is the party who notices. Double-counting a LOSS row is the dangerous half: it overstates capital loss, understates tax, inflates the IRC 1211(b) $3,000/$1,500 deduction against ordinary income AND inflates the capital-loss carryover this module computes into next year — so one duplicated loss row propagates ACROSS tax years, and nobody is positioned to notice. Stated in the direction rather than as a symmetric "double-counts", because that is the standard this module holds itself to elsewhere (../writableIsLongTerm defaults SHORT precisely because that is the taxpayer-adverse direction).

Fact.Name: Held more than one year (Form 8949 Part II) — attested fallback
Fact.Description: TRUE when the filer attests this transaction belongs in Part II (long-term), FALSE for Part I (short-term). /isLongTerm reads this ONLY when it cannot compute the answer itself from ../writableDateAcquired and ../writableDateSold — the two dates are printed on the same row (columns (b) and (c)) and IRC 1222(1)-(4) defines the split by the objective holding period, so a computed answer overrides a CONTRADICTORY attested one here whenever both dates are entered. This writable stays the answer of record for the two cases the dates cannot cover: either date left unanswered (including a filer who wrote "VARIOUS" in column (b) for a block of stock or digital assets acquired on several dates — the instructions require the filer to self-attest the Part I/Part II split in that case, "you must still report the short-term gain (or loss) on the sale on Part I and the long-term gain (or loss) on Part II") and inherited property, which is answered on ../writableIsInheritedProperty instead and always resolves long-term regardless of what stands here. Unanswered here (and no date, and no inheritance) is treated as SHORT-term by /isLongTerm, which is the taxpayer-ADVERSE default and is deliberate: a short-term gain is taxed at ordinary rates, so silence cannot buy a preferential rate. Form 1099-B box 2 (Short-term / Long-term / Ordinary gain or loss checkboxes). UNANSWERED (no date, no inheritance) is NO LONGER treated as short-term - /isLongTerm is INCOMPLETE until this is answered; /isLongTermAttested says why the adverse-default rationale did not hold for a loss. The application must ask Part I / Part II whenever both dates cannot be collected.

Fact.Name: Property acquired by inheritance (Form 8949 column (b) "INHERITED")
Fact.Description: Whether this transaction disposes of property the filer acquired by inheritance, entered on the printed form by writing "INHERITED" in column (b) instead of a date. IRC 1223(9) treats such a disposition as held more than 1 year — long-term — WITHOUT regard to the actual dates of death and disposition, provided the person's basis in the property is determined under section 1014 (the standard fair-market-value-at-death basis) and the disposition occurs within 1 year after the decedent's death. This graph does not model the section 1014/within-1-year conditions separately: the instructions' own column (b) guidance states the "INHERITED" entry unconditionally for property "acquired by inheritance", so answering TRUE here is read as the filer's attestation that the §1223(9) conditions are met, the same posture the printed form takes. TRUE overrides both the computed date comparison and ../writableIsLongTerm — see /isLongTerm. Unanswered defaults to NOT inherited (complete-safe FALSE via /isInheritedProperty), which is the taxpayer-ADVERSE default consistent with every other holding-period default in this collection.

Fact.Name: Property acquired by inheritance (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsInheritedProperty when answered, else FALSE. The complete-safe alias /isLongTerm reads to decide whether the §1223(9) override applies.

Fact.Name: Held more than one year, attested only (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsLongTerm when answered, else FALSE — the FALLBACK /isLongTerm reads when it cannot compute the holding period from the two printed dates and the item is not attested inherited property. Kept as its own named fact, unchanged from the module's original complete-safe alias, so the fallback is the same computation it always was and a reader can see exactly what /isLongTerm falls back TO. THE FALSE default is gone - this is now ../writableIsLongTerm bare, INCOMPLETE when unanswered. The old rationale ("a short-term default is taxpayer-adverse") held only for a GAIN: a short-term LOSS offsets ordinary-rate short-term gain first, which is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, so silence was buying something in half the cases. The document-only item (../transactionEntered FALSE) still sorts short-term with $0 amounts, decided in /isLongTerm, not here.

Fact.Name: Calendar years between column (b) and column (c)
Fact.Description: ../writableDateSold's year minus ../writableDateAcquired's year. An intermediate for /heldMoreThanOneYearByDates: reused by both the "more than one full calendar year apart" test and the "exactly one calendar year apart, so compare month and day" tie-break, rather than repeating the subtraction. Only meaningful when both dates are answered; /isLongTerm never reads this fact unless it has already confirmed that with its own IsComplete guards, so an unanswered date here never has to resolve.

Fact.Name: Held more than one year, computed from columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableDateSold falls more than one full year after ../writableDateAcquired, applying IRC 1222(1)-(4) and Pub 550's own day-after-acquisition holding-period rule to the two dates the collection already holds: "To determine how long you held the investment property, begin counting on the date after the day you acquired the property. The day you disposed of the property is part of your holding period," so a disposition on the exact one-year anniversary of acquisition is short-term (held for "not more than 1 year") and one day later is long-term — Pub 550's own worked example holds property bought January 31, 2024: sold January 29, 2025 is "not more than 1 year" (short-term), sold February 6, 2025 is "more than 1 year" (long-term). Computed by calendar-date component comparison rather than a fixed 365/366-day offset, so a February 29 acquisition or a disposition in a different leap pattern is exact rather than approximated: more than one full year apart (the years differ by more than 1), OR exactly one year apart AND the sold month/day is strictly later than the acquired month/day. /isLongTerm reads this ONLY when both dates are answered and the item is not attested inherited property; a contradictory ../writableIsLongTerm attestation is OVERRIDDEN by this computed answer in that case, because the two dates printed on the same row are the objective test IRC 1222 states and an inconsistent attestation cannot change the statute's answer.

Fact.Name: Held more than one year (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Derives the Part I/Part II split IRC 1222(1)-(4) states, in priority order: inherited property (../isInheritedProperty, IRC 1223(9)) is ALWAYS long-term regardless of the dates or the attested Boolean; otherwise, when both ../writableDateAcquired and ../writableDateSold are answered, the split is COMPUTED from them (../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates), which overrides a contradictory ../writableIsLongTerm because the two dates printed on the same row are the statute's own objective test; and only when a date is unanswered — including a "VARIOUS"-dated block, which the instructions route back to a self-attested Part I/Part II split — does this fall back to ../isLongTermAttested, FALSE by default (the taxpayer-ADVERSE posture: a short-term gain is taxed at ordinary rates, so silence cannot buy a preferential rate). (1) both dates answered but REVERSED (sold before acquired, ../datesInChronologicalOrder FALSE) is INCOMPLETE, not a computed short-term; (2) the fallback is ../isLongTermAttested WITHOUT its FALSE default - an item with any Form 8949 column answered and no attestation is INCOMPLETE, and only a document-only item (../transactionEntered FALSE, the section-1256-only Form 1099-B) is short-term by default so that its $0 columns keep sorting as they always did.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (d) — proceeds (sales price), writable
Fact.Description: Column (d), "Proceeds" "(sales price)". No floor: a short sale or a return-of-capital adjustment can leave it at zero, and the form applies no minimum. Form 1099-B box 1d (Proceeds).

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (d) — proceeds (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableProceeds when answered, else $0. Complete-safe so an unfinished item contributes a computable row rather than making the whole net unresolvable. THE else-$0 fallback is gone for a row that has STARTED (../transactionEntered): a missing proceeds figure stays INCOMPLETE, because $0 proceeds against a stated basis manufactured a loss of the whole basis. $0 is still the answer for a document-only Form 1099-B item (no Form 8949 column answered, the section-1256-only shape) and for the blank column of an item answered as single-amount reporting (../singleAmountReporting: the IRS row for a gain or loss whose sales price or basis is not known - the known gain in column (d), or the known loss in column (e), the other column blank). An explicit $0 is an answer, not a blank.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (e) — cost or other basis, writable
Fact.Description: Column (e), "Cost or other basis". Entered as the broker reported it when the broker reported it; where that figure is WRONG the form does not have the filer fix it here — the Note under Part I says to "enter in column (e) the basis as reported to the IRS, and" "enter an adjustment in column (g) to correct the basis", which is why the basis-correction code B moves through column (g) in this model too. Form 1099-B box 1e (Cost or other basis).

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (e) — cost or other basis (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableCostBasis when answered, else $0. THE else-$0 fallback is gone for a row that has STARTED (../transactionEntered): a missing basis stays INCOMPLETE, because a $0 basis against stated proceeds manufactured a gain of the whole proceeds - node case form8949-item-partly-entered-stays-incomplete (formerly ...-complete-safe) and the two d052-form1099b-* fixtures were CORRECTED from a $1,000 gain to Incomplete. $0 is still the answer for a document-only item and for the blank column under ../singleAmountReporting. An explicit $0 is an answer, not a blank.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (f) — code(s) from the instructions, writable
Fact.Description: Column (f), "Code(s) from" "instructions" — the letter or letters that EXPLAIN the column (g) adjustment: W for a wash sale, B for a basis correction, Q for a section 1202 exclusion, E for selling expenses, H for the excluded gain on a main home, and the rest of the instructions' table. Entered as the filer would write them on the form: "If more than" "one code applies, enter all the codes that apply in alphabetical" "order (for example, "BOQ"). Don't separate the codes by a space" "or comma." NOTHING IN THIS DICTIONARY READS THIS FACT, and that is faithful rather than lazy. On the printed form the whole of the arithmetic lives in column (g) — column (f) exists "In order to explain any adjustment to gain (or loss) in column (g)" — so the codes label an amount that this model already computes with. The DETERMINATION behind each code (is this a wash sale under section 1091, how much of a section 1202 gain is excluded) is the filer's, exactly as on paper. Exported so a consumer of this dictionary can render or transmit column (f) without this module inventing a use for it. CODES Y AND Z ARE THE ONE EXCEPTION: a QOF deferral (code Z) or a previously-deferred gain becoming includible (code Y) is answered as a RETURN-LEVEL TOTAL at /writableQofDeferredGainShortTerm / /writableQofDeferredGainLongTerm (code Z) or /writableQofIncludibleGainShortTerm / /writableQofIncludibleGainLongTerm (code Y), which this dictionary DOES read — see /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover and /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover. Entering a code-Y or code-Z row in THIS collection as well double-counts it: the generic column (g) arithmetic below would count the deferral or inclusion a second time, on top of the dedicated QOF total. A code-Y row's OWN sale (columns (b) through (e), the QOF investment's own current-year disposition) belongs in this collection as an ordinary item with column (g) left BLANK; only the previously- deferred amount itself belongs on the dedicated QOF writable, never in this column. THIS column IS now read, by ../adjustmentCodesPresent (a nonempty string) - a code obliges an explicit column (g) amount, $0 included, and a nonzero amount obliges a code. Still not parsed: spelling, order and the code alphabet remain the application's (card 419). The code-Y / code-Z carve-out above is unchanged.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (g) — amount of adjustment, writable
Fact.Description: Column (g). SIGNED, and the sign is the whole of the rule: "Enter in this column any necessary adjustments to gain (or loss)." "Enter negative amounts in parentheses." So a wash-sale disallowed loss is entered POSITIVE (it reduces the loss) and an excluded gain is entered NEGATIVE — the instructions' own worked example enters $220,000 of selling expenses plus excluded gain "as a negative number". Where more than one code applies the filer enters ONE net figure here: "If you entered more than one code in" column (f) on the same row, "enter the net adjustment in column" (g). No floor and no ceiling; the form imposes neither. DOES NOT CARRY A QOF DEFERRAL (code Z) OR INCLUSION (code Y) AMOUNT — see ../writableAdjustmentCodes's Description for why: those two adjustments are answered as return-level totals on the dedicated QOF writables instead, and entering one here as well double-counts it.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (g) — amount of adjustment (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableAdjustmentAmount when answered, else $0 — which is the form's own default: "For most transactions, you don't need to complete columns (f) and (g) and can leave them blank." both columns blank still means $0. A code in column (f) with no amount now stays INCOMPLETE (the codes table says to enter -0- for a code that moves no money, so the amount is always stated), and a nonzero amount with no code stays INCOMPLETE (the column header: "If you enter an amount in column (g), enter a code in column (f)."). ../adjustmentCodesPresent is the presence test; the code itself is still not parsed. Column (g) also carries ../esppBasisCorrectionAdjustment, the code-B correction for an ESPP disqualifying disposition, ADDED to whatever the filer entered by hand. That fact is complete-safe $0 unless the ESPP classification is answered true, so a return that never answers it resolves exactly as before; when it is answered and an ESPP input is missing, this column goes INCOMPLETE with it rather than defaulting to the filer's figure. The printed column (f) must then show the code "B" even where the filer typed no code, and the filer must NOT enter the same correction by hand — see ../esppBasisCorrectionAdjustment's Description for the carve-out and the node case that measures the double count.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (h) — gain or (loss) on this transaction
Fact.Description: The form states the formula on the column header itself: "Subtract column (e)" "from column (d) and" "combine the result" "with column (g)." So (h) = (d) - (e) + (g), with (g) signed. MAY BE NEGATIVE, and carries no Limit for that reason — a loss is the normal case for half this collection. NOT ROUNDED here. Rounding once, at the two nets below, matches where this module already rounds and keeps a hundred one-cent items from rounding a hundred times. NOW gated on ../calculationInputsComplete, so an unfinished row resolves INCOMPLETE instead of manufacturing a number; the arithmetic, and the worksheet-verified home-sale example, are unchanged.

Fact.Name: This transaction's contribution to the Part I (short-term) total
Fact.Description: ../gainOrLoss when the item is short-term, else $0. The two per-item contributions are how this module splits the collection without a Filter: IRC 1222 makes short and long term two different nets, and Form 8949 puts them on two different pages. READS ../isLongTerm through IsComplete - an unknown holding period leaves BOTH per-item contributions INCOMPLETE rather than placing the row on a Part; an incomplete ../gainOrLoss propagates into the selected term.

Fact.Name: This transaction's contribution to the Part II (long-term) total
Fact.Description: ../gainOrLoss when the item is long-term, else $0. The mirror of its short-term twin, and the two are exhaustive and disjoint by construction. READS ../isLongTerm through IsComplete - an unknown holding period leaves BOTH per-item contributions INCOMPLETE rather than placing the row on a Part; an incomplete ../gainOrLoss propagates into the selected term.

Fact.Name: This return reports Form 8949 detail per transaction
Fact.Description: TRUE only when /form8949Transactions is COMPLETE and non-empty. THE ISCOMPLETE WRAPPER IS THE POINT, and this repo has paid for it three times: a CollectionSize over an UNANSWERED collection does not resolve, and this fact gates the two Schedule D nets, which every return must be able to compute. Wrapped, the Switch short-circuits to false and every return that never opens a Form 8949 section behaves exactly as it did before U-8949.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 Part I line 2, column (h) — the short-term total
Fact.Description: The sum of every short-term transaction's column (h). $0 when the collection is unanswered or empty (the IsComplete guard). This is the number Form 8949 Part I line 2 carries to Schedule D lines 1b, 2 and 3 — which this module has always taken on trust as /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss, and now computes when the detail is there. ROUNDED ONCE, here, rather than per item.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 Part II line 2, column (h) — the long-term total
Fact.Description: The Part II mirror of /form8949ShortTermNet: the sum of every long-term transaction's column (h), $0 when the collection is unanswered or empty. Form 8949 Part II line 2 carries it to Schedule D lines 8b, 9 and 10.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Part I amounts NOT itemised on Form 8949 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss when answered, else $0 — the complete-safe alias used ONLY on the branch where per-transaction detail is present. On that branch the writable means the remainder of lines 4 and 5: line 4 (Forms 6252/6781/8824 — the Form 4684 part of line 4 is carved out and enters at /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover as form4684:/netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD, exactly as the Form 4797 leg does on the long-term twin) and line 5 (the K-1 short-term net). LINE 1a IS NOT PART OF THIS REMAINDER: it has its own dedicated intake (/writableScheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss, reaching line 7 through /scheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss) which is added at /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend the same way the Form 4684 leg is, never here. A detail filer with none of the line-4/line-5 amounts leaves this blank and gets $0 rather than an Incomplete return, which is why this alias exists at all. THE FALLBACK BRANCH DOES NOT USE THIS FACT. /netShortTermGainOrLoss reads the writable BARE when there is no detail, deliberately, so a return that answers neither intake stays Incomplete exactly as it did before U-8949 — that Incompleteness is load-bearing for the Form 2555 gate and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 7 guard downstream.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Part II amounts NOT itemised on Form 8949 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss when answered, else $0 — the complete-safe alias used ONLY on the branch where per-transaction detail is present. On that branch the writable means the remainder of line 12 (the K-1 long-term net) and any part of line 11 the shipping legs do not carry — form4797:/section1231LtcgPortion and form4684:/netLongTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD, both added separately at /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover — i.e. Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 (Form 2439 box 1a is its own leg at the same minuend, form2439:/form2439ScheduleDLine11LongTermCapitalGainOrZero, not part of this remainder). LINE 8a IS NOT PART OF THIS REMAINDER: it has its own dedicated intake (/writableScheduleDLine8aGainOrLoss, reaching line 15 through /scheduleDLine8aGainOrLoss) which is added at /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend the same way the Form 4797 and Form 4684 legs are, never here. A detail filer with none of the remaining amounts leaves this blank and gets $0 rather than an Incomplete return, which is why this alias exists at all. THE FALLBACK BRANCH DOES NOT USE THIS FACT. /netLongTermGainOrLoss reads the writable BARE when there is no detail, deliberately, so a return that answers neither intake stays Incomplete exactly as it did before U-8949 — that Incompleteness is load-bearing for the Form 2555 gate and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 7 guard downstream.

Fact.Name: Schedule D lines 1a through 5 — the current-year short-term net, from both intakes
Fact.Description: Form 8949 Part I line 2 column (h) PLUS the non-itemised remainder of Part I (/nonForm8949ShortTermRemainder — lines 1a, 4 and 5) when the return reports per-transaction detail; else /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss alone, read BARE so its completeness behaviour is byte-identical to what /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover saw before U-8949. THE FALLBACK IS THE WHOLE COMPATIBILITY STORY: /hasForm8949Transactions is a complete FALSE on every return that never opens a Form 8949 section, so this fact IS the writable on every scenario in the corpus, resolving and failing to resolve in exactly the same places. THE DETAIL BRANCH ADDS RATHER THAN SUBSTITUTES. Substituting the Form 8949 total for the whole net drops Schedule D lines 1a, 4 and 5, which no Form 8949 ever carries — and the guard that used to accompany the substitution refused the return that tried to supply them, so a filer with brokerage detail AND a Schedule K-1 had no legal path at all. Both halves are fixed here: the branch sums, and the guard is retired. THE FORM 8621 CAPITAL COMPONENT IS NOT HERE. It enters the Part I total one level up, at /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover, so a PFIC-only return — Form 8621 funds present, no Form 8949 detail and no collapsed writable answered — resolves this non-PFIC subtotal as a Complete $0 rather than refusing on the unanswered writable. That first arm is the only behaviour change: on every return that answers the writable or reports Form 8949 detail this fact is exactly what it was.

Fact.Name: Schedule D lines 8a, 8b, 9, 10 and 12 — the current-year long-term net, from both intakes
Fact.Description: The long-term mirror of /netShortTermGainOrLoss: Form 8949 Part II line 2 column (h) plus the non-itemised remainder of Part II (/nonForm8949LongTermRemainder), with the same bare fallback and the same compatibility story. THE NAME IS DELIBERATELY NOT "lines 8a through 14", matching /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss. Line 11's shipping leg (form4797:/section1231LtcgPortion), line 13 (capital gain distributions) and line 14 (the carryover) all enter OUTSIDE this fact, at /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover. What this fact spans is lines 8a, 8b, 9, 10 and 12 — plus, inside the remainder, whatever part of line 11 the Form 4797 leg does not carry, which is the one ragged edge and is named on /nonForm8949LongTermRemainder. THE FORM 8621 CAPITAL COMPONENT IS NOT HERE, for the same reason and with the same shape as on the short-term twin: it enters at /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover, and a PFIC-only return with no Form 8949 detail and no collapsed writable answered resolves this non-PFIC subtotal as a Complete $0.

Fact.Name: Short-term capital loss carryover from 2024 (Schedule D line 6)
Fact.Description:
US8-3: the prior-year short-term capital loss carryover, entered as a POSITIVE amount — the taxpayer transcribes line 8 of their 2024→2025 Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet (i1040sd), computed from the PRIOR year's Schedule D and 1040. OPTIONAL — unanswered means no carryover and line 7 equals the current-year net.
THE OUTBOUND HALF NOW SHIPS TOO, and this paragraph used to say it did not. It read "This year's 2025→2026 carryover is NEXT year's intake worksheet, not a 2025 form line". The 2025→2026 worksheet is now computed in this module — /shortTermCapitalLossCarryoverToNextYear is its line 8, and this fact is where that number is answered on the 2026 return. This writable stays ATTESTED rather than derived, because deriving it would mean reading 2024 state. Nothing is reported or silently defaulted this year.

Fact.Name: Long-term capital loss carryover from 2024 (Schedule D line 14)
Fact.Description: US8-3: the prior-year long-term capital loss carryover, entered as a POSITIVE amount — worksheet line 13 of the 2024→2025 Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet. OPTIONAL; same carry-IN posture as the short-term twin. Carryovers retain their character, so this reduces the LONG-term side (and thereby the preferential-rate net capital gain).

Fact.Name: Complete-safe short-term capital loss carryover floor
Fact.Description: Complete-safe arithmetic view of the prior-year short-term capital loss carryover. The intake is a positive magnitude and its XML minimum is advisory at resolution, so the worksheet-facing view floors any answered negative value at zero. An unanswered intake remains zero.

Fact.Name: Complete-safe long-term capital loss carryover floor
Fact.Description: Complete-safe arithmetic view of the prior-year long-term capital loss carryover. The intake is a positive magnitude and its XML minimum is advisory at resolution, so the worksheet-facing view floors any answered negative value at zero. An unanswered intake remains zero.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 7 — net short-term gain or (loss) after the carryover
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 7: "Combine lines 1a through 6 in column (h)." The current-year short-term net (lines 4 and 5 collapsed, /netShortTermGainOrLoss) plus line 1a (/scheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss, complete-safe $0 unless the filer used the line 1a shortcut row — see /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss's Description for why line 1a is NOT also folded into that writable) plus the Form 4684 line-4 leg (form4684:/netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD, complete-safe $0) plus a QOF inclusion (/qofIncludibleGainShortTerm — Form 8949 code-Y short-term, complete-safe $0), minus the line-6 carryover (a loss, so subtracted) minus a QOF deferral (/qofDeferredGainShortTerm — Form 8949 code-Z short-term, complete-safe $0). Equals /netShortTermGainOrLoss exactly when line 1a, the Form 4684 leg, both QOF terms and the carryover are all unanswered, which is every prior committed scenario. Plus the Form 8621 short-term capital component (form8621:/form8621ShortTermLoss), the short-term half of the section 1291 and section 1296 dispositions, complete-safe $0 on every return with no Form 8621. A filer who reports the same PFIC disposition through a collapsed manual intake must not also enter it there; the module computes it once.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 15 — net long-term gain or (loss) after the carryover
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 15: "Combine lines 8a through 14 in column (h)." The current-year long-term net (lines 8b, 9, 10 and 12 collapsed, /netLongTermGainOrLoss) plus line 8a (/scheduleDLine8aGainOrLoss, complete-safe $0 unless the filer used the line 8a shortcut row — see /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss's Description for why line 8a is NOT also folded into that writable) plus line 13 (capital gain distributions: Form 1099-DIV box 2a as dividendReports:/capitalGainDistributions, plus a Form 8814 parent's share of a child's capital gain distributions as form8814:/form8814TotalLine10CapitalGainDistributions — two disjoint populations, so both add) plus line 11 (gain from Form 4797 Part I as form4797:/section1231LtcgPortion, plus the Form 4684 line-15 long-term leg as form4684:/netLongTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD) plus a QOF inclusion (/qofIncludibleGainLongTerm — Form 8949 code-Y long-term, complete-safe $0), minus the line-14 carryover minus a QOF deferral (/qofDeferredGainLongTerm — Form 8949 code-Z long-term, complete-safe $0). Equals /netLongTermGainOrLoss exactly when line 8a and every other addend are unanswered, which is every prior committed scenario. Plus the Form 8621 long-term capital component (form8621:/form8621LongTermGain), the QEF net capital gain and the long-term half of the section 1291 and section 1296 dispositions, complete-safe $0 on every return with no Form 8621. The same amount is what /scheduleDLine11GainFromForm4797AndOtherForms prints in the line-11 cell, so the printed Part II cells and this total carry it exactly once each. A filer who reports the same PFIC disposition through a collapsed manual intake must not also enter it there. LINE 13 is read as the named subtotal /scheduleDLine13CapitalGainDistributions - box 2a plus the Form 8814 share, the same two addends as before, now one quantity shared with the printed line-13 cell. Value-identical on every committed fixture.

Fact.Name: Net capital gain or loss (line 16)
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 16: net short-term plus net long-term, each AFTER its prior-year loss carryover (US8-3; identical to the writables when no carryover). May be negative.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain or (loss) from Form 8949, Part II (writable)
Fact.Description:
28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 1, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 11, verbatim: "Enter the total of all collectibles gain or (loss) from items you reported on Form 8949, Part II". THIS IS A FILER ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION, and that is a modeling consequence rather than a choice: the graph collapses Schedule D lines 8a through 14 into a single /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss (scope ledger oos-scheduled-form8949-per-transaction), so the collectibles SUBSET of that collapsed net is not derivable from anything the graph holds. The filer states it. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /collectiblesGainFromForm8949 downstream. When it is LEFT UNANSWERED the alias falls back to the Form 8949 Part II rows whose Form 1099-B box 3 "Collectibles" checkbox is checked (/collectiblesGainFromForm1099BFlaggedRows), so the broker's own flag is not lost; an answer here replaces that fallback and is not added to it.
SIGN — NO Min $0 LIMIT, DELIBERATELY, and this is the asymmetry that forces line 1 and line 4 to have separate intakes rather than sharing one. The source says "gain or (loss)", so a net collectibles LOSS is a legitimate negative answer here, while the line-4 sibling /dividendReports/*/writableCollectiblesGain is a GAIN reported on Form 1099-DIV box 2d and does carry Min $0. Its line-2 neighbour /writableSection1202ExclusionFromForm8949 carries Min $0 for a third reason again ("Enter as a positive number"). Note that the line-4 SIBLING named above is the box-2d one specifically: line 4's Schedule K-1 leg /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 carries NO floor, because Schedule K-1 box 9b is captioned "Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss)". Three legs of one worksheet cited here, three different sign rules, none of them interchangeable — and the sign always comes from the issuer of the amount, never from the line that collects it.
NOT BOUNDED BY THE COLLAPSED NET IT SPLITS, and the contract asked this fill to say which way it went and why. It leaves the bound to the filer. /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss is a SUM over Form 8949 Part II items of both signs, so the collectibles subset of that sum is not bounded by it in either direction: a filer with a 10,000 collectibles gain and a 12,000 loss on other Part II property has a net of -2,000 and a perfectly correct line 1 of +10,000. A Max limit against the net would refuse that return. There is no acyclic, correct bound available at intake, so none is asserted — the over-claim risk is disclosed here rather than papered over with a limit that is wrong on its own terms.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain or (loss) from Form 8949, Part II
Fact.Description:
28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 1. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm8949, so every return that reports no Form 8949 collectibles item is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this line was a hardcoded $0 leg of the lines 1-4 subtotal.
MAY BE NEGATIVE — this alias passes the answered sign through unchanged. It carries no floor of its own because the worksheet's floor is line 7's ("Combine lines 1 through 6. If zero or less, enter -0-"), applied once at /twentyEightPercentRateGain; flooring here would silently discard the loss the intake exists to capture.
TWO CONSUMERS, BOTH THROUGH ONE SUBTOTAL, and the second one is the surprising half: /twentyEightPercentRateGainLines1Through4 feeds Schedule D line 18 (via /twentyEightPercentRateGain) AND the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 14 (via /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17), which spends the subtotal against line 13. The directions are OPPOSITE: a collectibles LOSS lowers line 18, and by deepening the line-17 combine it also lowers Schedule D line 19. Both movements are pinned.
UNANSWERED ATTESTATION FALLS BACK TO THE FLAGGED ROWS, not to $0. When /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm8949 is unanswered this alias is /collectiblesGainFromForm1099BFlaggedRows: the column (h) total of the Form 8949 Part II rows whose Form 1099-B box 3 "Collectibles" checkbox is answered checked. Box 3 says in terms "If checked, proceeds are from a transaction involving collectibles" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099b--2025.pdf, page 7), and worksheet line 1 is the total of "all collectibles gain or (loss) from items you reported on Form 8949, Part II", so those rows are line 1 items by the broker's own statement. An ANSWERED attestation still governs, because it may carry collectibles no Form 1099-B flagged (a private sale of art) and nothing here can split it; the rows and the attestation are the same money, so they are never added. Two scheduleD node tests pin both arms; the records file names them.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain or (loss) on Form 8949 Part II rows flagged by Form 1099-B box 3
Fact.Description: The sum of /form8949Transactions/*/form1099BCollectiblesGainPartII: the column (h) gain or (loss) of every entered long-term Form 8949 row whose Form 1099-B box 3 "Collectibles" checkbox is answered checked. The fallback arm of /collectiblesGainFromForm8949 when the filer has not stated the worksheet line 1 total. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /twentyEightPercentRateGain, per the Schedule D instruction to round only the total. Complete-safe: $0 when /form8949Transactions was never opened, because a CollectionSum over an unanswered collection does not resolve.

Fact.Name: This row's collectibles gain or (loss) for 28% Rate Gain Worksheet line 1
Fact.Description: ../longTermGainOrLoss (column (h) when the row is long-term, $0 when short-term) when this entered row's Form 1099-B box 3 "Collectibles" checkbox is answered checked, and $0 otherwise. A short-term collectible is not a line 1 item: the worksheet reads Form 8949 Part II only. The box is read IsComplete-first so an unanswered box is $0, never Incomplete; an unknown holding period on a flagged row stays Incomplete through ../longTermGainOrLoss, exactly as the Part II net does.

Fact.Name: Section 1202 exclusion reported on Form 8949, Part II with code Q, other than a Form 1099-DIV box 2c gain (writable): its 28% Rate Gain Worksheet line 2 amount
Fact.Description:
The part of line 2 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet for Schedule D line 18 that no Form 1099-DIV reported: the tier-weighted total of every section 1202 exclusion the filer reported in Form 8949, Part II, column (g) with code Q, other than the exclusion of a Form 1099-DIV box 2c gain. It covers a direct sale of qualified small business stock, a Form 2439 box 1c gain, a long-term installment gain from Form 6252, and a pass-through entity's sale of the stock; the instructions send each of these to the same worksheet line.
Worksheet line 2 asks, as a positive number, for the total of every section 1202 exclusion reported in column (g) of Form 8949, Part II with code Q that is 50 percent of the gain, two-thirds of every such exclusion that is 60 percent of the gain, and one-third of every such exclusion that is 75 percent of the gain, with no entry for an exclusion that is 100 percent of the gain. The filer applies those fractions and enters the result, because the graph does not carry Form 8949 by transaction and cannot tell which exclusion percentage each sale qualified for. A 100 percent exclusion is left out, since a fully excluded gain is not in the 28 percent group.
The Form 1099-DIV box 2c exclusion is dividendReports /section1202ExclusionFromDividends and is added to worksheet line 2 separately, so it is left out here; entering it again counts it twice.
Entered as a positive number (Min $0), unlike its line 1 neighbour /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm8949, which is a signed gain or loss; the exclusion appears on Form 8949 as a negative adjustment, and this intake takes its magnitude. Not bounded by /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss, which nets Part II items of both signs. Read downstream through /section1202ExclusionFromForm8949.

Fact.Name: Section 1202 exclusion from Form 8949, Part II code Q
Fact.Description:
The non-Form-1099-DIV half of 28% Rate Gain Worksheet line 2: /writableSection1202ExclusionFromForm8949 when answered, floored at $0, else $0, so every return without such an exclusion resolves line 2 from its Form 1099-DIV component alone.
LINE 2 IS A SUM OF TWO INDEPENDENT LEGS: this fact and dividendReports /section1202ExclusionFromDividends are separate addends of /twentyEightPercentRateGainLines1Through4, neither gating the other, because a filer can hold both a Form 8949 code Q exclusion (a direct sale, a Form 2439 box 1c gain, an installment or pass-through sale) and a section 1202 fund dividend in the same year.
NON-NEGATIVE, matching the writable's Min $0: resolution does not enforce that limit, so this alias floors an answered negative value at $0 before the exclusion is added to the worksheet. The worksheet's own floor is line 7's, at /twentyEightPercentRateGain.
DIRECTION: a section 1202 exclusion RAISES the 28 percent rate gain, because the worksheet adds the excluded amount back. So this leg can only increase Schedule D line 18 and, through the line 14 read at /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17, only decrease the line 17 offset and so increase or hold Schedule D line 19.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain reported on Form 2439, box 1d (writable)
Fact.Description:
The Form 2439 leg of 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 4, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 11, verbatim: "Enter the total of any collectibles gain reported to you on: ... Form 2439, box 1d". Form 2439 (Notice to Shareholder of Undistributed Long-Term Capital Gains) is the notice a regulated investment company or REIT sends a shareholder for gains it retained and paid tax on rather than distributing; box 1d breaks out the collectibles (28%-rate) part.
A SCALAR TOTAL, NOT A FORM 2439 MODEL, and that is this fill's one renegotiation. The retired contract said "the fill is a Form 2439 unit, not a Schedule D one" because no Form 2439 intake exists anywhere in the graph. The worksheet line does not ask for one: it asks for "the total of any collectibles gain reported to you on ... Form 2439, box 1d", across however many notices the filer received. A single attested total answers the line exactly, introduces no collection, and models no other Form 2439 box — so the deeper Form 2439 unit stays open for the boxes this line does not name (1a, 1b, 2), while the line the graph actually needs stops being a hardcoded $0.
MIN $0, on the source's own words: line 4 says "collectibles GAIN reported to you" with no "(loss)" anywhere in it, unlike line 1 (:905) and line 3 (:914-915), which both say "gain or (loss)". This is the same sign rule the box-2d twin /dividendReports/*/writableCollectiblesGain carries, and for the same reason — a payer reports a gain, not a net. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /collectiblesGainFromForm2439 downstream.
ITS BOX 1c TWIN LANDED IN THE SAME COMMIT: /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm2439 is the unrecaptured section 1250 gain from the SAME notice, feeding the OTHER worksheet (Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 11). Both contracts said neither should land alone; neither did.
THE paragraph above that says "no Form 2439 intake exists anywhere in the graph" is NO LONGER TRUE, kept only as the record of why this scalar was built: form2439:/form2439Forms (block 15) records every Copy B box per notice, and since this unit the worksheet line reads that list. THIS SCALAR IS THE LEGACY PATH. /collectiblesGainFromForm2439 reads it only while /form2439Forms is unanswered or empty; once a notice is listed the list governs (form2439:/form2439IncludedCollectiblesGain, VOID and wrong-year notices excluded, a blank box 1d counting $0), and this writable, if still answered, must equal that total or /knockoutForm2439NoticeTotalsDisagreeWithScheduleDEntries refuses the return. The application should collect Form 2439 through the notice list.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain reported on Form 2439, box 1d
Fact.Description:
The Form 2439 leg of 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 4. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm2439, so every return without a Form 2439 is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this leg was a hardcoded $0 term of the lines 1-4 subtotal.
NON-NEGATIVE, matching the writable's Min $0. Resolution does not enforce that XML limit, so the writable fallback explicitly floors an answered negative value at $0 before it reaches the worksheet. The worksheet's own floor is line 7's, applied once at /twentyEightPercentRateGain.
DIRECTION: this leg can only RAISE the 28%-rate gain, which is the opposite of what its line-1 neighbour /collectiblesGainFromForm8949 can do. Through the lines 1-4 subtotal it raises Schedule D line 18 — and, through the line-14 read at /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17, it SHRINKS the line-17 offset and so raises-or-holds Schedule D line 19.
TWO SOURCES, ONE RULE. When the return lists at least one Form 2439 notice (form2439:/hasForm2439Notices) this leg is form2439:/form2439IncludedCollectiblesGain, the box 1d total over the notices that are not VOID and whose RIC or REIT tax year ends in 2025; the scalar above is then not added (it is checked, see the knockout). With no notice list the scalar carries the leg as before, complete-safe $0, so every committed scenario is value-identical. On the list path a live notice with no resolvable year leaves this leg Incomplete (ruling 6).

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain or (loss) from Forms 4684, 6252, 6781 and 8824 (writable)
Fact.Description:
28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 3, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 11, verbatim: "Enter the total of all collectibles gain or (loss) from Form 4684, line 4 (but only if Form 4684, line 15, is more than zero); Form 6252; Form 6781, Part II; and Form 8824". Four forms, one printed line, one attested total.
NO LIMIT OF ANY KIND, and this is the SECOND leg of this worksheet with that property. The source says "gain or (loss)", exactly as line 1 (:905) does — a Form 6781 section 1256 straddle or a Form 8824 like-kind exchange can settle either way — while line 2 says "Enter as a positive number" and line 4 says "collectibles GAIN reported to you". Three sign rules across four lines of one worksheet, which is why none of these legs may share an intake. There is also no upper bound to assert: the four forms are outside the collapsed /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss rather than a subset of it, so unlike the line-1 attestation this one is not even a candidate for a Max against that net.
THE FORM 4684 LEG IS UNREACHABLE FOR ANYONE THIS GRAPH CAN REFUSE, and the retired contract was right to flag it — but the conclusion it drew ("it must be built in the same unit that retires that knockout — never before, or a return the graph currently refuses would start computing") does not follow for an ATTESTATION, because this fact reads nothing from form4684 and gates nothing on it. THE ARGUMENT RUNS THROUGH LINE 4, NOT THROUGH LINE 15, and the difference matters because the obvious shortcut is wrong. The obvious shortcut would be "line 15 above zero requires a Form 4684 line-4 gain": that is FALSE. Line 15 has three branches (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 1), and its THIRD — line 13 less than line 14, with qualified disaster losses subject to the $500 reduction — puts a positive amount on line 15 derived entirely from LOSSES, with line 13 possibly zero. So the gate can open with no gain at all. The sound argument is about the amount the worksheet actually asks for, which is Form 4684 LINE 4, the per-event gain. Either the filer has a line-4 gain or they do not. If they do not, line 13 ("Add the amounts on line 4 of all Forms 4684", :49) is zero and there is nothing to include, whatever line 15 says. If they do, and they claim a casualty loss, form4684 /knockoutCasualtyGain fires — it triggers on ANY line-4 gain, without waiting for the gains to exceed the losses — and it carries BlockSubmissionOnTrue, so the return is REFUSED before any of this is read. No refused return starts computing. A filer who claims no casualty loss holds no /casualtyEvents at all, so the graph models no Form 4684 for them and this attestation is that filer's only channel. Deliberately NO dependency on the knockout: gating an attestation on a submission-blocking flag would make the intake Incomplete-by-contagion for the population it exists to serve.
THE OTHER THREE FORMS HAVE NO INTAKE AND NO KNOCKOUT — Form 6252 (installment sales), Form 6781 Part II (section 1256 straddles) and Form 8824 (like-kind exchanges) are simply absent from the graph, so before this fact a filer with one of them had no way to report the collectibles amount at all and line 3 silently entered $0. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /collectiblesGainFromOtherForms downstream.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain or (loss) from Forms 4684, 6252, 6781 and 8824
Fact.Description:
28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 3. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableCollectiblesGainFromOtherForms, so every return without one of those four forms is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this line was a hardcoded $0 leg of the lines 1-4 subtotal.
MAY BE NEGATIVE — this alias passes the answered sign through unchanged. It carries no floor of its own because the worksheet's floor is line 7's ("Combine lines 1 through 6. If zero or less, enter -0-"), applied once at /twentyEightPercentRateGain; flooring here would silently discard the loss the intake exists to capture, exactly as it would at line 1.
DIRECTION, BOTH WAYS, IN BOTH CONSUMERS. Through the lines 1-4 subtotal an answered GAIN raises Schedule D line 18 and, by shrinking the line-17 offset, raises Schedule D line 19; an answered LOSS lowers both.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1's collectibles (28%) gain or (loss)
Fact.Description:
This Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S) item's contribution to the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 4: box 9b as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableK1065Box9bCollectiblesGain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. Complete-safe, so a /formK1s item recorded for its ordinary income alone still contributes a Complete $0 and the CollectionSum over the collection stays Complete.
SIGNED, WITH NO FLOOR, and that is deliberate: box 9b is captioned "Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss)" and its instructions say "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18". Removing the Min $0 from /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 applies with the same force here; flooring would silently discard the loss the box exists to report. Its §1250 sibling ../unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD IS floored, because box 9c prints no loss.
A scheduleD fact living on scheduleE's /formK1s collection, the cross-module shape qbi:/formK1s/*/sstbPtpQualifiedAmount uses on the same collection.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1 answers box 9b
Fact.Description: True when THIS /formK1s item answered box 9b, the collectibles (28%) gain or (loss). It is an IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../collectiblesGainForScheduleD, because that bridge is Complete on every item and a predicate built from it would be true for a K-1 recorded for its ordinary income alone. Counted by /collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered, which decides whether worksheet line 4's K-1 leg is derived from the rows or falls back to the attested total /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1's unrecaptured section 1250 gain
Fact.Description:
This Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S) item's contribution to Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 LINE 5, "Enter the total of any amounts reported to you on a Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation as 'unrecaptured section 1250 gain'": box 9c as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableK1065Box9cUnrecapturedSection1250Gain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. Complete-safe.
LINE 5, NOT LINE 11, and the distinction is the whole point of having two facts. Line 5 sits inside the worksheet's lines 1 through 9 block, which line 7 caps at "the gain from Form 4797, line 7" and line 8 then reduces; the estate or trust K-1's box 4c is worksheet line 11, a DIRECT addend of line 13 with no cap. Crossing them would move a capped amount into an uncapped line. The estate or trust twin is /form1041K1s/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD.
NON-NEGATIVE. Box 9c is captioned "Unrecaptured section 1250 gain" with no "(loss)" branch, and the attested total this bridge stands in for, /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1, carries Min $0 on its intake. The scheduleE leaf carries no such limit, so the floor is applied here rather than inherited, which keeps the derived arm and the attestation arm on the same footing. This is the exact asymmetry /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 documents: box 9b is signed, box 9c is not.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1 answers box 9c
Fact.Description: True when THIS /formK1s item answered box 9c, the unrecaptured section 1250 gain. An IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD, for the reason ../reportsCollectiblesGainForScheduleD gives. Counted by /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1RowsAnswered, which decides whether worksheet line 5 is derived from the rows or falls back to the attested total.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's 28% rate gain
Fact.Description:
This Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) item's contribution to the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 4: box 4b as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox4b28PercentRateGain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. The form's own back-of-form routing table sends box 4b to "28% Rate Gain Worksheet, line 4 (Schedule D instructions)", the same worksheet line the partnership K-1's box 9b reaches through ../../formK1s/*/collectiblesGainForScheduleD. Complete-safe.
SIGNED, WITH NO FLOOR, for the reason the partnership twin gives: worksheet line 4 collects three sources and the sign of each is set by the document that issues it. Box 4b is the beneficiary's share of the estate's or trust's 28%-rate gain, which section 1(h) computes as a net that can be a loss.
A scheduleD fact living on scheduleE's /form1041K1s collection.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1 answers box 4b
Fact.Description: True when THIS /form1041K1s item answered box 4b, the 28% rate gain. An IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../collectiblesGainForScheduleD. Counted by /collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's unrecaptured section 1250 gain
Fact.Description:
This Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) item's contribution to Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 LINE 11: box 4c as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox4cUnrecapturedSection1250Gain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. The form's own routing table sends box 4c to "Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet, line 11 (Schedule D instructions)". Complete-safe.
LINE 11, NOT LINE 5. Line 11 is a DIRECT addend of line 13 ("Add lines 9 through 12") with no intervening cap, so the whole amount reaches Schedule D line 19; the partnership and S corporation twin /formK1s/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD is worksheet line 5, inside the lines 1 to 9 block that line 7 caps at the Form 4797 line 7 gain. The two must not be crossed.
NON-NEGATIVE. Box 4c is captioned "Unrecaptured section 1250 gain" with no "(loss)" branch and the attested total it stands in for, /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1, carries Min $0; the scheduleE leaf carries no limit, so the floor is applied here.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1 answers box 4c
Fact.Description: True when THIS /form1041K1s item answered box 4c, the unrecaptured section 1250 gain. An IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD. Counted by /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromEstateOrTrustK1RowsAnswered.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 11 code D long term capital loss carryover
Fact.Description:
The total of the box 11 "Final year deductions" rows on THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) whose printed letter code is D, the unused LONG-term capital loss carryover a terminating estate or trust passes to the beneficiary succeeding to its property under section 1212. The box is recorded as a row list and every row of it is read, however many the K-1 lists; this fact sums a per-row part over the rows: a row contributes its amount only when the row's code AND its amount are both answered and the code is D, and $0 otherwise. Complete-safe, and the code is TESTED rather than assumed because box 11 is a coded row box carrying six different codes (A, B, C, D, E, F) that reach five different forms — the same shape scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box9DirectlyApportionedDeductions uses for box 9.
A POSITIVE MAGNITUDE, the convention /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear already uses for the Schedule D line 14 carryover that shares both worksheet lines with it. Its consumer /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverFromForm1041K1 subtracts it at the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet line 5 and adds it as a magnitude at Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 16, exactly as the line 14 carryover is treated in the same two places.
CODE D ONLY. The routing table sends box 11 code D to three destinations at once — "Schedule D, line 12; line 5 of the wksht. for Sch. D, line 18; and line 16 of the wksht. for Sch. D, line 19" — and this fact serves the two WORKSHEET destinations. The Schedule D line 12 destination is the print component /writableScheduleDLine12NetLongTermFromScheduleK1, which this unit did not rebody; see the report. The box's other codes belong to other modules and are deliberately not read here: code A to income:/writableSchedule1Line24kExcessDeductionsSection67e, code C to Schedule D line 5, code E to income:/writableNetOperatingLossDeduction and code F to form6251:/writableAlternativeTaxNolCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear. A row coded anything else contributes $0 rather than silently offsetting an amount whose treatment is unknown.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 11 code D long term capital loss carryover: this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /form1041K1s/*/finalYearDeductionEntries as /form1041K1s/*/longTermCapitalLossCarryoverForScheduleD reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is D, both the code and the amount are answered; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: A recorded Schedule K-1 answers its collectibles or 28% rate gain box
Fact.Description:
True when at least one recorded Schedule K-1 answered the box that reaches 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 4: box 9b on a /formK1s partnership or S corporation K-1, or box 4b on a /form1041K1s estate or trust K-1. It is the "was the source answered" predicate that lets /collectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 prefer the recorded rows and keep the attested total /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 as its fallback.
DOUBLE-GUARDED, and both guards are load-bearing. The inner test is a Count over per-item IsComplete flags on the RAW scheduleE leaves. The outer test is an IsComplete on the COLLECTION ROOT, because a Count over a collection the return never opened does not resolve Complete and this fact would then make Schedule D line 18 Incomplete by contagion on every return in the corpus — the failure reconciliation unit X1 hit and documented. Neither /formK1s nor /form1041K1s appears in most scheduleD scenarios, so each collection needs its own guard, defaulting to false. The cross-module IsComplete on a collection root is the shape qbi already uses on scheduleC:/scheduleCs.
THIS BOX ONLY. The predicate deliberately does not ask whether any capital gain box was answered: a filer who records box 9a and attests the collectibles total must keep the attestation.

Fact.Name: A recorded estate or trust Schedule K-1 answers box 4c
Fact.Description:
True when at least one /form1041K1s item answered box 4c, the unrecaptured section 1250 gain that reaches Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 LINE 11. The "was the source answered" predicate behind /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1, which keeps the attested total /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1 as its fallback. Double-guarded exactly as /collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered is, and for the same reason: /form1041K1s is absent from nearly every scenario, so a Count over it must sit inside an IsComplete on the collection root that defaults to false.
THE ESTATE OR TRUST LEG ONLY. The partnership and S corporation leg is worksheet line 5 and has its own predicate, /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1RowsAnswered. The two worksheet lines carry different limits and must not be crossed.

Fact.Name: A recorded partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1 answers box 9c
Fact.Description:
True when at least one /formK1s item answered box 9c, the unrecaptured section 1250 gain that reaches Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 LINE 5. The "was the source answered" predicate behind /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1, which keeps the attested total as its fallback. Double-guarded exactly as /collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered is.
THE PARTNERSHIP AND S CORPORATION LEG ONLY, worksheet line 5, inside the capped lines 1 to 9 block. The estate or trust leg is worksheet line 11 and has its own predicate, /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromEstateOrTrustK1RowsAnswered.

Fact.Name: Long term capital loss carryover from Schedule(s) K-1 (Form 1041), box 11 code D
Fact.Description:
The total across every recorded Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) of the box 11 code D long-term capital loss carryover, stored as a POSITIVE magnitude. Complete-safe: $0 when no /form1041K1s collection was opened, so every return without an estate or trust K-1 is byte-identical to the graph before this fact shipped.
ONE NODE, TWO CONSUMERS, which is exactly what /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1's Description said this leg needed: "a SUBTRACTED carryover appearing on both worksheets at once, so it needs one node serving two consumers". /twentyEightPercentRateGain SUBTRACTS it at 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 5, and /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17 ADDS it as a magnitude at Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 16 (that fact builds the combine as a positive offset, so both worksheet lines reduce their gain by it). Both worksheet lines name TWO sources — "your long-term capital loss carryovers from Schedule D, line 14; and Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), box 11, code D" — so this fact is an ADDITIONAL term beside /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear, not a replacement for it, and there is no attestation to fall back to: none ever existed.
DIRECTION: it can only LOWER Schedule D line 18 and line 19, because it is subtracted on the 28% worksheet and enters the line 17 offset on the §1250 worksheet. Its absence therefore OVER-stated both lines, which is the harm the two interpretation:provisional notes on those facts recorded and this fact retires.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain reported on a Schedule K-1 (writable)
Fact.Description:
The Schedule K-1 leg of 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 4, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 11, verbatim: "Enter the total of any collectibles gain reported to you on: ... Schedule K-1 from a partnership, S corporation, estate, or trust". A pass-through entity that sold collectibles reports the filer's share on the K-1 it issues; the filer transcribes the total.
A SCALAR TOTAL, AND IT INTRODUCES NO SCHEDULE K-1 COLLECTION. Filling this line does not require a K-1 collection. Line 4 asks for "the TOTAL of any collectibles gain reported to you on ... Schedule K-1", one number across every K-1 the filer holds, so an attested total answers it exactly while modelling no K-1 at all. Nothing in the Schedule E Part II follow-on surface — the per-entity basis, at-risk and passive-activity machinery that row is actually about — is touched, brought forward, or made harder by this fact.
WHAT IS STILL COUPLED TO A REAL K-1 INTAKE, so the retired contract's warning is not lost: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 5 (:982-983, the partnership/S-corporation unrecaptured section 1250 leg) sits inside that worksheet's lines 1-9 block, which is capped at line 7 by "the gain from Form 4797, line 7" — a number this module cannot read because form4797 /netSection1231GainOrLoss carries no Export. That block is blocked for a structural reason of its own, not for a K-1 reason. Worksheet line 11's Schedule K-1 (estate or trust) leg (:990-992) is a DIRECT addend and was unblocked by the argument above; it ships as /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1, on the other worksheet. The Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D leg of 28% worksheet line 5 (:920-922) and §1250 worksheet line 16 (:1001-1002) is a SUBTRACTED carryover appearing on both worksheets at once, so it needs one node serving two consumers and is deliberately not contracted here. That node exists. It is /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverFromForm1041K1, a code-keyed sum over the box 11 rows of scheduleE's /form1041K1s collection, and it serves both consumers this fact needs.
NO Min $0 LIMIT. Min $0 read off the Schedule D worksheet line's own wording, "collectibles GAIN reported to you", which has no "(loss)" branch. That is the wrong authority for THIS leg. The worksheet line names three sources and the K-1 leg's sign is set by the K-1's own instructions, which are explicit and signed: "Box 9b. Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss) — Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 in the Instructions for Schedule D (Form 1040)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 16), with the same signed caption on the S-corporation K-1, "8b Collectibles (28%) gain (loss)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1120ssk.pdf, page 1). A partnership or S corporation that disposed of collectibles at a loss reports that loss, and the filer is told to put it on this very line. Under the clamp a correct negative answer was rewritten to $0 and the loss was unrepresentable: 1099-DIV box 2d 5,000 with K-1 box 9b (3,000) should give line 4 = 2,000, and the shipped graph gave 5,000, taxing 3,000 at 28% that the filer's own K-1 had already offset.
THE OTHER TWO LEGS OF LINE 4 KEEP THEIR FLOORS, and the asymmetry is the point: Form 1099-DIV box 2d and Form 2439 box 1d are REPORTED GAINS whose boxes print no loss, so /dividendReports/*/writableCollectiblesGain and /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm2439 are correctly Min $0. One worksheet line, three sources, and the sign must be read off the source that issues each amount rather than off the line that collects them. THE §1250 SIBLING IS NOT AFFECTED: Schedule K-1 box 9c is captioned "Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain" with no loss (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 16, and box 8c on the S-corporation K-1), so /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1 keeps its floor.
DEMOTED TO FALLBACK. This attestation is no longer the only way the K-1 leg of worksheet line 4 can be answered. scheduleE records every Schedule K-1 box by box, and box 9b of a partnership or S corporation K-1 and box 4b of an estate or trust K-1 are exactly this line's amounts. When any recorded K-1 answers one of those boxes (/collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered) the alias /collectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 sums the rows and does NOT read this fact; this fact is read only when no row answered the box. The precedence is deliberate and it is the anti double count: the rows and this total are the SAME money, so they may never be added. A filer who both records the K-1s and types the total gets the rows.
This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /collectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 downstream.

Fact.Name: Collectibles gain reported on a Schedule K-1
Fact.Description:
The Schedule K-1 leg of 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 4. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1, so every return without a K-1 collectibles amount is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this leg was a hardcoded $0 term of the lines 1-4 subtotal.
MAY BE NEGATIVE — this alias passes the answered sign through unchanged: the writable carries no Min $0. Schedule K-1 box 9b is captioned "Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss)" and its instructions say "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 16); the sign is set by the K-1 that issues the amount, not by the Schedule D line that collects it. It carries no floor of its own because the worksheet's floor is line 7's, applied once at /twentyEightPercentRateGain; flooring here would silently discard the loss the intake exists to capture, exactly as it would at lines 1 and 3.
WITH THIS FACT, WORKSHEET LINE 4 IS COMPLETE — all three of its legs are real: the Form 1099-DIV box 2d total (dividendReports /collectiblesGainFromDividends), the Form 2439 box 1d attestation (/collectiblesGainFromForm2439) and this one.
DIRECTION, BOTH WAYS. An answered GAIN raises the 28%-rate gain: through the lines 1-4 subtotal it raises Schedule D line 18, and through the line-14 read at /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17 it shrinks the line-17 offset and so raises-or-holds Schedule D line 19. This is now the THIRD signed leg of this worksheet, alongside lines 1 and 3; only line 2 and line 4's two reported-gain legs are floored.
DERIVED FROM THE RECORDED K-1 ROWS. The first arm of the Switch is the sum of scheduleE's own K-1 boxes — box 9b on /formK1s (partnership and S corporation) and box 4b on /form1041K1s (estate and trust) — taken whenever /collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered says at least one recorded K-1 answered that box. /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 is the FALLBACK behind that predicate, not a second addend: the rows and the attested total are the same money. The predicate is built from IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaves and never on the complete-safe per item bridges, because an IsComplete on those is true on every item and would retire the attestation on any return that merely opened a K-1.

Fact.Name: 28% Rate Gain Worksheet lines 1 through 4 (subtotal)
Fact.Description:
The sum of lines 1 through 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 11. Named as its own fact because the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 14 (:997-998) asks for exactly this subtotal — "If you had any section 1202 gain or collectibles gain or (loss), enter the total of lines 1 through 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet. Otherwise, enter -0-" — and NOT for the line-7 total that becomes Schedule D line 18. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /twentyEightPercentRateGain.
THE FOUR LINES, and which of them the graph can actually supply: line 1 (:905) collectibles gain or (loss) from Form 8949, Part II — REAL: /collectiblesGainFromForm8949, an attestation, because the graph collapses Form 8949 into one /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss (scope ledger oos-scheduled-form8949-per-transaction) and a collectibles SUBSET of that net cannot be derived. May be a LOSS, which is why it can never share an intake with line 4, and why it is the only leg here whose answer can make this subtotal NEGATIVE. line 2 (:906-913) the section 1202 exclusion — COMPLETE, as two independent addends: the 1099-DIV-attributable component (dividendReports /section1202ExclusionFromDividends) and the PRIMARY population, a direct QSBS sale on Form 8949, Part II code "Q" with no 1099-DIV (/section1202ExclusionFromForm8949, attested). Both are positive numbers with the 50%/60%/75%/100% tier fractions already applied by the filer. This line was PARTIAL and under-stated lines 18 and 19 for the direct seller; it no longer does. line 3 (:914-915) collectibles gain or (loss) from Form 4684 line 4 (only if Form 4684 line 15 is more than zero), Form 6252, Form 6781 Part II and Form 8824 — REAL: /collectiblesGainFromOtherForms, an attested total over four forms none of which the graph models. The SECOND leg here that may be a LOSS.
