The Form 4684 limb of it is unreachable for any casualty-loss claimant (form4684 /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses them), which is stated on the writable rather than encoded as a dependency. line 4 (:916-919) collectibles gain reported on Form 1099-DIV box 2d, Form 2439 box 1d and Schedule K-1 — COMPLETE, all three legs real: dividendReports /collectiblesGainFromDividends, /collectiblesGainFromForm2439 and /collectiblesGainFromScheduleK1, the last two attested totals across however many notices the filer holds. TWO of the three are non-negative and one is not, which is why they cannot share an intake with each other OR with line 1: box 2d and Form 2439 box 1d print no loss and are floored at $0, while Schedule K-1 box 9b is captioned "Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss)" and its instructions say "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 16), so that leg is signed. This line's own wording, "collectibles GAIN reported to you", is the COLLECTING wording and does not govern the sign of the amounts it collects — reading it that way is what put a wrong Min $0 on the K-1 intake.
THERE ARE NO $0 LEGS LEFT. Every one of lines 1 through 4 resolves from a fact. All four contracts are retired. What survives is the WHY: this subtotal moves real tax, so an omitted leg was never a bookkeeping gap. The chain is /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet reads Schedule D line 18, /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax consumes the gate, and taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome switches Form 1040 line 16 onto that worksheet when the gate fires — all shipping. What remains UNDER-STATED here is not a leg of these four lines but a limb inside two of them: line 3's Form 4684 amount is unreachable for a casualty-loss claimant (that return is refused outright, so no wrong number is filed), and line 5's Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D carryover is not modelled at all, which OVER-states this worksheet's line 7 for a filer who has one.
LINES 1 AND 2 ARE NO LONGER $0 LEGS, and their directions are opposite. Line 1 is an answered attestation that MAY BE NEGATIVE, so where a filer reports a collectibles loss it LOWERS this subtotal — lowering Schedule D line 18, and (through the line-14 read at /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17) lowering Schedule D line 19 as well. Line 2's direct-sale leg is floored at Min $0 and can only RAISE the subtotal. The two compose linearly, neither gating the other.
LINE 4 IS COMPLETE, and it is a THIRD sign rule on the same worksheet: Min $0 like line 2, but for its own reason — line 4 asks only for "collectibles GAIN reported to you", where line 2 says "Enter as a positive number" and line 1 says "gain or (loss)". Its Form 2439 and Schedule K-1 legs can only RAISE this subtotal. 100.
LINE 4 ALSO CARRIES A QUALIFIED ELECTING FUND LEG: form8621 /form8621CollectiblesGain, the collectibles (28%-rate) portion of Form 8621 line 7c that each fund reports under the section 1(h) categories (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8621.pdf, page 12), floored at $0 and capped at that fund's line 7c. The worksheet names no Form 8621 line, so the choice of line 4 is an interpretation: it is the line for collectibles gain reported to the filer by a pass-through vehicle. The amount is already inside Schedule D line 15 through the Form 8621 long-term total; this leg only moves it into the 28% group.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 18 — 28% rate gain (28% Rate Gain Worksheet line 7)
Fact.Description:
Schedule D line 18, the 28%-rate gain. The 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 line 7, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 11, verbatim: "Combine lines 1 through 6. If zero or less, enter -0-. If more than zero, also enter this amount on Schedule D, line 18." Built as the lines 1-4 subtotal, plus line 5 and line 6, floored at $0, with ONE Round at this fact.
LINE 5 (:920-922) is the long-term capital loss carryover from Schedule D line 14, printed on the worksheet as "5. ( )" — a NEGATIVE term. /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear stores it as a POSITIVE amount (its own Description says so), so this fact SUBTRACTS it, mirroring the line-14 usage already in /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover. Complete-safe: an unanswered carryover subtracts $0. The second leg ships as /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverFromForm1041K1, a code-keyed sum over the box 11 slots of scheduleE's /form1041K1s collection, stored POSITIVE like its neighbour and subtracted beside it. Both legs of line 5 are real, and the same node also serves Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 16, which names the identical pair of sources.
LINE 6 (:923) is "If Schedule D, line 7, is a (loss), enter that (loss) here. Otherwise, enter -0-", i.e. the lesser of Schedule D line 7 and $0. /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover is line 7; it is Incomplete when the filer has entered no short-term amount at all, so it is read through an IsComplete guard that contributes $0 in that case — never a bare Placeholder, which would make this fact Incomplete by contagion.
THE FLOOR is the source's own "If zero or less, enter -0-", so this fact is never negative even though lines 1, 5 and 6 all may be. The floor and the Round commute here (Round is whole-dollar HALF_UP and 0 rounds to 0), so the Round sits outermost.
CONSUMED, AND IT NOW MOVES TAX. /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet (the line-18-or-19 entry test) reads this fact, /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax reads the gate's worksheet, and taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome switches Form 1040 line 16 onto that worksheet when the gate fires — all three shipping. This paragraph used to end "so this fact moves no return's tax", which was true only while the last link was a contract.
IT NO LONGER CARRIES ANY $0 LEG: lines 1 through 4 are all real and the lines 1-4 subtotal holds no literal zero. What CAN still under-state this line is line 5's second leg, the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D long-term loss carryover, which has no fact anywhere in the graph — and it under-states the SUBTRAHEND, so its absence OVER-states line 18 rather than under-stating it. That is the opposite direction from the legs that used to be listed here, which is exactly why it must not inherit their sentence.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain from the sale of a partnership interest (writable)
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 10, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the amount of any gain from the sale or exchange of an interest in a partnership attributable to unrecaptured section 1250 gain. See instructions".
A FILER ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION, and nothing in this graph could derive it. The prose instruction (:1013-1027) defines the amount as the filer's share of the unrecaptured section 1250 gain that WOULD result if the partnership had transferred all of its section 1250 property in a fully taxable transaction immediately before the interest was sold — a look-through the PARTNERSHIP computes and reports on the statement required by Regulations section 1.1(h)-1(e). The graph holds no partnership-level section 1250 basis or depreciation history, so the number arrives from outside or not at all.
NOT BOUNDED BY THE COLLAPSED NET THE GAIN ITSELF LANDS IN. The gain on the interest sits inside /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss (scope ledger oos-scheduled-form8949-per-transaction), and the contract asked this fill to say whether it caps the attestation against that total. It does not, on the ground the line-1 sibling established: that net is a SUM over Form 8949 Part II items of BOTH signs, so a slice of it is not bounded by it in either direction — a filer with a 40,000 partnership-interest gain and a 50,000 loss on other Part II property has a net of -10,000 and a perfectly correct line 10. A Max against the net would refuse that return.
MIN $0, WHICH IS WHERE IT PARTS COMPANY WITH THAT SIBLING: the source here says "any GAIN from the sale or exchange of an interest in a partnership", with no "(loss)" branch, while 28% worksheet line 1 says "gain or (loss)". Same collapsed net, same no-Max reasoning, opposite floor rule — read off each line's own text rather than inherited. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipInterestSale downstream.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain from the sale of a partnership interest
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 10. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipInterestSale, so every return without a partnership-interest sale is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this line was a hardcoded $0 leg of line 13.
NON-NEGATIVE, matching the writable's Min $0. Resolution does not enforce that XML limit, so this alias explicitly floors an answered negative value at $0 before the amount enters worksheet line 13. The worksheet's own floor is line 18's, applied once at /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
DIRECTION, AND IT IS THE SIMPLE ONE: line 10 is a DIRECT addend of line 13 ("Add lines 9 through 12") with no intervening cap, so an answered amount raises line 13 and passes through to Schedule D line 19 undiminished — the line-17 offset it is spent against does not move, because line 10 touches neither worksheet's lines 1-4. Contrast the 28% worksheet attestations, which reach line 19 only by shrinking line 17.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain reported on Form 2439, box 1b (writable)
Fact.Description:
The Form 2439 leg of Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 11, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the total of any amounts reported to you as 'unrecaptured section 1250 gain' on a Schedule K-1, Form 1099-DIV, or Form 2439 from an estate, a trust, a real estate investment trust, or a mutual fund (or other regulated investment company) or in connection with a Form 1099-R". Box 1b of Form 2439 is the unrecaptured section 1250 part of the undistributed long-term capital gain a REIT or regulated investment company reports to a shareholder.
THE BOX NUMBER IS 1b, AND IT IS ROUTED BY NAME, so no reader has to infer it. The Schedule D instructions route all three Form 2439 sub-boxes in three consecutive paragraphs (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 6): "If there is an amount in box 1b of Form 2439, include that amount on line 11 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet if you complete line 19 of Schedule D" (:508-512) — THIS fact; "If there is an amount in box 1c of Form 2439, see Exclusion of Gain on Qualified Small Business (QSB) Stock, later" (:514-516); and "If there is an amount in box 1d of Form 2439, include that amount on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet if you complete line 18 of Schedule D" (:518-521) — the collectibles twin /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm2439.
BOX 1c IS A DIFFERENT THING ENTIRELY and this fact must never be labelled with it: it is the section 1202 QUALIFIED SMALL BUSINESS STOCK gain ("If you received a Form 2439 with a gain in box 1c, part or all of that gain (which is also included in box 1a) may be eligible for the section 1202 exclusion", :697-702). This fact was previously mislabelled as box 1c; the wiring was right throughout, only the label was wrong. The divergence the label could have caused is not hypothetical — a filer with box 1b = 5,000 and box 1c = 20,000 who followed the label would enter 20,000, over-stating worksheet line 13 by 15,000 into the 25% rate group while the real 5,000 never arrived.
A SCALAR TOTAL, NOT A FORM 2439 MODEL, exactly as its box 1d twin /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm2439 — same renegotiation, same reason, stated in full there. The worksheet line asks for a TOTAL of amounts reported to the filer, so an attested total answers it and introduces no collection.
MIN $0: the line asks for amounts "reported to you as 'unrecaptured section 1250 GAIN'", with no loss branch anywhere in it — the same sign rule as the Form 1099-DIV box-2b twin /dividendReports/*/writableUnrecapturedSection1250Gain. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm2439 downstream.
EVERY OTHER LEG OF THIS WORKSHEET LINE IS NOW REAL, and none of them is this fact's business. The Form 1099-R leg was the last $0 one — it had no node because /form1099Rs existed as a collection but carried no unrecaptured section 1250 amount, a missing collection FIELD rather than a missing computation — and the field now exists (form1099Rs /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm1099Rs). The Schedule K-1 (estate or trust) leg was also $0 when this fact landed and no longer is: /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1 shipped later the same day, on the same scalar-total argument this fact's own renegotiation established.
"A SCALAR TOTAL, NOT A FORM 2439 MODEL" is superseded: form2439:/form2439Forms (block 15) records every Copy B box per notice and since this unit the worksheet line reads that list. THIS SCALAR IS THE LEGACY PATH. /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm2439 reads it only while /form2439Forms is unanswered or empty; once a notice is listed the list governs (form2439:/form2439IncludedUnrecapturedSection1250Gain, VOID and wrong-year notices excluded, a blank box 1b counting $0), and this writable, if still answered, must equal that total or /knockoutForm2439NoticeTotalsDisagreeWithScheduleDEntries refuses the return. The application should collect Form 2439 through the notice list.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain reported on Form 2439, box 1b
Fact.Description:
The Form 2439 leg of Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 11. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm2439, so every return without a Form 2439 is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this leg was a hardcoded $0 term of line 11.
NON-NEGATIVE, matching the writable's Min $0. Resolution does not enforce that XML limit, so the scalar fallback explicitly floors an answered negative value at $0 before the amount reaches worksheet line 11. The worksheet's own floor is line 18's, applied once at /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
DIRECTION: this leg can only RAISE line 13 and therefore raise-or-hold Schedule D line 19. It reaches line 19 through a DIFFERENT edge from its box 1d twin: box 1b adds to line 13, the gross 25%-rate gain, while box 1d adds to the 28% worksheet's lines 1-4 subtotal and so shrinks the line-17 offset.
TWO SOURCES, ONE RULE. When the return lists at least one Form 2439 notice (form2439:/hasForm2439Notices) this leg is form2439:/form2439IncludedUnrecapturedSection1250Gain, the box 1b total over the notices that are not VOID and whose RIC or REIT tax year ends in 2025; the scalar above is then not added (it is checked, see the knockout). With no notice list the scalar carries the leg as before, complete-safe $0, so every committed scenario is value-identical. On the list path a live notice with no resolvable year leaves this leg Incomplete (ruling 6).

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain reported on a Schedule K-1 from an estate or trust (writable)
Fact.Description:
The Schedule K-1 (estate or trust) leg of Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 11, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the total of any amounts reported to you as 'unrecaptured section 1250 gain' on a Schedule K-1, Form 1099-DIV, or Form 2439 from an estate, a trust, a real estate investment trust, or a mutual fund (or other regulated investment company) or in connection with a Form 1099-R".
A SCALAR TOTAL, NOT A SCHEDULE K-1 MODEL, and this fact introduces no K-1 collection of any kind. The printed line asks for a TOTAL of amounts reported to the filer, one number across however many K-1s they hold, so an attested total answers it exactly — the same argument the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet's own K-1 leg /writableCollectiblesGainFromScheduleK1 landed on earlier the same day, and the argument that dissolved the deferral this leg used to carry. Nothing in the Schedule E Part II follow-on surface (per-entity basis, at-risk, passive-activity) is touched or brought forward.
MIN $0: the line asks for amounts "reported to you as 'unrecaptured section 1250 GAIN'", with no loss branch anywhere in it — the same sign rule as its three shipping neighbours on this worksheet.
DEMOTED TO FALLBACK. scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox4cUnrecapturedSection1250Gain is this same amount, box by box, and the estate or trust K-1's own routing table sends it to worksheet line 11. When any recorded estate or trust K-1 answers box 4c (/unrecapturedSection1250GainFromEstateOrTrustK1RowsAnswered) the alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1 sums the rows and does NOT read this fact. The rows and this total are the SAME money and may never be added.
This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1 downstream.
NOT WORKSHEET LINE 5, which is also a Schedule K-1 leg and is NOT built. Line 5 (:982-983) is the PARTNERSHIP/S-CORPORATION leg, it sits inside the lines 1-9 block, and line 7 caps that block at "the gain from Form 4797, line 7". This fact is line 11's ESTATE-OR-TRUST leg, which sits after the block and is capped by nothing. Routing a partnership K-1 amount here would carry it past a cap the source applies to it.
THE LAST REMAINING $0 LEG OF LINE 11 WAS THE FORM 1099-R ONE, and it deliberately got no contract: /form1099Rs existed as a collection but carried no unrecaptured section 1250 amount at all, so what was missing there was a COLLECTION FIELD rather than a computation. The field is form1099Rs /form1099Rs/*/writableUnrecapturedSection1250Gain. Line 11 has no $0 leg left.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain reported on a Schedule K-1 from an estate or trust
Fact.Description:
The Schedule K-1 (estate or trust) leg of Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 11. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1, so every return without such a K-1 is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this leg was a hardcoded $0 term of line 11.
NON-NEGATIVE, matching the writable's Min $0. Resolution does not enforce that XML limit, so the scalar fallback explicitly floors an answered negative value at $0 before it reaches worksheet line 11. The recorded K-1 row arm is already source-bounded by its own box value; the worksheet's own output floor remains line 18's, applied once at /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
DIRECTION: this leg can only RAISE line 13 and therefore raise-or-hold Schedule D line 19. It is a DIRECT addend of "Add lines 9 through 12" with no intervening cap, so the whole attested amount passes through to line 19 unless the line-18 floor binds — which the line-17 offset it is spent against does not move, because line 17 is fed by the 28% worksheet's lines 1-4 and by Schedule D lines 7 and 14, none of which this leg touches. For example, line 13 goes 1,000 to 1,900, line 17 stays 300, and line 19 goes 700 to 1,600.
DERIVED FROM THE RECORDED K-1 ROWS. The first arm of the Switch sums /form1041K1s/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD, box 4c of every recorded Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), whenever /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromEstateOrTrustK1RowsAnswered says at least one such K-1 answered it; /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1 is the FALLBACK, not a second addend. WORKSHEET LINE 11, the estate or trust leg — the partnership and S corporation box 9c is worksheet line 5 and lives at /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1. The two legs carry different limits and must not be crossed.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain from other section 1250 dispositions (writable)
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 12, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the total of any unrecaptured section 1250 gain from sales (including installment sales) or other dispositions of section 1250 property held more than 1 year for which you didn't make an entry in Part I of Form 4797 for the year of sale. See instructions". The named example in the "Line 12" prose (:1029-1036) is a vacation home previously used as rental property and converted to personal use before the sale — that is the population.
IT IS THE COMPLEMENT OF THE REFUSED SURFACE, NOT AN INCONSISTENT SECOND PATH, and that is this fill's renegotiation. The contract argued the leg was knockout-coupled: "a fill that builds line 12 while a section 1250 disposition still refuses would produce a graph that computes one section 1250 path and refuses another." The two paths are disjoint by the LINE'S OWN DEFINITION. Line 12's population is section 1250 property "for which you didn't make an entry in Part I of Form 4797", and form4797's refusal was triggered by ENTERING a section 1250 disposition in /section1245Dispositions. A filer who made the Part I entry was still refused; a filer who makes none is outside worksheet lines 1-3 by the source's own words and has no Form 4797 collection item to refuse. Computing one and refusing the other was the SOURCE'S split, not an incoherence introduced here. THE REFUSAL IS RETIRED and the disjointness argument is unaffected — it never rested on the refusal, only on the line's own "didn't make an entry in Part I" clause, which is now the same clause form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent reads from the other side. The two populations remain complementary, and nothing here double-counts. No dependency on the knockout is declared: this fact reads nothing from form4797, and gating an attestation on a submission-blocking flag would make it Incomplete-by-contagion.
WHAT THIS FILL DOES NOT DO, so the contract's real content is not lost: it does not model the three-step allocation the "Line 12" prose describes (the smaller of the depreciation allowed or allowable, or the total gain for the sale, reduced by the section 1250 ordinary income recapture from Form 4797 line 26g, and for installment sales further reduced by gain reported in prior years). The filer performs it. Prior-year gain is multi-year state this graph does not hold, so it could not be derived here in any case; the attestation makes that explicit rather than approximating it.
KEEP IT DISJOINT FROM LINE 4, WHICH SHIPS as /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm6252. This paragraph is the pointer that line's own fill owed this one: when this fact was built, worksheet line 4 was a $0 leg and the overlap could not arise, and the note that recorded that ("Both lines cover installment sales") lived only on the blocked contract. Both lines cover installment sales — this one by "sales (INCLUDING installment sales)", line 4 by its own words — and the source separates them on the PART I ENTRY and nothing else: property for which a Form 4797 Part I entry WAS made for the year of sale belongs on line 4, property for which none was made belongs here. Two properties, one on each line, is a correct return.
MIN $0: the line asks for "unrecaptured section 1250 GAIN", with no loss branch. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromOtherDispositions downstream.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain from other section 1250 dispositions
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 12. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromOtherDispositions, so every return without such a disposition is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph, where this line was a hardcoded $0 leg of line 13.
NON-NEGATIVE, inherited from the Min $0 on the writable rather than re-imposed here. The worksheet's own floor is line 18's, applied once at /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
DIRECTION: a direct addend of line 13 with no intervening cap, so it can only RAISE Schedule D line 19, passing through undiminished because it touches neither worksheet's lines 1-4 and so leaves the line-17 offset alone. It shares that topology with its line-10 neighbour and NOT with the 28%-worksheet attestations.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain from Form(s) 6252 installment sales (writable)
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 4, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the total unrecaptured section 1250 gain included on line 26 or line 37 of Form(s) 6252 from installment sales of trade or business property held more than 1 year. See instructions".
AN ATTESTATION, AND THE THREE-STEP ALLOCATION IS THE FILER'S. The "Line 4" prose (:964-967) sends the filer to the three steps at :942-967: step 1 is the smaller of the depreciation allowed or allowable or the total gain (Form 4797 lines 22 and 24 for the year of sale), step 2 reduces that by the section 1250 ordinary income recapture (Form 4797 line 26g), and step 3 makes each installment payment unrecaptured section 1250 gain until the step-2 total is used up, so the amount entered here is the smaller of (a) Form 6252 line 26 or 37 and (b) "the total unrecaptured section 1250 gain for the sale reduced by all gain reported in prior years (excluding section 1250 ordinary income recapture)". Limb (b) is MULTI-YEAR STATE this engine does not hold, and no Form 6252 is modelled anywhere in the graph, so the whole allocation is intaken as a single carry-IN the way /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear is. Nothing here derives it or checks it.
KEEP IT DISJOINT FROM LINE 12, which ships as /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromOtherDispositions. Both lines cover installment sales — this one by its own words, line 12 by "sales (INCLUDING installment sales) ... for which you didn't make an entry in Part I of Form 4797 for the year of sale" (:993-995). The source separates them on the PART I ENTRY and on nothing else: an installment sale that DID get a Part I entry belongs here, one that did not belongs on line 12. THE SAME DOLLARS MUST NOT BE ENTERED ON BOTH. Two properties, one on each line, is a correct return; one property on both lines is a double count no fact in this graph can detect, because both are attestations.
WHAT THE SOURCE'S OWN CAP DOES ABOUT IT, which is why prose and a test are the guard here and a mutual-exclusion knockout would be wrong. A misplacement in this direction — a line-12 amount entered here — lands inside the lines 1-9 block, where line 7 caps the total at the Form 4797 line 7 gain. Property with no Form 4797 Part I entry contributes nothing to that gain, so absent unrelated section 1231 gains the cap absorbs the misplacement entirely. A misplacement in the other direction is not cappable, which is why line 12's own writable now carries the pointer back to this line.
MIN $0: the line asks for unrecaptured section 1250 GAIN, with no "(loss)" branch anywhere in it — the same rule its line-5, line-10, line-11 and line-12 neighbours read off their own printed text. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm6252 downstream.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain from Form(s) 6252 installment sales
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 4. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm6252, so every return without a Form 6252 installment sale is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph.
NON-NEGATIVE, matching the writable's Min $0. Resolution does not enforce that XML limit, so this alias explicitly floors an answered negative value at $0 before it enters the worksheet line-6 subtotal. The worksheet's own floors remain line 9's and line 18's, applied where the source prints them.
DIRECTION: NOT a direct addend of line 13. It reaches line 13 through line 6, the line-7 minimum against the Form 4797 line 7 gain, and the line-8 reduction, so it can RAISE Schedule D line 19 by AT MOST the room the Form 4797 line 7 gain leaves after Form 4797 line 8 — and by nothing at all on a return with no Form 4797 line 7 gain. That is the topology it shares with its line-5 neighbour and with NEITHER the line-10/12 attestations nor the 28%-worksheet ones.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on a partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1 (writable)
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 5, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the total of any amounts reported to you on a Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation as 'unrecaptured section 1250 gain'".
NOT /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1, WHICH ALSO SHIPS IN THIS FILE, and the two are the reason this path carries "PartnershipOrSCorp" in its NAME rather than only in its prose. That one is worksheet line 11's Schedule K-1 leg — an ESTATE or TRUST K-1, grouped there with Form 1099-DIV and Form 2439 — and it is a direct addend of line 13. This one is line 5, a PARTNERSHIP or S CORPORATION K-1, and it sits inside the lines 1-9 block under the line-7 minimum. A filer holding a partnership K-1 is the person most likely to enter it in the wrong place, and the two lines do not pay the same.
UNBLOCKED BY THE CAP, NOT BY A K-1 COUPLING: this leg was held up by the line-7 minimum, not by any Schedule K-1 modelling gap — a printed "enter the total of any amounts reported to you" line is answered by a scalar attestation without introducing a Schedule K-1 collection, the same argument as on /collectiblesGainFromScheduleK1. The block this leg sits in now exists.
MIN $0: the line asks for amounts reported as "unrecaptured section 1250 gain", with no "(loss)" branch.
DEMOTED TO FALLBACK. scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableK1065Box9cUnrecapturedSection1250Gain is this same amount, box by box, and the partner's instructions send it to worksheet line 5 by name. When any recorded partnership or S corporation K-1 answers box 9c (/unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1RowsAnswered) the alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1 sums the rows and does NOT read this fact. The rows and this total are the SAME money and may never be added.
This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1 downstream.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on a partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1
Fact.Description:
Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 5. Complete-safe: $0 when the taxpayer did not answer /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1, so every return without such a K-1 is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph.
NON-NEGATIVE, matching the writable's Min $0. Resolution does not enforce that XML limit, so the scalar fallback explicitly floors an answered negative value at $0 before it enters the worksheet line-6 subtotal. The recorded K-1 row arm is source-bounded by its own box value and remains authoritative when present.
DIRECTION: like its line-4 neighbour and unlike every other leg of line 13, it is capped — it reaches line 13 through line 6, the line-7 minimum against the Form 4797 line 7 gain, and the line-8 reduction.
DERIVED FROM THE RECORDED K-1 ROWS. The first arm of the Switch sums /formK1s/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD, box 9c of every recorded Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S), whenever /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1RowsAnswered says at least one such K-1 answered it; /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipOrSCorpK1 is the FALLBACK, not a second addend. WORKSHEET LINE 5, the partnership and S corporation leg — the estate or trust box 4c is worksheet line 11 and lives at /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1. The two legs carry different limits and must not be crossed.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 3, all properties (the Form 4797 Part III section 1250 legs)
Fact.Description:
Line 3 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Subtract line 2 from line 1" — totalled across properties, because lines 1 through 3 are PER PROPERTY. The instruction is printed: "If you had more than one property described on line 1, complete lines 1 through 3 for each property on a separate worksheet. Enter the total of the line 3 amounts for all properties on line 3 and go to line 4" (:958-963). So the per-property arithmetic lives at form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent — where lines 1 (the smaller of Form 4797 line 22 or line 24), 2 (that property's line 26g) and the line-3 subtraction and floor all are — and this fact is only the total the printed rule asks for. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /unrecapturedSection1250Gain — but ITS ADDENDS ARE NOT, and that seam is named on the form4797 fact rather than hidden here. form4797 rounds per item throughout Part III, so each property's line 3 arrives already rounded and this sum of them is a genuine exception to the block's "one Round at the end" discipline. The divergence is bounded by 50 cents per property and needs a cents-carrying line 22 that binds the line-1 minimum to appear at all.
THIS TERM IS REAL: form4797 admits the section 1250 class, so the return exists. Nothing about lines 4 through 9 is affected.
GATED BY form4797:/claimsSection1245Disposition, the /section1245OrdinaryRecapture idiom verbatim, so a return that never populates the disposition collection never reads it and resolves Complete-$0 exactly as the hardcoded zero did. AND BY form4797:/hasUnsupportedSection1245Disposition FIRST, for the reason /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine7 gives at length one fact down: when any disposition is refused the return does not complete at all, and this block must not turn one refusal into six by carrying an Incomplete into line 6, line 13, Schedule D line 19 and every consumer of it. That arm cannot mask a filable return — a filable return has no unsupported disposition — and it is tested FIRST because the engine's Switch is lazy and positional. (The per-property fact is itself Complete on every return, so this is defence in depth rather than the only guard.) BESIDE the paragraphs above rather than over them. "the per-property arithmetic lives at form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent" IS NOW HALF FALSE: a SALE item's lines 1-3 live there, and a CASUALTY column's lines 1-3 live at form4684:/casualtyEvents/*/sectionBUnrecapturedSection1250GainComponent, totalled by form4684:/casualtyUnrecapturedSection1250GainTotal. A casualty event can attest section 1250 property and carry a Form 4797 Part III line 26g recapture, whose non-recapture remainder returns on Form 4684 line 33, leaves on line 39 and enters Form 4797 PART I line 3 - so the property satisfies both of line 1's clauses, "a section 1250 property in Part III of Form 4797" and "for which you made an entry in Part I of Form 4797", and its line 3 belongs in this printed total. THE PRINTED LINE THIS FACT CARRIES DID NOT MOVE and neither did the sale leg's condition or operand: the Switch's refusal arm is byte-identical and the /claimsSection1245Disposition arm is now nested inside an Add whose second operand is the casualty total. THE REFUSAL ARM STILL WINS: a return whose Form 4797 refuses reports $0 here whether or not it also has a casualty column, because an already-refused return's resolved output must not change.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 6 (add lines 3 through 5)
Fact.Description:
Line 6 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Add lines 3 through 5". The UNCAPPED subtotal of the block — what the filer's own records say, before the line-7 minimum measures it against the Form 4797 line 7 gain. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
THE LINE-3 TERM IS REAL and is /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3 above: form4797 admits attested section 1250 real property, computes its Part III lines 26a-26g block, and carries the per-property worksheet lines 1-3 as form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent. Lines 4 and 5 are real and are untouched by that landing.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 7 (smaller of line 6 or the Form 4797 line 7 gain)
Fact.Description:
Line 7 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 6 or the gain from Form 4797, line 7". THE CAP THE WHOLE BLOCK EXISTS FOR. UNROUNDED.
"THE GAIN FROM FORM 4797, LINE 7" IS form4797 /netSection1231GainOrLoss, which is Form 4797 Part I line 7 ("Combine lines 2 through 6", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1) and gained its Export in this unit. IT IS NOT /section1231LtcgPortion, which is Form 4797 line NINE (:45-47 of the same file, "Subtract line 8 from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0-"). Substituting line 9 for the pair of reads this fact and line 8 make is the defect the retired BLOCKED contract named, and it is invisible on most cases: line 9 is max(0, L7 - L8) while this block computes max(0, min(line 6, L7) - L8), which agree whenever line 6 is at least L7.
TWO ARMS ENTER $0, and both are the source's, not a safety net bolted on. FIRST, THE BLOCK HEADER (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13): "If you aren't reporting a gain on Form 4797, line 7, skip lines 1 through 9 and go to line 10." A Form 4797 line 7 that is zero or a loss is not "a gain", so the block is skipped and everything in it, this line included, contributes nothing. That is also what makes an attestation on line 4 or line 5 harmless on a return with no Form 4797 Part I gain: the source discards it here rather than this module second-guessing the filer. SECOND, A REFUSED FORM 4797 (form4797 /hasUnsupportedSection1245Disposition): when any disposition is unsupported, /netSection1231GainOrLoss resolves Result.Incomplete and the return does not complete at all — /form4797OrdinaryIncome and /totalIncome refuse. Reading the value there would make this line, line 13, Schedule D line 19 and every consumer of it Incomplete TOO, replacing one refusal with six and changing the resolved output of an already-refused return.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 8 (the amount from Form 4797, line 8)
Fact.Description:
Line 8 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Enter the amount, if any, from Form 4797, line 8". A pass-through of form4797 /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss, which IS Form 4797 Part I line 8 ("Nonrecaptured net section 1231 losses from prior years", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1) and gained its Export in this unit. UNROUNDED.
THE RAW CARRY-IN, NOT THE RECHARACTERIZED MINIMUM. Form 4797 line 12 takes min(line 7 gain, line 8) and form4797 /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary models that; the printed line 8 does not, and neither does this. Non-negative by the Min $0 on the carry-IN writable it wraps, so it can only REDUCE line 9.
NO SKIP-RULE ARM HERE, deliberately, and the arithmetic is unaffected. When the block is skipped (or Form 4797 refuses) line 7 is $0, so line 9 is max(0, 0 - this) = $0 whatever this line holds — the skip is enforced once, at line 7, where the source's own header condition is read. Leaving this line as the verbatim pass-through keeps a snapshot reader able to see the Form 4797 line 8 amount the worksheet asks them to copy. It is also why this fact never becomes Incomplete: /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss is the IsComplete-wrapped carry-IN alias and is Complete on every return, disposition or no disposition.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 9 (subtract line 8 from line 7, floored at zero)
Fact.Description:
Line 9 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Subtract line 8 from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0-". The whole lines 1-9 block reduced to the one number line 13 adds. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
THE FLOOR IS THE SOURCE'S, printed on this line, and it is the reason neither line 4 nor line 5 needs a second floor of its own: a line-8 carry-IN larger than the capped line 7 cannot drive this block negative and so cannot reduce any OTHER leg of line 13.
THIS IS NOT form4797 /section1231LtcgPortion. That fact is Form 4797 line 9, max(0, L7 - L8); this is max(0, min(line 6, L7) - L8). They agree exactly when line 6 is at least L7 — which is most returns, and the reason the retired BLOCKED contract insisted the unblocking unit build this line rather than reuse the export. See /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine7's Description for the witness pair.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 13 (add lines 9 through 12)
Fact.Description:
Line 13 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Add lines 9 through 12". The gross unrecaptured section 1250 gain, before the line-17 offset. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
LINES 1 THROUGH 9 ARE REAL and enter as /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine9. Lines 1-3 (:975-979) are real too: they are the Form 4797 Part III section 1250 legs, that class is now IN scope, and they enter as /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3. Lines 4 (:980-981, Form 6252 installment sales) and 5 (:982-983, a partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1) are now filer attestations, line 6 (:984) is their subtotal, line 7 (:985) takes the smaller of it and the Form 4797 line 7 gain (form4797 /netSection1231GainOrLoss, exported in the same unit), line 8 (:986) is the Form 4797 line 8 carry-IN (form4797 /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss, likewise), and line 9 (:987) subtracts and floors at $0.
THIS IS THE ONE CAPPED LEG OF THIS LINE, which is the whole reason it took six facts where the other legs took two. Everything else here is a direct addend and passes through undiminished; the block is bounded by the Form 4797 line 7 gain and vanishes entirely on a return that reports no such gain (the skip rule at :974). An attested line 4 wired straight into this Add would have been WRONG, not merely under-stated — see /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine7.
LINE 10 (:988-989) is the partnership-interest-sale leg — REAL: /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromPartnershipInterestSale, a filer attestation of the partnership's own Regulations section 1.1(h)-1 look-through, which nothing in this graph could derive. LINE 11 (:990-992) has TWO real legs: dividendReports /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromDividends (the Form 1099-DIV box 2b total) and /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm2439 (the box 1b total, attested — an amount reported TO the filer on a notice the graph does not otherwise model) — and a THIRD: /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromScheduleK1, the estate-or-trust K-1 total, also attested. AND A FOURTH — form1099Rs /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm1099Rs, the per-form intake summed with an IsComplete guard. This Add carries no zero-dollar literal at all. LINE 12 (:993-995) is REAL: /unrecapturedSection1250GainFromOtherDispositions, an attestation whose population is the COMPLEMENT of the refused Part I surface — property "for which you didn't make an entry in Part I of Form 4797 for the year of sale". A filer who makes that entry is still refused; a filer who makes none has no form4797 collection item to refuse. Computing the one while refusing the other is the source's own split, not an incoherence.
THIS FACT HAS NO $0 TERM LEFT AT ALL. The Form 1099-R leg of line 11 was not a computation gap but a missing collection FIELD — the field now exists (form1099Rs /form1099Rs/*/writableUnrecapturedSection1250Gain) with its total wired, and worksheet line 3 inside the block is real too.
THE SCHEDULE K-1 LEG OF LINE 11 is filled, on the argument the 28% worksheet's own K-1 fill established earlier that day: the worksheet lines ask for a TOTAL of amounts reported to the filer, which an attestation answers without introducing a Schedule K-1 collection. Line 11's estate-or-trust K-1 leg is a direct addend of this line and was buildable on exactly that argument; worksheet line 5's K-1 leg (:982-983) is NOT, because it sits inside the lines 1-9 block described above, under the line-7 cap.
THE FORM 1099-R LEG GOT NO CONTRACT, and the reason was a category difference rather than an ordering one: /form1099Rs existed as a collection but carried no unrecaptured section 1250 amount, so what was missing was a COLLECTION FIELD, not a computation. The field is form1099Rs /form1099Rs/*/writableUnrecapturedSection1250Gain, per FORM rather than per return because the collection is modeled (its Form 2439 and estate/trust K-1 siblings are return-level totals precisely because those notices are not). NO BOX NUMBER IS CLAIMED for it: the worksheet line names the form and not a box, and nothing in the vendored corpus ties the amount to one — see the writable's own Description for the open reachability question that silence leaves behind.
DIRECTION: a $0 LEG would UNDER-state line 13 and therefore line 19, under-taxing a filer who had one — real tax, not a latent exposure. None remains: taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome now switches Form 1040 line 16 onto /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax whenever /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is true, and form6251 Part III reads the same gate, so on a gate-true return an omitted leg lowers both the regular tax's 25% group and the AMT's.
LINE 11 ALSO CARRIES A QUALIFIED ELECTING FUND LEG: form8621 /form8621UnrecapturedSection1250Gain, the unrecaptured section 1250 portion of Form 8621 line 7c that each fund reports under the section 1(h) categories (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8621.pdf, page 12), floored at $0 and capped at that fund's line 7c. The worksheet names no Form 8621 line, so the choice of line 11 is an interpretation: it is the line for amounts reported to the filer as unrecaptured section 1250 gain by an investment vehicle. The amount is already inside Schedule D line 15 through the Form 8621 long-term total; this leg only moves it into the 25% group.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 17 (the 28%-rate and loss offset)
Fact.Description:
Line 17 of the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Combine lines 14 through 16. If the result is a (loss), enter it as a positive amount. If the result is zero or a gain, enter -0-." The amount that is spent against line 13 at line 18. Non-negative by the source's own two branches. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /unrecapturedSection1250Gain.
THE ALGEBRA, because the fact is not written as a literal "combine": lines 15 and 16 are both printed "( )" and are therefore NEGATIVE terms, so the combine is line14 − line15magnitude − line16magnitude. "Enter it as a positive amount" NEGATES that when it is a loss, giving line15magnitude + line16magnitude − line14; "zero or a gain, enter -0-" is the floor at $0 on the negated value. This fact is exactly that: the two magnitudes summed, less line 14, floored at $0.
LINE 14 (:997-998) is "If you had any section 1202 gain or collectibles gain or (loss), enter the total of lines 1 through 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet. Otherwise, enter -0-" — /twentyEightPercentRateGainLines1Through4, the named subtotal the Schedule D line 18 fill landed for exactly this consumer, NOT /twentyEightPercentRateGain's line-7 total. The source's conditional needs no Switch, and the reason is an IDENTITY rather than an accident of today's graph: lines 1 through 4 of that worksheet are the section 1202 exclusion and the collectibles gain or (loss), so their total is zero precisely when the filer "had" none of those items. That stays true after the blocked legs of that subtotal fill; nobody needs to re-introduce the conditional.
LINE 15 (:999-1000) is "Enter the (loss), if any, from Schedule D, line 7. If Schedule D, line 7, is zero or a gain, enter -0-", i.e. the magnitude of the lesser of Schedule D line 7 and $0. /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover is line 7; it is Incomplete when the filer has entered no short-term amount at all, so it is read through an IsComplete guard that contributes $0 in that case — never a bare Placeholder, which would make this fact Incomplete by contagion.
LINE 16 (:1001-1002) is the long-term capital loss carryover from Schedule D line 14. /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear already stores it as a POSITIVE amount (its own Description says so), so it IS the magnitude and enters directly, read through the same IsComplete guard. The second leg ships as /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverFromForm1041K1 and enters this line as a positive magnitude beside the line 14 carryover. Both legs of line 16 are real.
BOTH OFFSETS ALSO APPEAR IN THE 28% RATE GAIN WORKSHEET, at its lines 5 and 6, and that is the source's design, not a duplication to be fixed: the same carryover and the same Schedule D line 7 loss reduce the 28%-rate gain and the unrecaptured section 1250 gain independently. The sd19-worked-example node test pins both worksheets on one scenario so that a future "de-duplication" fails a test instead of a return.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 19 — unrecaptured section 1250 gain (worksheet line 18)
Fact.Description:
Schedule D line 19, the unrecaptured section 1250 gain taxed at 25%. The Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet—Line 19 line 18, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13, verbatim: "Unrecaptured section 1250 gain. Subtract line 17 from line 13. If zero or less, enter -0-. If more than zero, enter the result here and on Schedule D, line 19." Built as /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine13 less /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17, floored at $0, with ONE Round at this fact.
THE FLOOR is the source's own "If zero or less, enter -0-", so this fact is never negative even though line 17 may exceed line 13. The floor and the Round commute here (Round is whole-dollar HALF_UP and 0 rounds to 0), so the Round sits outermost — the same treatment /twentyEightPercentRateGain gives its line 7.
THE FORM 2555 FOOTNOTE IS IMPLEMENTED, AND NOT ON THIS FACT. The worksheet's footnote (:1008-1009) attaches to line 16: "If you are filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income), see the footnote in the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040 before completing this line." That redirect leads to modification (4) ("Include your capital gain excess as a loss on line 16 of your Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), which is /feiSdtwUnrecapturedSection1250GainLine17 feeding /feiSdtwScheduleDLine19. THIS fact is the UNMODIFIED Schedule D line 19 — the one every non-Form-2555 return uses, and the one the shipping Schedule D Tax Worksheet reads at its lines 11 and 35. The two coexist by design: the footnote's modifications are "to be made only for purposes of filling out the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet above" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), so Schedule D's own printed line 19 is this fact and stays this fact.
CONSUMED, AND IT MOVES TAX TWICE OVER. /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet (the line-18-or-19 entry test) reads this fact; /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax computes the worksheet; taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome switches Form 1040 line 16 onto it when the gate fires; and form6251 Part III line 14 (/amtPart3UnrecapturedGain) reads THIS fact directly for the AMT's 25% rate group. All of them ship. The paragraph this replaces said the opposite — "moves no return's tax" — which held only while the last of those was a contract. The $0 legs line 13 still carries are therefore live under-statements on a gate-true return. All seven legs of this line are real: lines 10 and 12, line 11's Form 2439 box 1b leg, line 11's Schedule K-1 leg, the whole lines 4-9 chain behind its line-7 cap, the lines 1-3 Form 4797 Part III block (coupled to the section 1250 knockout), and line 11's Form 1099-R leg (a per-form collection field rather than a computation). NONE IS LEFT.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet applies (worksheet entry test)
Fact.Description:
The Schedule D Tax Worksheet's own entry test: true when the SDTW, not the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (QDCGT), is the worksheet that figures Form 1040 line 16. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Complete this worksheet only if line 18 or line 19 of Schedule D is more than zero and lines 15 and 16 of Schedule D are gains or if you file Form 4952 and you have an amount on line 4g, even if you don't need to file Schedule D. Otherwise, complete the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet in the instructions for Form 1040, line 16, (or in the instructions for Form 1040-NR, line 16) to figure your tax. Before completing this worksheet, complete Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR through line 15."
THE PREDICATE, term by term, all four comparisons STRICTLY "more than zero": (Schedule D line 18 > 0 OR Schedule D line 19 > 0) AND line 15 > 0 AND line 16 > 0 — /twentyEightPercentRateGain, /unrecapturedSection1250Gain, /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover and /netCapitalGainOrLoss, every one of them real and shipping in this module. The first term is a disjunction because the source's is; the other two are conjuncts of it.
WHY "> 0" AND NOT ">= 0", on both halves. Lines 18 and 19 are floored at zero by their own worksheets ("If zero or less, enter -0-"), so a worksheet that computed to zero renders identically to one that was never reached; reading "more than zero" as "at least zero" would put every return with a floored worksheet into the SDTW. On lines 15 and 16 the phrase is "are gains", and a zero is not a gain — that reading comes from the entry test's own wording at :1073-1074 and from nowhere else.
THE FIRST EXCEPTION (:1078-1080) DOES NOT SUPPLY THAT READING, and conflating the two is the trap this paragraph exists to close. Its first bullet is a CONJUNCTION — "Line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D is zero or less and you have no qualified dividends on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a" — so it withholds BOTH worksheets only from a filer who ALSO has no qualified dividends. A filer with a zero-or-less line 15 or 16 who DOES have qualified dividends still completes the QDCGT. Either way that return never reaches the SDTW, so the Exception is consistent with the strict reading above without being its source.
THE SECOND EXCEPTION (:1081) IS DELIBERATELY NOT A TERM OF THIS FACT, and this is a decision, not an omission. "Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15, is zero or less" routes the return away from the QDCGT AND this worksheet alike, to the Form 1040 line 16 instructions (:1082). This fact is a TWO-WAY SELECTOR between the two worksheets; that Exception is a THREE-WAY pre-empt sitting above both. Adding a taxable-income conjunct here would not implement it — it would send a zero-taxable-income return to the QDCGT, which the same Exception forbids just as firmly. The obligation therefore belongs to taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome (taxCalculations.xml), which is the fact that actually chooses among all three routes for Form 1040 line 16. It resolves the Exception by the documented-equivalence argument in its own Description rather than by a third arm. The sdtw-gate-zero-taxable-income node test pins this fact's side of that split so the decision cannot drift silently.
THE FORM 4952 LINE 4g DISJUNCT NOW SHIPS. A positive complete-safe form4952:/electedInvestmentIncome4gAmount selects this worksheet before the Schedule-D- gain arm, exactly as the printed independent "or" requires. It has a SECOND consumer, no longer restated by preferentialRateTax /knockoutForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetPreferentialRate, which refused every Form 2555 return whose line 4 needed the Schedule D Tax Worksheet; that knockout RETIRED when the route it was waiting for filled (scheduleD /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax), so this paragraph is the home for the rule. Concretely: preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 now selects the second Schedule D Tax Worksheet on THIS fact, so a Form 2555 filer with a positive Form 4952 line 4g amount is routed to the starred SDTW even without a Schedule D line 18/19 gain. The second worksheet therefore inherits the same election route. THE THIRD, QUIETER CONSEQUENCE is the measure of the capital gain excess itself: /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcess reads /sdtwLine10, which is net of the Form 4952 line 4g/4e offset, so it needs no separate rebody.
COMPLETE-SAFETY, and which guards are load-bearing. An unanswered return must resolve this fact Complete-and-FALSE, never Incomplete: this Boolean is destined to be a Switch condition, and an Incomplete condition would make Form 1040 line 16 Incomplete by contagion. TWO of the four inputs can be Incomplete and both are guarded: /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover reaches /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss through /netLongTermGainOrLoss, whose FALLBACK branch reads that writable BARE — so on a return with no Form 8949 detail it is Incomplete until the filer answers it, exactly as this paragraph said before the repoint, and the bareness is preserved for that reason rather than by accident. THE HOLE THIS PARAGRAPH DESCRIBES IS NARROWER NOW, and the narrowing is a real change to the analysis rather than a wording refresh: a return that answers /form8949Transactions takes the OTHER branch, which is complete-safe, so it resolves Complete with the writable unanswered — node-test scheduleD/form8949-multi-item-short-and-long-split asserts exactly that (/longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover Complete -4000.00, writable never answered). The guard below is therefore load-bearing only for the no-detail population, which is every return in the corpus today; and /netCapitalGainOrLoss adds /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover bare inside its claims-Schedule-D arm, so it is Incomplete when Schedule D is claimed and only the LONG-term side was answered. The two holes are independent — a non-claiming return has line 16 Complete at $0 while line 15 is still Incomplete. HONESTY ABOUT WHICH GUARD CARRIES WEIGHT (review finding): under the engine's false-dominant All (a Complete-false operand decides the result regardless of an Incomplete sibling), the line-16 guard is the load-bearing one — sdtw-gate-short-term-unanswered-complete-safe genuinely isolates it (line 18 nonzero, line 16 Incomplete, gate still Complete-false). The line-15 guard is defense-in-depth, not provably load-bearing today: in every reachable line-15-Incomplete state either the line-16 guard fires first (claims=true) or line 16 is Complete $0 and the All is already false (claims=false). It is KEPT deliberately — guarding each read is the module idiom, and false-dominance is engine behavior, not a contract this fact may lean on — but no test claims to isolate it, and sdtw-gate-unanswered-default-safe proves only the end-to-end Complete-false posture (its Any head is already false on $0 worksheets). Schedule D lines 18 and 19 need NO guard, and that is proved rather than assumed: every leg of both worksheets is either a literal $0, a dividendReports CollectionSum (Complete at $0 with no reports), or already read through its own IsComplete guard — which is why sd19-unanswered-default-safe asserts both Complete at $0 on a return where /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover is Incomplete.
A POPULATION THIS FACT UNDER-STATES, named rather than left to look handled: a filer with an amount in Form 1099-DIV box 2b, 2c or 2d is REQUIRED to file Schedule D — Exception 1 to the Form 1040 line 7 instructions withholds the "Schedule D not required" path from exactly those boxes (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 31). If such a filer never answers /hasCapitalGainsOrLosses or the long-term writable, line 15 is Incomplete, this gate resolves false, and the return is figured on the QDCGT — taxing a collectibles or unrecaptured section 1250 amount at 0/15/20% instead of 28%/25%. The guards make that return SAFE (Complete, and routed exactly as it is today); they do not make it CORRECT. The intake gap is the fix, not a looser gate.
WORLD-1 SAFETY, RESTATED NOW THAT THIS FACT IS LOAD-BEARING. Both worksheets are shipping and either may exceed zero, so this fact is genuinely TRUE on representable returns — the sdtw-gate-worked-example case is one. It used to be safe because NOTHING CONSUMED it; that is no longer why. /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax and taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome both ship, so a TRUE here routes Form 1040 line 16 to the Schedule D Tax Worksheet and (through form6251 Part III lines 13 and 15) selects the AMT's "whichever applies" arm. The whole gate-false population — the entire conformance corpus — is byte-identical, which is what made the switch additive; the gate-TRUE population is where the $0 legs still carried by lines 18 and 19 become live under-statements.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 1 (taxable income)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter your taxable income from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15. (However, if you are filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income), enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the instructions for Form 1040, line 16.)" taxCalculations /taxableIncome, read bare exactly as /qdcgLine1 reads it. THE FORM 2555 REDIRECT IS IMPLEMENTED, AND NOT HERE: this fact is the FIRST run's line 1, the unsubstituted taxable income that figures Form 1040 line 16 for every filer who is not completing the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet. The substitution lives on /feiSdtwLine1, the second run's line 1, which takes preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine3. THIS fact is also what the capital gain excess is measured against, because the footnote's subtrahend is Form 1040 line 15 itself — see /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcess. The root fact /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax states the routing of both halves.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 2 (qualified dividends)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter your qualified dividends from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a". income /qualifiedDividends, the same fact /qdcgLine2 reads — and read DIRECTLY, not through /qdcgLine2 itself. Aliasing the QDCGT's line 2 would couple this worksheet to the other worksheet's internal line numbering for no gain; the two worksheets share an INPUT, not a line.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 3 (Form 4952 line 4g)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the amount from Form 4952 (used to figure investment interest expense deduction), line 4g". Reads the same complete-safe dollar that Form 4952 adds to line 4h.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 4 (Form 4952 line 4e)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the amount from Form 4952, line 4e*", whose footnote (:1171-1172) reads "If applicable, enter instead the smaller amount you entered on the dotted line next to line 4e of Form 4952". Reads that optional dotted-line amount and otherwise falls back to Form 4952 line 4e.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 5
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 4 from line 3. If zero or less, enter -0-".

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 6 (qualified dividends after the line-5 offset)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 5 from line 2. If zero or less, enter -0-**". The double asterisk is the Form 2555 footnote (:1173-1174), and it IS implemented — on the SECOND run, as /feiSdtwLine6, where modification (2) reduces this amount by the unused capital gain excess. This fact is the FIRST run's line 6 and is deliberately unmodified; it is also the minuend /feiSdtwLine6 subtracts from, because the footnote says "the amount you would OTHERWISE enter".

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 7 (smaller of Schedule D line 15 or line 16)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D". Those are /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover and /netCapitalGainOrLoss in this module.
BOTH LEGS ARE GUARDED, and both guards are load-bearing here in a way the gate's are not. /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover reaches /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss through /netLongTermGainOrLoss, whose FALLBACK branch reads that writable BARE — so on a return with no Form 8949 detail it is Incomplete until the filer answers it, exactly as this paragraph said before the repoint, and the bareness is preserved for that reason rather than by accident. THE HOLE THIS PARAGRAPH DESCRIBES IS NARROWER NOW, and the narrowing is a real change to the analysis rather than a wording refresh: a return that answers /form8949Transactions takes the OTHER branch, which is complete-safe, so it resolves Complete with the writable unanswered — node-test scheduleD/form8949-multi-item-short-and-long-split asserts exactly that (/longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover Complete -4000.00, writable never answered). The guard below is therefore load-bearing only for the no-detail population, which is every return in the corpus today; /netCapitalGainOrLoss adds /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover bare inside its claims-Schedule-D arm, so it is Incomplete when Schedule D is claimed and only the long-term side was answered. Unlike the gate — whose All is false-dominant, so one Complete-false operand decides it — this is a LesserOf, which has no dominant operand: either Incomplete leg would make line 7 Incomplete and carry that through the whole worksheet to line 47. A blank Schedule D line is $0 on the worksheet, and line 9 floors line 7 at zero anyway, so $0 is both the safe and the correct substitution.
ONE POPULATION WHERE THIS LINE DIVERGES FROM THE QDCGT'S line 3, found by cross-checking the whole corpus and recorded here because the NEXT unit needs it. On the box-2a-only path — a filer with Form 1099-DIV capital gain distributions who files no Schedule D at all — /netCapitalGain deliberately returns the box-2a total, so /qdcgLine3 is that amount, while THIS line resolves $0: Schedule D lines 15 and 16 are genuinely blank for such a filer, and the guard supplies $0 for the Incomplete long-term leg. Both readings are right for their own worksheet — the source says "the smaller of line 15 or line 16 of SCHEDULE D", and a filer who files none has no such lines — but the consequence is that the SDTW would OVERSTATE tax for that population relative to the QDCGT (three corpus snapshots show it: one at $14,555 against $14,205, and two at $45,623 against $43,923). IT IS UNREACHABLE TODAY AND MUST STAY THAT WAY: /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet requires Schedule D lines 15 AND 16 to exceed zero, which is exactly what this population lacks, so all three snapshots have the gate false. Anyone loosening that gate — or wiring this worksheet to a filer who did not file Schedule D — must fix this line first.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 8
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 3 or line 4".

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 9 (net capital gain slice)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 8 from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0-**". The floor is what makes a Schedule D LOSS on line 7 harmless here. The double asterisk is the Form 2555 footnote (:1173-1174), implemented on the SECOND run as /feiSdtwLine9 (modification (1)); this fact is the first run's line 9, and it is also both the "amount you would otherwise enter" that modification reduces and the amount /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcessNotUsedAgainstLine9 measures the leftover against.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 10 (total preferential-rate income)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Add lines 6 and 9".

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 11 (Schedule D lines 18 and 19)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Add lines 18 and 19 of Schedule D**". The 28%-rate gain and the unrecaptured section 1250 gain, both shipping in this module (/twentyEightPercentRateGain and /unrecapturedSection1250Gain). Neither needs an IsComplete guard: every leg of both worksheets is a literal $0, a dividendReports CollectionSum, a complete-safe attestation alias, or already read through its own guard, which is why sd19-unanswered-default-safe can assert both Complete at $0 on a return where /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover is Incomplete. Six aliases were added to those worksheets and this sentence still holds, BY CONSTRUCTION: each alias is an IsComplete/Switch wrapper over its own writable, so an unanswered intake resolves Complete at $0 and cannot make this line Incomplete by contagion.
THE DOUBLE ASTERISK is the Form 2555 footnote (:1173-1174), and this is the line its modifications (3) and (4) exist for. IMPLEMENTED on the SECOND run as /feiSdtwLine11, which adds /feiSdtwScheduleDLine18 and /feiSdtwScheduleDLine19 — Schedule D's lines 18 and 19 as the footnote rewrites them. This fact is the FIRST run's line 11 and reads the unmodified amounts. THE $0 LEGS still carried by the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet under-state this line, and therefore under-state the 25% group downstream, for a filer who has one of them; the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet's lines 1-4 no longer carry any, though its line 5 is missing a SUBTRACTED Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) leg, which pushes the other way. The inventories live on /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine13 and /twentyEightPercentRateGain rather than being restated here.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19 threshold (top of the 24% ordinary bracket)
Fact.Description:
The dollar amount named inside Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15: "$197,300 if single or married filing separately; $394,600 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; or $197,300 if head of household."
THIS IS AN ORDINARY-RATE BOUNDARY, NOT A PREFERENTIAL ONE, which is the whole reason it is a new fact instead of a reuse. preferentialRateTax /qualDivCapGain0RateMax and /qualDivCapGain15RateMax come from Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section .03 (Maximum Capital Gains Rate); these two figures come from section .01 (Tax Rate Tables) and are EXACTLY the top of the 24% bracket in the 2025 rate schedule for every filing status — compare /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome, whose single/MFS/HOH 24% case ends at $197,300 and whose MFJ/QSS 24% case ends at $394,600. Reusing a preferential-rate fact here would have been numerically wrong and conceptually worse.
THE IDENTITY IS DEFINITIONAL, NOT COINCIDENTAL, and it is worth stating because it explains what line 19 is doing. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at the LESSER of 25% and the filer's ordinary rate, and 28%-rate gain at the lesser of 28% and the ordinary rate. Both caps can therefore only bite where the marginal ordinary rate first rises above them, and in a 10/12/22/24/32/35/37 schedule that point is the top of the 24% bracket. So the threshold moves with the ordinary bracket, and must: it is the same figure, not a parallel one. The param annotations below deliberately name the EXISTING bracket-top ledger rows rather than minting new ids, so the two can never drift apart.
MFS TAKES THE SINGLE/HOH AMOUNT HERE, unlike the 15%-rate maximum (where MFS is $300,000, half of MFJ). That asymmetry is the source's own — it prints $197,300 for single, MFS and head of household alike — and it matches the ordinary rate schedule, where MFS shares the single 24% bracket top.

The threshold itself is /sdtwLine19Threshold above. NOT to be confused with SCHEDULE D line 19, the unrecaptured section 1250 gain (/unrecapturedSection1250Gain), which this worksheet reads at lines 11 and 35.

The floor never actually bites: line 23 is always at least line 24 (the block header proves L23 >= L22 = L24), which is what keeps line 33 non-negative downstream.

Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter: $533,400 if single; $300,000 if married filing separately; $600,050 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; or $566,700 if head of household." Those are EXACTLY the figures preferentialRateTax /qualDivCapGain15RateMax already carries for QDCGT line 13, so this line REUSES that fact. Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 28 from line 27. If zero or less, enter -0-".

The instruction below it (:1144) reads "If lines 1 and 32 are the same, skip lines 33 through 43 and go to line 44"; not encoded, because line 1 equal to line 32 forces line 33 to zero and the 25%/28% groups with it (proof in the block header).

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 33 (amount taxed at 20%)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 32 from line 23". THE SOURCE GIVES THIS LINE NO FLOOR and it does not need one: line 33 equals line 25 less line 30, line 30 is a LesserOf with line 25 as an operand, so line 33 is max(line 25 - line 29, 0) and is never negative. The block header carries the L23 >= L22 step that argument rests on.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 34 (tax at 20%)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 33 by 20% (0.20)". Unrounded, as line 31.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 35 (the 25% group begins)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 9 above or Schedule D, line 19". SCHEDULE D line 19 is /unrecapturedSection1250Gain — the shipping worksheet, not this worksheet's own line 19.
THE GATE ABOVE THIS LINE (:1147), "If Schedule D, line 19, is zero or blank, skip lines 35 through 40 and go to line 41", IS NOT ENCODED and does not need to be: a zero Schedule D line 19 makes this line the smaller of line 9 and $0, hence $0, and line 39 then floors to $0 because line 38 is never negative. The sdtw-tax-28-percent-group-derived-example case is exactly that state (Schedule D line 19 = $0) and asserts lines 35 through 40 at zero.

How much of the unrecaptured section 1250 gain sits BELOW the point where the 25% cap beats the ordinary rate, and is therefore taxed inside line 21 instead.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 39 (amount taxed at 25%)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 38 from line 35. If zero or less, enter -0-".
