Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 40 (tax at 25%)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 39 by 25% (0.25)". Unrounded, as lines 31 and 34.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 41 (the 28% group begins)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Add lines 21, 22, 30, 33, and 39". Every dollar of taxable income already assigned to a rate: the ordinary base, the 0% slice, the 15% slice, the 20% slice and the 25% slice.
THE GATE ABOVE THIS LINE (:1154), "If Schedule D, line 18, is zero or blank, skip lines 41 through 43 and go to line 44", IS NOT ENCODED. A zero SCHEDULE D line 18 makes line 42 identically zero — that is the least obvious of the four skip proofs and the block header carries it in full. The sdtw-tax-25-percent-group-derived-example case is exactly that state (Schedule D line 18 = $0) and asserts lines 41 through 43 accordingly.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 42 (amount taxed at 28%)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 41 from line 1". THE SOURCE GIVES THIS LINE NO FLOOR EITHER, and again it does not need one: substituting line 41's collapse (line 21 + line 23 + line 39) shows line 42 is never negative, and is identically zero whenever Schedule D line 18 is zero. Both steps are in the block header.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 43 (tax at 28%)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 42 by 28% (0.28)". Unrounded, as lines 31, 34 and 40 — the last of the four multiplications the single Round at line 47 exists to protect.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 at its Tax Table row midpoint
Fact.Description: The Tax Table row midpoint of /sdtwLine21, exactly as taxCalculations /roundedTaxableIncome does for /taxableIncome and preferentialRateTax /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded does for the QDCGT's ordinary slice. Drives line 44 (the tax on line 21). STRUCTURAL TWIN of both of those (the engine has no taxOnAmount(x) primitive, so the midpoint Switch is duplicated with its input swapped); all three MUST stay in sync.

Fact.Name: Ordinary tax on Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 (worksheet line 44)
Fact.Description:
The tax-rate-schedule tax on /sdtwLine21, figured with the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet exactly as Form 1040 line 16 is. This is Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44.
THIS IS THE THIRD HARD-WIRED INSTANCE OF THE 2025 ORDINARY RATE SCHEDULE, and saying so plainly is part of this fact's contract rather than an apology for it. The other two are taxCalculations /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome (over /taxableIncome) and preferentialRateTax /ordinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncome (over the QDCGT's line-5 ordinary slice). The frozen engine has no function abstraction, so a single derivation cannot be parameterised by an arbitrary input amount and the bracket Switch has to be duplicated with its input swapped. GENERALISING THE RATE SCHEDULE INTO A REUSABLE HELPER IS A SEPARATE, LARGER REFACTOR AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SMUGGLED INTO THIS UNIT: it would be an engine-shaped change touching every filing status of three shipping facts, and it belongs in its own unit with its own baseline diff.
ALL THREE SWITCHES MUST STAY IN SYNC, and this one is pinned to the first by an identity rather than by hand-copied numbers: whenever line 21 equals line 1 — which happens whenever no preferential dollar escapes the ordinary base — line 44 must equal line 46. sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-at-top is exactly that state at a nonzero amount (line 21 = line 1 = $197,300, line 44 = line 46 = $40,199), and sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe is the degenerate $0 form of it. The bracket boundaries and base-tax amounts here were COPIED mechanically from the QDCGT twin rather than retyped, so the three cannot differ by a typo.
ROUNDING: this fact applies its own Round, and that is the first of the two carve-outs the subtree's "one Round at line 47" rule names. A rate-schedule tax is a whole-dollar table lookup, so rounding it is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate. Line 46 inherits the identical carve-out from /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44 (tax on line 21)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 21. If the amount on line 21 is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure the tax. If the amount on line 21 is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet." That is /ordinaryTaxOnSdtwLine21 above — the third hard-wired instance of the 2025 ordinary rate schedule, which that fact's Description explains and justifies. Arrives ALREADY ROUNDED; see the rounding carve-out there.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 45 (the worksheet tax)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Add lines 31, 34, 40, 43, and 44". The four rate multiplications still carry their cents at this point; only line 44 is pre-rounded. THIS is the sum the subtree's single Round exists to protect.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 46 (tax on line 1)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 1. If the amount on line 1 is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure the tax. If the amount on line 1 is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet." Line 1 is taxable income, so this is EXACTLY taxCalculations /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome, REUSED — the same fact /qdcgLine24 reads for the QDCGT's identical line. THE SECOND ROUNDING CARVE-OUT: that fact applies its own Round internally (dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml, Derived/Round/Switch), so line 46 arrives already rounded and this subtree inherits it. Consistent, not a conflict, for the same reason as line 44.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 47 — tax on all taxable income
Fact.Description:
THE SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET'S FINAL TAX, and the root of the /sdtwLine1 through /sdtwLine46 subtree above. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Tax on all taxable income (including capital gains and qualified dividends). Enter the smaller of line 45 or line 46. Also, include this amount on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16. (If you are filing Form 2555, don't enter this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040.)" This fact IS line 47; there is no separate /sdtwLine47, exactly as /qdcgLine25 is both the QDCGT's last line and its output.
THE SINGLE ROUND OF THE WHOLE WORKSHEET SITS HERE, matching /qdcgLine25's sibling treatment: the per-line children stay unrounded so the 15%, 20%, 25% and 28% multiplications (lines 31, 34, 40 and 43) do not each accumulate a rounding error before line 45 sums them. TWO EXCEPTIONS, stated so the claim is not read as absolute — lines 44 and 46 are rate-schedule taxes and each arrives already rounded from the fact that computes it (/ordinaryTaxOnSdtwLine21 and taxCalculations /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome). Rounding a whole-dollar table lookup is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate.
THAT PRE-ROUNDING IS NOT COSMETIC, and the tests say so: on sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-one-dollar-over, line 45 is $40,199.25 and line 46 is $40,199, so the lesser-of picks line 46 — the extra dollar's 25% tax loses to a line 46 that was rounded down from $40,199.32. A reviewer changing where the Round sits will break that case, which is the point of it.
THE FORM 2555 CARVE-OUT, BOTH HALVES, AND BOTH ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED — BY A SECOND WORKSHEET, NOT BY THIS ONE. Line 47's own text redirects the RESULT away from Form 1040 line 16 for a Form 2555 filer, and worksheet line 1 (:1084-1086) redirects the INPUT the same way ("if you are filing Form 2555 ... enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet"); the same footnote hangs off lines 6, 9 and 11 (:1173-1174). The footnote does not ask this worksheet to change — it asks for a SECOND run, "in its entirety and with the following additional modifications" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), whose modifications are "to be made only for purposes of filling out the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet above". That second run is /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax and the /feiSdtw* lineage below, and its root is taken by preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 on the arm that fires on /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet. THIS fact is the first run and keeps its unsubstituted input and its Form 1040 line 16 destination, which is right for every filer who is not completing that worksheet — and for the filer who is, taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome pre-empts the arm that reads this fact, so it never figures line 16 for them.
COMPUTED ON EVERY RETURN, DELIBERATELY. /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is NOT a term of this fact: it decides WHICH worksheet figures Form 1040 line 16, and that decision belongs to the consumer. Gating this fact on it would make the SDTW resolve to a fictitious $0 on every QDCGT return, which is worse than an honest "what the SDTW would produce". On a return with no preferential income at all the honest answer is the ordinary tax itself (line 21 = line 1, so line 44 = line 46 = line 45), which is what sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe asserts at $0.
CONSUMER: exactly one, AND IT EXISTS — /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome in taxCalculations (SHIPPING, dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml), which takes this path on its gate-true arm. It must not acquire another: Form 1040 line 16 has a single home, and a duplicate global path for it is a defect this fact deliberately avoids. STILL NO Export element, and the reason has changed rather than expired. The old reason was "the consumer lands one commit later", which is spent; the standing reason is that the consumer now genuinely reads this fact, so the wiring obligation is discharged by real consumption rather than by a declared visibility marker. An Export added on top of that would assert a broader downstream surface than one consumer, and nothing needs it.
WORLD-1 SAFETY, AS THE COMMIT THAT WIRED IT LEFT THINGS. This fact used to move no return's tax because nothing read it; now the rebody does, and Form 1040 line 16 follows this worksheet whenever /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is true. The gate-false population — the entire conformance corpus — keeps /qdcgLine25 character for character, which is what made the switch an additions-only delta. On the gate-TRUE population the consequence to keep in view is that the $0 legs still carried by Schedule D line 19 are live under-statements of tax for any filer who has one, in the regular tax through this worksheet and in the AMT through form6251 Part III. SCHEDULE D LINE 18 IS NOT AMONG THEM: the attestation pack fills every leg of its lines 1-4 subtotal. What line 18 can still get wrong runs the OTHER way — its line 5 is missing a SUBTRACTED Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D carryover, so that absence OVER-states line 18 and the 28% group.
COMPLETENESS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: Complete on 934 of the 938 resolved snapshots in the corpus, and the four it is absent from are EXACTLY the four /qdcgLine25 is absent from (all four resolve /taxableIncome Incomplete). Unconditional completeness is therefore NOT claimed: line 1 reads taxCalculations /taxableIncome bare, exactly as /qdcgLine1 does, so a return that leaves /taxableIncome Incomplete leaves this Incomplete too. That is the identical posture Form 1040 line 16 already has today, fact for fact, not a new hole.
CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE QDCGT ON THE WHOLE CORPUS, which is the strongest evidence this subtree has: when Schedule D lines 18 and 19 are both zero the SDTW degenerates to the QDCGT line for line (line 21 = /qdcgLine5, 22 = /qdcgLine9, 30 = /qdcgLine17, 33 = /qdcgLine20, 44 = /qdcgLine22, 45 = /qdcgLine23, 46 = /qdcgLine24, and this fact = Round(/qdcgLine25) — /qdcgLine25 carries the same lesser-of UNROUNDED). All eight identities hold on 931 of 931 eligible snapshots against a separately authored shipping implementation. The three excluded snapshots are the divergence recorded in /sdtwLine7's Description.

Fact.Name: Capital gain excess, measured on the SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET (starred footnote)
Fact.Description:
The Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet starred footnote's capital gain excess, in its Schedule D Tax Worksheet spelling: "To find out if you have a capital gain excess, subtract Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 15, from line 4 of your Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (line 10 of your Schedule D Tax Worksheet). If the result is more than zero, that amount is your capital gain excess" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
THE MINUEND IS SDTW LINE 10, NOT QDCGT LINE 4, AND THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE TWO MEASURES CAN DIVERGE. The parenthesis is not a restatement — it names a different quantity for the filer who uses this worksheet. SDTW line 10 is line 6 + line 9 (:1102), i.e. qualified dividends NET of the Form 4952 line 4g/4e offset at line 5 and net capital gain NET of the same offset at line 8 (:1097, :1101). QDCGT line 4 has no such offset. preferentialRateTax /feiCapitalGainExcess is the QDCGT measure and now diverges whenever a positive Form 4952 line 4g is present. This fact deliberately reads the SDTW's own line 10, so the newly representable election cannot overstate the excess.
THE MINUEND IS THE PASS-1 LINE 10. SDTW lines 2 through 10 do not depend on line 1 at all — check them: line 2 is qualified dividends, lines 3-5 the Form 4952 amounts, line 6 their offset against line 2, line 7 the Schedule D lines 15/16 minimum, line 8 the 4g/4e minimum, line 9 the offset against line 7, line 10 their sum — so the substitution at line 1 leaves line 10 unchanged and /sdtwLine10 IS the "line 10 of your Schedule D Tax Worksheet" the footnote means after "Complete the rest of that worksheet through ... line 10". Reading it off the MODIFIED /feiSdtwLine10 would be a cycle as well as wrong.
THE SUBTRAHEND IS FORM 1040 LINE 15 ITSELF, which in this module is /sdtwLine1 — the shipping worksheet's own line 1, read for the same reason preferentialRateTax's /feiCapitalGainExcess reads /qdcgLine1. It is NOT the substituted line 1: worksheet line 3 is Form 1040 line 15 PLUS the excluded income, and using it would make this quantity structurally negative.
WHAT IT MEASURES: the amount by which the return's preferential-rate income exceeds its POST-exclusion taxable income. Without the clawback the foreign earned income exclusion would shelter capital gain, and the second worksheet would tax preferential income the return's actual taxable income cannot hold.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (the footnote's "more than zero", floored here). Not rounded — an intermediate of unrounded worksheet lines.

Fact.Name: Capital gain excess left over after modification (1)
Fact.Description:
Modification (2)'s "any of your capital gain excess not used in (1) above" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). Modification (1) reduces SDTW line 9 by the excess but not below zero, so the amount it actually USES is the smaller of the excess and line 9, and what is left over is excess minus line 9, floored at zero.
WHY THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the excess is absorbed against the NET CAPITAL GAIN first (line 9) and only the remainder touches QUALIFIED DIVIDENDS (line 6). The footnote numbers the modifications and (2) names (1); reversing them would move income between the rate groups in the wrong order on any return carrying both. The QDCGT twin preferentialRateTax /feiCapitalGainExcessNotUsedAgainstLine3 makes the same argument about the QDCGT's lines 3 and 2.
THE SUBTRAHEND IS THE UNMODIFIED /sdtwLine9, deliberately: "the amount you would otherwise enter on ... line 9" is the amount before modification (1), which is exactly the shipping line. Reading /feiSdtwLine9 here would be a cycle.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE.

Fact.Name: SCHEDULE D line 18 as modification (3) rewrites it (28%-rate gain, reduced by the excess)
Fact.Description:
Modification (3), verbatim: "Reduce (but not below zero) the amount on your Schedule D, line 18, by your capital gain excess" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
SCHEDULE D line 18 is the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet's line 7 total, /twentyEightPercentRateGain in this module. This is one of the two modifications that made the predecessor contract a module-boundary unit: nothing in the QDCGT reads Schedule D line 18, so its starred lineage never needed this fact.
WHERE IT IS CONSUMED: /feiSdtwLine11 ("Add lines 18 and 19 of Schedule D**"). Note that the shipping /sdtwLine41 and /sdtwLine42 read no Schedule D line at all — the 28% group is driven by the worksheet's own lines — so line 11 is the only consumer here, unlike Schedule D line 19, which line 35 also reads directly.
COLLAPSES to the unmodified /twentyEightPercentRateGain when there is no excess.

Fact.Name: Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet line 17 as modification (4) rewrites it
Fact.Description:
Modification (4), verbatim: "Include your capital gain excess as a loss on line 16 of your Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet in the Instructions for Schedule D" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37). The worksheet's own line 16 carries the pointer back: "* If you are filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income), see the footnote in the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040 before completing this line" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13).
THE STRUCTURAL TWIN IS /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine17 and the ONLY difference is a third addend. Line 16 is a PRINTED NEGATIVE — "( )" on the form — so "include your capital gain excess as a loss on line 16" ADDS the excess to line 16's magnitude, which raises line 17 (the offset) and therefore LOWERS Schedule D line 19. That direction is the point of the modification: the same excess that is stripped out of lines 6 and 9 is stripped out of the 25% group too.
WHY THIS IS NOT "shipping line 17 plus the excess". Line 17's floor sits on the whole combine: shipping line 17 is max(line15mag + line16mag - line14, 0) and this fact is max(line15mag + line16mag + excess - line14, 0). When the shipping combine is a GAIN the shipping line is $0 and this one may still be $0 or may be positive, depending on whether the excess covers the gap. Adding the excess to the floored value would over-state the offset on exactly that population.
LINES 14, 15 AND 16 ARE THE TWIN'S, READ THE SAME WAY, guards and all: line 14 is /twentyEightPercentRateGainLines1Through4 (subtracted, because "enter it as a positive amount" negates the combine), line 15 is the magnitude of the Schedule D line 7 loss behind an IsComplete guard, and line 16 has BOTH of the twin's legs: the Schedule D line 14 carryover /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear behind the same guard, and the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D carryover /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverFromForm1041K1 ("Enter your long-term capital loss carryovers from Schedule D, line 14; and Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), box 11, code D", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13). Modification (4) adds the capital gain excess to line 16; it does not remove either carryover leg. The twin's Description carries the full algebra and the reason each guard is there; nothing about it changes here.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE by the source's own two branches. UNROUNDED: the single Round sits on /feiSdtwScheduleDLine19.

Fact.Name: SCHEDULE D line 19 as modification (4) rewrites it (unrecaptured section 1250 gain)
Fact.Description:
The Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 18 — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, pages 13, 15, 16, verbatim: "Unrecaptured section 1250 gain. Subtract line 17 from line 13. If zero or less, enter -0-. If more than zero, enter the result here and on Schedule D, line 19" — run with modification (4)'s line 17.
LINE 13 IS UNMODIFIED and is the shipping /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine13. Modification (4) names line 16 and nothing else, and line 13 is the sum of lines 9 through 12; the two halves of the worksheet do not meet until line 18.
TWO CONSUMERS IN THE SECOND WORKSHEET, and the second one is the trap the block header names: /feiSdtwLine11 ("Add lines 18 and 19 of Schedule D**") and /feiSdtwLine35 ("Enter the smaller of line 9 above or Schedule D, line 19"). Line 35 carries no `**` marker, because the marker records where the FOOTNOTE attaches and not where Schedule D line 19 is read; the modification is to Schedule D's line itself, so both reads move.
COLLAPSES to the unmodified /unrecapturedSection1250Gain when there is no excess. The Round is the twin's, in the twin's place, and commutes with the floor for the same reason.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 1 (the SUBSTITUTED taxable income)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter your taxable income from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15. (However, if you are filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income), enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the instructions for Form 1040, line 16.)" THIS SUBSTITUTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE SECOND LINEAGE — it is the only line that differs from the shipping /sdtwLine1 by more than an arithmetic reduction, and everything downstream differs because of it. The Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet states the same substitution from its own end at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37.
The shipping /sdtwLine1 keeps its unsubstituted reading and is still the right fact for Form 1040 line 16 on every non-Form-2555 return; it is also what /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcess subtracts, because the footnote's subtrahend is Form 1040 line 15 itself.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 2 (qualified dividends)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter your qualified dividends from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a". Independent of line 1 and untouched by the modifications — modification (2) names line 6, not line 2 — so this is the shipping /sdtwLine2.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 3 (Form 4952 line 4g)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the amount from Form 4952 (used to figure investment interest expense deduction), line 4g". Aliases the shipping /sdtwLine3 so the second worksheet receives the same elected Form-4952 dollar.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 4 (Form 4952 line 4e)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the amount from Form 4952, line 4e*". Aliases /sdtwLine4, including its optional dotted-line attribution.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 5
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 4 from line 3. If zero or less, enter -0-". Derived from THIS worksheet's lines 3 and 4, which are the first run's amounts, so it equals the shipping /sdtwLine5 on every return; written as the subtraction rather than as an alias of that fact because the printed line says "line 3" and "line 4", and in a second run those are this worksheet's own.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 6 (qualified dividends, reduced by modification (2))
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 5 from line 2. If zero or less, enter -0-**", as modified by the starred footnote's modification (2): "Reduce (but not below zero) the amount you would otherwise enter on ... line 6 of your Schedule D Tax Worksheet by any of your capital gain excess not used in (1) above" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
THE DOUBLE ASTERISK IS THE FOOTNOTE POINTER ITSELF (:1173-1174: "If you are filing Form 2555, see the footnote in the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040, line 16, before completing this line"), so this modification is printed on both ends rather than inferred.
THE BODY IS THE FOOTNOTE'S OWN CONSTRUCTION, in two steps rather than one: "the amount you would otherwise enter" — this worksheet's line 6 computed normally, max(line 2 − line 5, 0) — reduced by the leftover excess, "but not below zero". The inner floor is the printed line's own "If zero or less, enter -0-" and the outer one is the modification's; they are written separately because they come from different sentences, even though the pair collapses to a single floor arithmetically. Lines 2 and 5 are the first run's amounts, so this fact equals max(/sdtwLine6 − the leftover, 0) on every return, and collapses to /sdtwLine6 itself when there is no excess.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 7 (smaller of Schedule D line 15 or line 16)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D". No modification names Schedule D lines 15 or 16 — (3) names line 18 and (4) the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet — and this line does not depend on line 1, so it is the shipping /sdtwLine7, guards and all. The box-2a divergence recorded on that fact is inherited unchanged, and is unreachable here for the same reason: the route that selects this worksheet requires Schedule D lines 15 and 16 to be gains.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 8
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 3 or line 4" — this worksheet's lines 3 and 4, which are the first run's amounts, so it equals the shipping /sdtwLine8 on every return.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 9 (net capital gain slice, reduced by modification (1))
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 8 from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0-**", as modified by the starred footnote's modification (1): "Reduce (but not below zero) the amount you would otherwise enter on ... line 9 of your Schedule D Tax Worksheet by your capital gain excess" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37).
THIS IS WHERE THE EXCESS LANDS FIRST, which is what makes /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcessNotUsedAgainstLine9 a leftover rather than the whole excess. The double asterisk (:1173-1174) is the printed pointer to the footnote.
THE BODY IS THE FOOTNOTE'S OWN CONSTRUCTION, in two steps, exactly as /feiSdtwLine6: "the amount you would otherwise enter" — this worksheet's line 9 computed normally, max(line 7 − line 8, 0) — reduced by the excess, "but not below zero". Lines 7 and 8 are the first run's amounts, so that inner value is /sdtwLine9 to the cent, which is why /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcessNotUsedAgainstLine9 may read the shipping fact for the same quantity without a cycle. Collapses to /sdtwLine9 when there is no excess.

NOT the pass-1 line 10 the capital gain excess is measured against — that is the shipping /sdtwLine10; see /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcess. This one is the sum of the two MODIFIED lines, and the difference between them is exactly the excess that modifications (1) and (2) removed.

Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Add lines 18 and 19 of Schedule D**". THE DOUBLE ASTERISK IS THE FOOTNOTE POINTER (:1173-1174) and this is the line it exists for: modifications (3) and (4) are the two that reach out of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet and into Schedule D, and they meet here. /feiSdtwScheduleDLine18 is Schedule D line 18 reduced by the excess; /feiSdtwScheduleDLine19 is Schedule D line 19 recomputed with the excess included as a loss on the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 16.
Collapses to the shipping /sdtwLine11 when there is no excess.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 35 (the 25% group begins — the second read of Schedule D line 19)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 9 above or Schedule D, line 19".
THIS LINE CARRIES NO `**` MARKER AND IS MODIFIED ANYWAY, and it is the one place a reader working the printed markers alone gets this worksheet wrong. The markers on lines 6, 9 and 11 record where the FOOTNOTE attaches; modification (4) modifies SCHEDULE D's line 19 itself, so every read of that amount moves — here and at line 11. Schedule D line 19 in this second run is /feiSdtwScheduleDLine19.
THE GATE ABOVE THIS LINE (:1147), "If Schedule D, line 19, is zero or blank, skip lines 35 through 40 and go to line 41", IS NOT ENCODED and does not need to be, on the shipping twin's proof read over the modified amount: a zero MODIFIED Schedule D line 19 makes this line the smaller of line 9 and $0, hence $0, and line 39 then floors to $0 because line 38 is never negative.

Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 41 from line 1". Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 42 by 28% (0.28)". Unrounded, as lines 31, 34 and 40.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 at its Tax Table row midpoint
Fact.Description: The Tax Table row midpoint of /feiSdtwLine21, the second worksheet's line 21. STRUCTURAL TWIN of /sdtwLine21Rounded, taxCalculations /roundedTaxableIncome, preferentialRateTax /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded and preferentialRateTax /feiWorksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded (the engine has no taxOnAmount(x) primitive, so the midpoint Switch is duplicated with its input swapped); all five MUST stay in sync. Drives the second worksheet's line 44.

Fact.Name: Ordinary tax on the second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 (its line 44)
Fact.Description:
The tax-rate-schedule tax on /feiSdtwLine21, figured with the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet exactly as Form 1040 line 16 is. This is the SECOND Schedule D Tax Worksheet's line 44 — the run the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet's starred footnote orders on a substituted line 1.
THIS IS THE FIFTH HARD-WIRED INSTANCE OF THE 2025 ORDINARY RATE SCHEDULE, and the second one this module carries. The other four are taxCalculations /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome (over /taxableIncome), preferentialRateTax /ordinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncome (over the QDCGT's line-5 ordinary slice), /ordinaryTaxOnSdtwLine21 above (over the shipping worksheet's line 21) and preferentialRateTax /ordinaryTaxOnFeiWorksheetOrdinaryIncome (over the starred QDCGT's line 5). The engine has no function abstraction, so a single derivation cannot be parameterised by an arbitrary input amount and the bracket Switch has to be duplicated with its input swapped. GENERALISING THE RATE SCHEDULE INTO A REUSABLE HELPER IS A SEPARATE, LARGER REFACTOR and was deliberately not smuggled into this unit; the count is stated plainly rather than apologised for, and it is the reason the predecessor contract asked whether a parallel lineage was the right shape. The answer is that this engine has no scalar parameterisation, so it is.
WHY THIS COPY IS NEEDED AT ALL, when the second worksheet's line 46 needs none: line 46 taxes line 1, and the second worksheet's line 1 is the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet's line 3, which preferentialRateTax already taxes as /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4OrdinaryRoute. Line 21 is a different amount — larger than the shipping worksheet's line 21 by the excluded income — and nothing else in the graph taxes it.
ALL FIVE SWITCHES MUST STAY IN SYNC. This one is a byte-for-byte copy of /ordinaryTaxOnSdtwLine21 with its input dependency swapped; nothing else differs, and nothing else may.
ROUNDED HERE, like every one of its twins: a whole-dollar Tax Table lookup is rounded as part of computing it, not truncated early. The second worksheet's one-Round rule is about lines 31, 34, 40 and 43, which stay unrounded to line 45.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44 (tax on line 21)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 21. If the amount on line 21 is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure the tax. If the amount on line 21 is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet." That is /ordinaryTaxOnFeiSdtwLine21 above — the FIFTH hard-wired instance of the 2025 ordinary rate schedule in this dictionary, and the second one this module carries. Arrives ALREADY ROUNDED; see the rounding note there.
A COPY IS UNAVOIDABLE HERE, unlike at line 46. Line 46 taxes line 1, and the second worksheet's line 1 is Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 3, which preferentialRateTax already taxes as /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4OrdinaryRoute. Line 21 is a quantity nothing else in the graph taxes.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 45 (the worksheet tax)
Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 46 (tax on line 1)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 1. If the amount on line 1 is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure the tax. If the amount on line 1 is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet." Line 1 here is the SUBSTITUTED line 1 — Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 3 — so this line is exactly preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4OrdinaryRoute, the unstarred route's own answer, and no SIXTH copy of the bracket schedule is needed.
IT MUST POINT AT THE EXTRACTED ORDINARY BODY AND NEVER AT THE SELECTOR. preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 is the fact that CHOOSES between the unstarred route, the starred QDCGT and this worksheet; a line 46 pointing at it would be a cycle through this fact's own consumer. The extraction that made this possible is the same one starred QDCGT line 24 needed.
THE SECOND ROUNDING CARVE-OUT, as on the twin: that fact applies its own Round internally, so line 46 arrives already rounded.

Fact.Name: Second Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 47 — the tax the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet puts on its line 4
Fact.Description:
THE SECOND WORKSHEET'S FINAL TAX, and the root of the /feiSdtwLine1 through /feiSdtwLine46 subtree above. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Tax on all taxable income (including capital gains and qualified dividends). Enter the smaller of line 45 or line 46. Also, include this amount on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16. (If you are filing Form 2555, don't enter this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040.)" This fact IS line 47; there is no separate /feiSdtwLine47, exactly as /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax is both the shipping worksheet's last line and its output.
THE PARENTHESIS IS THIS FACT'S ENTIRE REASON FOR EXISTING. Line 47's Form 2555 sentence names the destination — Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 4 — and its line 1 names the input; the shipping /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax honours neither, because it is the FIRST run, the one that figures Form 1040 line 16 for everybody else. This fact is the second run.
UNROUNDED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE SHIPPING TWIN — the one place a faithful copy would be wrong. /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax wraps its LesserOf in a Round because its destination is Form 1040 line 16, a printed whole-dollar entry line. THIS worksheet's printed destination is Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 4, and that line has a Round of its own on preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4. Rounding here as well would be a second rounding of the same number — harmless when idempotent but wrong in principle and untrue to the printed route. This is precisely the treatment preferentialRateTax /feiQdcgLine25 gets for the starred QDCGT, and for the same printed reason. The module's "all three Switches MUST stay in sync" rule is about the bracket-schedule twins and does NOT reach this line; a reviewer "restoring" the Round here will move a Form 2555 return's tax.
CONSUMER: exactly one — preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4, arm 1, which fires on /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet. It must not acquire another: this is a worksheet run FOR one printed line and has no other printed destination.
COMPUTED ON EVERY RETURN, like the shipping twin and for the twin's reason: the gate decides WHICH worksheet figures the tax, and that decision belongs to the consumer. Completeness posture is the twin's too — line 1 reads preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine3, which reads /taxableIncome through worksheet line 1, so a return that leaves /taxableIncome Incomplete leaves this Incomplete as well, in exactly the places /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax and /qdcgLine25 are already Incomplete. No new hole.
THE COLLAPSE THAT MAKES THE ARM SAFE, which is the same argument /feiQdcgLine25 makes for the default arm: with no preferential income at all, lines 6, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 are zero, line 18 equals line 1, line 20 is at most line 14 = line 1, so line 21 = line 1 and lines 22, 30, 33 and 39 are zero — leaving line 45 = line 44 = the tax on line 1 = line 46, so this fact IS line 46. The arm therefore degenerates to the unstarred route for a return with nothing preferential, which is what the entry test guarantees it will never actually see.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE. UNROUNDED, per the paragraph above.

Fact.Name: Capital loss deduction limit
Fact.Description:
Schedule D line 21: the maximum net capital loss deductible against ordinary income, $3,000 ($1,500 MFS).
THE EXCESS IS NOW MODELLED, and the sentence that used to stand here said the opposite. It read "Excess loss carries to future years - NOT modeled, interpretation:provisional D4". That is false as of this commit: the excess this limit discards is computed line by line by the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet at the end of this module and lands in /shortTermCapitalLossCarryoverToNextYear (worksheet line 8) and /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverToNextYear (worksheet line 13). The provisional D4 tag is retired with it — the two carry-OUTs are worksheet-verified against the printed worksheet, not a provisional reading.
WHAT REMAINS TRUE is narrower and worth keeping: this graph still does not carry the amount INTO a following year by itself. That transfer is a cross-year unit, and its receiving half already ships as the attested writables /writableShortTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear and /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear. No prior-year state is read anywhere in the worksheet.

Fact.Name: Capital gain or loss for Form 1040 line 7
Fact.Description: Form 1040 line 7a: the line-16 net if a gain or zero; if a loss, the smaller in magnitude of the loss or the $3,000/$1,500 limit (i.e. the loss floored at -$3,000/-$1,500). Flows into total income.

Fact.Name: Net capital gain (preferential-rate eligible)
Fact.Description: Net capital gain per §1(h)/§1222(11): the excess of net long-term gain over net short-term loss, floored at zero - modeled as max(0, min(line 16 net, net long-term)). Used as the "net capital gain" subtraction in the QBI cap base (Form 8995 line 12) AND as /qdcgLine3, the net-capital-gain input to the (live) Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet — so it drives the preferential 0/15/20% rate on Form 1040 line 16. On the box-2a-only "no Schedule D required" path (the non-claiming case) this returns the box-2a total /capitalGainDistributions, so a box-2a-only filer reaches that worksheet too (previously it returned 0 and was over-taxed at ordinary rates). ON THAT SAME NO-SCHEDULE-D PATH THE return is box 2a PLUS form8814:/form8814TotalLine10CapitalGainDistributions, the child's capital gain distributions an IRC 1(g)(7) election puts on the parent's line 7a by the direct route (i8814 Line 10: "or Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 7a"). They are Form 1099-DIV box 2a distributions in the child's hands and carry the same long-term character the parent's own box 2a has here, so without this addend a Form 8814 parent with no Schedule D would have line 7a filled by income:/capitalGainsOrLosses while the QDCG worksheet's line 3 read $0, an over-taxation re-opened for the child's share. On the Schedule-D path the figure arrives through /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's line 13 term, so it is never counted twice.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 21, the capital loss allowed against ordinary income
Fact.Description:
THE PRINTED SCHEDULE D LINE 21, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sd.pdf, page 2, verbatim: "If line 16 is a loss, enter here and on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 7a, the smaller of: The loss on line 16; or ($3,000), or if married filing separately, ($1,500). Note: When figuring which amount is smaller, treat both amounts as positive numbers."
WHY THIS FACT EXISTS, since the graph already holds the quantity twice. The IRS1040SD register printed line 21 out of /clcwLine2, a Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet fact, and the carry-map audit asked for it to be re-pointed at /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 instead. NEITHER IS THE PRINTED BOX. /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 is Form 1040 line 7a: it is SIGNED and on a gain return it holds the whole GAIN, so printing it would fill the line-21 box with a number the line forbids. /clcwLine2 has the right magnitude but the wrong domain: it is floored at $0 so the carryover worksheet always has a number, and on a gain return - where Schedule D line 21 is BLANK, because line 17's "No" routes the filer past lines 18 through 21 - it prints 0.00. This fact is the printed box itself: the positive magnitude when line 16 is a loss, and UNDEFINED otherwise, so the box renders empty exactly when the form leaves it empty. The undefined fall-through is the display idiom ctcOdc /pdf8812Line24 and its Part II-B neighbours already use.
POSITIVE, NOT SIGNED, because the printed box carries its own parentheses: the form prints "21 ( )" and the Note tells the filer to "treat both amounts as positive numbers". That is the same magnitude /clcwLine2 needs, which is why /clcwLine2 now READS this fact instead of re-deriving it - one quantity, one fact - and keeps only its own $0 floor for the gain case the worksheet still has to number.
NO VALUE MOVES ANYWHERE. Nothing on the tax path reads this fact; /clcwLine2's output is identical case for case (on a loss return the old GreaterOf and this Subtract are the same number, and on a gain return both are $0), so the carryover worksheet, Form 1040 line 7a and every committed figure are untouched.
COMPLETE-SAFE IN THE SAME SENSE /clcwLine2 IS: the only fact it reads on the loss arm is /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040, which reaches the Schedule D nets through /netCapitalGainOrLoss and its /claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses gate. On a return that never claims capital gains, line 16 is not a loss and this fact is undefined, which is a blank box and not an Incomplete return.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 1 (Form 1040 line 15, UNFLOORED)
Fact.Description:
Line 1 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Enter the amount from your 2024 Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15. If the amount would have been a loss if you could enter a negative number on that line, enclose the amount in parentheses" — read for the 2025-to-2026 direction, so "2024" is THIS return.
THIS FACT EXISTS BECAUSE taxCalculations /taxableIncome CANNOT ANSWER THE LINE. That fact is Round(GreaterOf(Subtract(/agi, /totalDeductions), $0)) — floored at zero, read on disk, not assumed — so the parenthesised negative the line explicitly asks for has already been thrown away by the time /taxableIncome exists. This is the same subtraction with the floor removed and nothing else changed, which is why it is authored here in scheduleD rather than beside /taxableIncome: it exists only for this worksheet and has no other consumer.
READ BARE, no completeness wrapper, exactly as /sdtwLine1 reads /taxableIncome: /agi and /totalDeductions are Complete on any return that reaches this point.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 2 (Schedule D line 21 loss, as a positive amount)
Fact.Description:
Line 2 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Enter the loss from your 2024 Schedule D, line 21, as a positive amount" — the 2025-to-2026 reading, so "2024" is THIS return.
THIS LINE IS NOT /capitalLossLimit. /capitalLossLimit is the $3,000/$1,500 CAP. The line asks for Schedule D line 21 itself, which is the loss actually TAKEN — the smaller of the line 16 loss and that cap. The two differ for every filer whose whole capital loss fits under the limit, and using the cap OVER-states line 4, which OVER-states line 7, which UNDER-states the short-term carryover at line 8. the contract's wiring returns 0 on the same return.
IT READS /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 BECAUSE THAT FACT IS SCHEDULE D LINE 21 WHEN LINE 21 EXISTS. The printed form says so: "21 If line 16 is a loss, enter here and on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 7a, the smaller of: [the loss on line 16]; ($3,000), or if married filing separately, ($1,500)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sd.pdf, page 2). Line 21 and Form 1040 line 7a are the same number on a loss return, and /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 is that number. No separate line-21 node is added for a value the graph already holds.
THE Max $0 FLOOR IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DEFENSIVE. When line 16 is a gain, Schedule D line 21 is blank and the worksheet's "the loss from line 21" is nothing, but /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 holds the GAIN, so the bare negation would be negative and line 4 would go negative with it — manufacturing a short-term carryover for a filer with no short-term loss at all. An 8,000 short-term gain against a 5,000 long-term loss, netting to a 3,000 gain, is exactly that return: both outputs are 0 with the floor and the unfloored reading yields 3,000.
Complete-safe with no wrapper of its own: /capitalGainOrLossForForm1040 reaches the Schedule D nets only through /netCapitalGainOrLoss, which already carries the /claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses gate.
IT READS THE PRINTED LINE-21 FACT RATHER THAN RE-DERIVING IT. /scheduleDLine21CapitalLossAllowed is the printed Schedule D line 21 box (positive magnitude, undefined on a gain return), which lets the IRS1040SD register print line 21 from that fact rather than this worksheet fact. The Max $0 floor argued for above did not go away - it is the explicit second Case, which is what makes this fact different from the printed one and is the whole reason both exist. The value is unchanged case for case: on a loss return the GreaterOf and the second arm are the same Subtract, and on a gain return both are $0, so every committed clcw figure is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 3 (combine lines 1 and 2)
Fact.Description:
Line 3 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Combine lines 1 and 2. If zero or less, enter -0-".
WHAT IT MEANS, since the arithmetic alone does not show it: line 1 is taxable income AFTER the capital loss deduction and line 2 is that deduction as a positive, so their sum is taxable income as it would have stood WITHOUT the deduction. The floor at zero is what makes line 4 measure the part of the loss the return could actually absorb.
Line 4 is then 0 — none of the deduction was absorbed — and the ENTIRE 5,000 short-term loss carries, which is correct: a return with no taxable income loses nothing. Without the printed floor line 4 would be -5,750, line 7 would follow it negative, and line 8 would report a 10,750 carryover — MORE than the loss the filer had. That is the sharpest statement of why line 1 must be the unfloored Form 1040 line 15 and this line must be floored: the negative belongs on line 1, where it measures unused deduction, and must not survive past line 3.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 4 (the smaller of line 2 or line 3)
Fact.Description: Line 4 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 2 or line 3". This is the amount of the capital loss deduction the return actually used: the deduction claimed (line 2), or all the income there was to absorb it (line 3), whichever is less. It is SHARED by both outputs — line 7 for the short-term side and line 11 for the long-term side.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 5 (Schedule D line 7 loss, as a positive amount)
Fact.Description:
Line 5 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Enter the loss from your 2024 Schedule D, line 7, as a positive amount", governed by the skip instruction printed immediately above it at lines 804-805: "If line 7 of your 2024 Schedule D is a loss, go to line 5; otherwise, enter -0- on line 5 and go to line 9."
THE SKIP INSTRUCTION IS THE FLOOR, not a separate arm. "Enter -0- on line 5" for a line 7 that is not a loss is precisely what GreaterOf(0 - line 7, 0) returns, and the "go to line 9" half — which skips lines 6, 7 and 8 — needs no encoding either, because line 8 already floors at zero and line 7 is never negative. An explicit conditional would add an arm no witness could distinguish from this one.
/shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover is Incomplete for a filer reporting no capital gains, so the read sits behind the /claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses Switch that /netCapitalGainOrLoss already uses.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 6 (any gain from Schedule D line 15)
Fact.Description:
Line 6 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Enter any gain from your 2024 Schedule D, line 15. If a loss, enter -0-". A long-term GAIN absorbs short-term loss before any of it can carry, which is why it is added to line 4 at line 7. Same /claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses wrapper as line 5, for the same Incomplete read.
Line 7 becomes 5,000 rather than 3,000 and the carryover is 5,000; a fill omitting this line would report 7,000, over-stating it by exactly the amount the long-term gain absorbed.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 7 (add lines 4 and 6)
Fact.Description: Line 7 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Add lines 4 and 6". The total short-term loss the year consumed: the part deducted against ordinary income (line 4) plus the part netted against long-term gain (line 6).

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 8 — short-term capital loss carryover to 2026
Fact.Description:
Line 8 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Short-term capital loss carryover for 2025. Subtract line 7 from line 5. If zero or less, enter -0-. If more than zero, also enter this amount on Schedule D, line 6" — the 2025-to-2026 instance, so the carryover is for 2026 and its destination is NEXT year's Schedule D line 6.
It landed in ONE commit with its long-term twin /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverToNextYear, which is what both contracts required: "Neither lands alone."
EXPORTED, CONSUMED THIS YEAR, AND NOT TRANSMITTED. Form 8960's /niitWorksheetRow2iCapitalLossCarryforwardAdjustment reads this beside the long-term carry-out to supply worksheet row 2(i)(2), when that NIIT row has a positive column-(A) basis to adjust. The result can change this return's net investment income, but the carry-out itself still appears on no line of the 2025 return: its downstream form-line consumer is next year's Schedule D line 6, which this graph models as the carry-IN writable /writableShortTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear. Both uses preserve the positive-magnitude convention. Export downstreamFacts makes the current-year NIIT dependency available; the output remains deliberately NOT mef because there is nothing to transmit as this year's standalone carry-out.
SIGN AND ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE by the printed floor. The single Round is here, at the printed entry line, per the /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover convention; every input is already whole-dollar, so it changes nothing today.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 9 (Schedule D line 15 loss, as a positive amount)
Fact.Description:
Line 9 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Enter the loss from your 2024 Schedule D, line 15, as a positive amount", governed by the skip instruction printed immediately above it at line 812: "If line 15 of your 2024 Schedule D is a loss, go to line 9; otherwise, skip lines 9 through 13."
THE SKIP IS THE FLOOR AGAIN. "Skip lines 9 through 13" means line 13 is blank, and a line 9 of 0 gives exactly that: line 13 subtracts a non-negative line 12 from it and floors at zero. The mirror of the line-5 argument, and the second of the two block-skip conditionals the long-term contract warned a fill would get wrong. It is not skipped here; it is proved equal.
Same /claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses wrapper as line 5.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 10 (any gain from Schedule D line 7)
Fact.Description: Line 10 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Enter any gain from your 2024 Schedule D, line 7. If a loss, enter -0-". The mirror of line 6: a short-term GAIN absorbs long-term loss before any of it can carry. Same /claimsCapitalGainsOrLosses wrapper.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 11 (subtract line 5 from line 4)
Fact.Description:
Line 11 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Subtract line 5 from line 4. If zero or less, enter -0-".
THIS IS THE COUPLING, and it is the reason the two outputs could not land separately. Line 4 and line 5 are the SHORT-term computation's own terms, and this line carries what is left of the ordinary-income deduction after the short-term loss has taken its share — the part that must have come from the long-term side, and so must be subtracted from the long-term carryover at line 12.
THE CONDITION UNDER WHICH IT BITES, stated precisely because the contract's version was not. /longTermCapitalLossCarryoverToNextYear's contract warned that a fill omitting lines 4, 5 and 11 "diverges whenever only one of the two nets is a loss". That is not the condition. This line is non-zero exactly when line 4 exceeds line 5 — when the deduction actually absorbed is LARGER than the short-term loss, so the excess necessarily came out of the long-term side. A fill without this line would report a 5,000 long-term carryover instead of 3,000 — over-stating it by exactly the long-term loss the return already deducted, and breaking the conservation identity (the two carryovers sum to the line-16 loss less the allowed deduction) that every other case in the set satisfies. It is the ONLY case, in the node tests and in the committed corpus alike, where this line is non-zero.

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 12 (add lines 10 and 11)
Fact.Description: Line 12 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Add lines 10 and 11". The total long-term loss the year consumed: the part netted against short-term gain (line 10) plus the part deducted against ordinary income after the short-term loss took its share (line 11).

Fact.Name: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet line 13 — long-term capital loss carryover to 2026
Fact.Description:
Line 13 of the Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 10, verbatim: "Long-term capital loss carryover for 2025. Subtract line 12 from line 9. If zero or less, enter -0-. If more than zero, also enter this amount on Schedule D, line 14" — the 2025-to-2026 instance, so the destination is NEXT year's Schedule D line 14.
It ships together with its short-term twin.
CHARACTER IS PRESERVED, which is the whole reason there are two outputs rather than one: a short-term carryover stays short-term and a long-term one stays long-term, and the inbound side already ships as two separate writables for the same reason. This one lands in /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear next year, which reduces the LONG-term side and thereby the preferential-rate net capital gain.
Form 8960's /niitWorksheetRow2iCapitalLossCarryforwardAdjustment reads this beside the short-term carry-out to supply worksheet row 2(i)(2). Its current-year use and the downstream Schedule D line-14 carry-in preserve the long-term character. As on the short-term twin, this is an exported calculation, not a TY2025 form-line amount, so it is not transmitted on this return.
SIGN AND ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE by the printed floor; the single Round is here.
Both entry-test-fails cases pin this output at 0.

Fact.Name: Net long-term gain or loss from Schedule(s) K-1 (Schedule D line 12)
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 12 as printed: the net LONG-term capital gain or (loss) passed through to the filer on Schedules K-1 from partnerships, S corporations, estates and trusts. The long-term twin of the line 5 intake and the same posture: an OPTIONAL PRINT COMPONENT of the collapsed long-term intake /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss, never a second addend. /netLongTermGainOrLoss is titled "Schedule D lines 8a, 8b, 9, 10 and 12", so line 12 is already inside that net; wiring this fact into it, or into /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover, would double count. IT IS NOT PURELY ATTESTED: scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableK1065Box9aNetLongTermCapitalGain (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 9a, whose instructions say "Report the net long-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 12") and scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox4aNetLongTermCapitalGain (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 4a, routed by the K-1's own table to "Schedule D, line 12"). The printed line is now /scheduleDLine12NetLongTermFromScheduleK1, which sums those rows when any of them answered the box and reads THIS attestation otherwise. This fact stays as the FALLBACK arm, and the register must print the derived fact rather than this one. Dollar with NO minimum, because the printed line reads "gain or (loss)" and a K-1 long-term loss is a negative entry.

Fact.Name: Net short-term gain or loss from Schedule(s) K-1 (Schedule D line 5)
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 5 as printed: the net SHORT-term capital gain or (loss) passed through to the filer on Schedules K-1 from partnerships, S corporations, estates and trusts. It is an OPTIONAL PRINT COMPONENT of an amount this module already collects, not a second addend, and nothing may wire it into a total. The line-5 figure is one of the amounts the taxpayer already folds into the collapsed short-term intake /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss: /nonForm8949ShortTermRemainder names it in so many words as "line 5 (the K-1 short-term net)". Adding it to /netShortTermGainOrLoss or to /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover would therefore double count it. It exists so the printed form can show the line rather than leave it blank while its value sits inside the collapsed net, exactly the posture scheduleA takes for the line 5a print component of its combined tax intake. IT IS NOT PURELY ATTESTED: scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableK1065Box8NetShortTermCapitalGain (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 8, whose instructions say "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5") and scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox3NetShortTermCapitalGain (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 3, routed by the K-1's own table to "Schedule D, line 5"). The printed line is now /scheduleDLine5NetShortTermFromScheduleK1, which sums those rows when any of them answered the box and reads THIS attestation otherwise. This fact stays as the FALLBACK arm, and the register must print the derived fact rather than this one. Dollar with NO minimum, because the printed line reads "gain or (loss)" and a K-1 short-term loss is a negative entry.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1's net short-term capital gain or (loss)
Fact.Description:
This Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S) item's contribution to Schedule D line 5: box 8 as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableK1065Box8NetShortTermCapitalGain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. Complete-safe, so a /formK1s item recorded for its ordinary income alone still contributes a Complete $0 and the CollectionSum over the collection stays Complete.
SIGNED, WITH NO FLOOR: box 8 is captioned "Net short-term capital gain (loss)" and the printed Schedule D line 5 reads "Net short-term gain or (loss)", so a pass-through loss is a negative entry and flooring it would discard the amount the box exists to report. The Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) twin is box 7, "Net short-term capital gain (loss)", and this module reads the same leaf for it because scheduleE records both entity types on the one /formK1s collection.
A scheduleD fact living on scheduleE's /formK1s collection, the cross-module shape ../collectiblesGainForScheduleD uses one block up.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1 answers box 8
Fact.Description: True when THIS /formK1s item answered box 8, the net short-term capital gain (loss). It is an IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../shortTermCapitalGainForScheduleD, because that bridge is Complete on every item and a predicate built from it would be true for a K-1 recorded for its ordinary income alone. Counted by /shortTermGainFromK1RowsAnswered, which decides whether Schedule D line 5 is derived from the rows or falls back to the attested total /writableScheduleDLine5NetShortTermFromScheduleK1.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's net short-term capital gain
Fact.Description: This Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) item's contribution to Schedule D line 5: box 3 as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox3NetShortTermCapitalGain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. Complete-safe, the twin of /formK1s/*/shortTermCapitalGainForScheduleD, and signed for the same reason: the K-1's own routing table sends box 3 to "Schedule D, line 5", which is a gain or (loss) line.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1 answers box 3
Fact.Description: True when THIS /form1041K1s item answered box 3, the net short-term capital gain. An IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../shortTermCapitalGainForScheduleD. Counted by /shortTermGainFromK1RowsAnswered.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1's net long-term capital gain or (loss)
Fact.Description:
This Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S) item's contribution to Schedule D line 12: box 9a as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableK1065Box9aNetLongTermCapitalGain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. Complete-safe, signed and unfloored for the reason its short-term twin gives: box 9a is captioned "Net long-term capital gain (loss)" and Schedule D line 12 reads "Net long-term gain or (loss)". The Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) twin is box 8a, and this module reads the same leaf for it because scheduleE records both entity types on the one /formK1s collection.
NOT THE SAME MONEY AS ITS SIBLINGS 9b AND 9c. Box 9a is the whole long-term net; boxes 9b and 9c are RATE CHARACTERISATIONS of amounts already inside it, which is why they feed the two worksheets rather than the face line and why ../collectiblesGainForScheduleD and ../unrecapturedSection1250GainForScheduleD are separate facts landing on separate lines.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1 answers box 9a
Fact.Description: True when THIS /formK1s item answered box 9a, the net long-term capital gain (loss). An IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../longTermCapitalGainForScheduleD. Counted by /longTermGainFromK1RowsAnswered, which decides whether Schedule D line 12 is derived from the rows or falls back to the attested total /writableScheduleDLine12NetLongTermFromScheduleK1.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's net long-term capital gain
Fact.Description: This Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) item's contribution to Schedule D line 12: box 4a as scheduleE recorded it (scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/writableBox4aNetLongTermCapitalGain), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. Complete-safe, the twin of /formK1s/*/longTermCapitalGainForScheduleD. Box 4a is the whole long-term net; its siblings 4b (28% rate gain) and 4c (unrecaptured section 1250 gain) characterise amounts inside it and land on the two worksheets through their own Y1 facts, so nothing here double counts them.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1 answers box 4a
Fact.Description: True when THIS /form1041K1s item answered box 4a, the net long-term capital gain. An IsComplete on the RAW scheduleE leaf, never on the complete-safe bridge ../longTermCapitalGainForScheduleD. Counted by /longTermGainFromK1RowsAnswered.

Fact.Name: A recorded Schedule K-1 answers its net short-term capital gain box
Fact.Description:
True when at least one recorded Schedule K-1 answered the box that prints on Schedule D line 5: box 8 on a /formK1s partnership or S corporation K-1, or box 3 on a /form1041K1s estate or trust K-1. It is the "was the source answered" predicate that lets /scheduleDLine5NetShortTermFromScheduleK1 prefer the recorded rows and keep the attested total /writableScheduleDLine5NetShortTermFromScheduleK1 as its fallback.
DOUBLE-GUARDED for the reason /collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered states at length: the inner test is a Count over per-item IsComplete flags on the RAW scheduleE leaves, and the outer test is an IsComplete on the COLLECTION ROOT, because a Count over a collection the return never opened does not resolve Complete and this fact would then make the printed line Incomplete by contagion on every return in the corpus. Each collection needs its own guard, defaulting to false.
THIS BOX ONLY, and deliberately so: a filer who records box 9a and attests the line 5 total keeps the attestation.

Fact.Name: A recorded Schedule K-1 answers its net long-term capital gain box
Fact.Description: True when at least one recorded Schedule K-1 answered the box that prints on Schedule D line 12: box 9a on a /formK1s partnership or S corporation K-1, or box 4a on a /form1041K1s estate or trust K-1. The long-term twin of /shortTermGainFromK1RowsAnswered, double-guarded for the same reason, and the predicate behind /scheduleDLine12NetLongTermFromScheduleK1.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 5 as printed - net short-term gain or (loss) from Schedule(s) K-1
Fact.Description:
Schedule D line 5, "Net short-term gain or (loss) from partnerships, S corporations, estates, and trusts from Schedule(s) K-1": the sum of the recorded K-1 rows' box 8 (partnership or S corporation) and box 3 (estate or trust) amounts when /shortTermGainFromK1RowsAnswered says at least one row answered that box, and the attested total /writableScheduleDLine5NetShortTermFromScheduleK1 otherwise. This is the fact the register should print on line 5; the attestation is its FALLBACK arm, not a second addend, because the rows and the attested total are the same money.
A PRINT COMPONENT AND NOTHING ELSE. Line 5 is already inside the collapsed short-term intake /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss - /nonForm8949ShortTermRemainder names it in so many words as "line 5 (the K-1 short-term net)" - so this fact may not be wired into /netShortTermGainOrLoss or /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover, and the Export above records that it is deliberately unconsumed rather than merely unwired. Signed, with no floor: a K-1 short-term loss is a negative entry on this line.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 12 as printed - net long-term gain or (loss) from Schedule(s) K-1
Fact.Description:
Schedule D line 12, "Net long-term gain or (loss) from partnerships, S corporations, estates, and trusts from Schedule(s) K-1": the sum of the recorded K-1 rows' box 9a (partnership or S corporation) and box 4a (estate or trust) amounts when /longTermGainFromK1RowsAnswered says at least one row answered that box, and the attested total /writableScheduleDLine12NetLongTermFromScheduleK1 otherwise. This is the fact the register should print on line 12; the attestation is its FALLBACK arm, not a second addend.
A PRINT COMPONENT AND NOTHING ELSE, exactly as its short-term twin /scheduleDLine5NetShortTermFromScheduleK1 is: /netLongTermGainOrLoss is titled "Schedule D lines 8a, 8b, 9, 10 and 12", so line 12 is already inside the collapsed long-term intake and wiring this fact into that total, or into /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover, would double count. Signed, with no floor.

Fact.Name: The transactions printed as Form 8949 Part II rows 1 through 11
Fact.Description: The long-term view of /form8949Transactions, in the collection's order: the items Part II prints, filtered on ../isLongTerm. It is the Part I filter's mirror, and it exists for the same reason: the printed Part II rows do NOT quantify over the unfiltered collection, so an index into /form8949Transactions would print a short-term transaction into a long-term row. dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv declares the axis (IRS8949 /form8949LongTermTransactions rows 11) that the Part II row tokens need. This is a print-shaped view and moves no dollar: /form8949LongTermNet keeps summing ../longTermGainOrLoss over the whole collection exactly as it does today.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 Part I line 2, column (g) - the short-term total
Fact.Description: The sum of every short-term transaction's column (g). $0 when the collection is unanswered or empty (the IsComplete guard on /form8949Transactions, the /form8949ShortTermNet idiom, because a CollectionSize or CollectionSum over an unanswered collection does not resolve). Rounded once here rather than per item, exactly as the two nets are. The sum is signed, because a column (g) adjustment is signed and the form says so: "subtract negative amounts". Line 2 adds columns (d), (e), (g) and (h); the module shipped only the column (h) total, so this is the column (g) half of the same line.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 Part I line 2, column (e) - the short-term total
Fact.Description: The sum of every short-term transaction's column (e). $0 when the collection is unanswered or empty (the IsComplete guard on /form8949Transactions, the /form8949ShortTermNet idiom, because a CollectionSize or CollectionSum over an unanswered collection does not resolve). Rounded once here rather than per item, exactly as the two nets are. Line 2 adds columns (d), (e), (g) and (h); the module shipped only the column (h) total, so this is the column (e) half of the same line.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 Part I line 2, column (d) - the short-term total
Fact.Description: The sum of every short-term transaction's column (d). $0 when the collection is unanswered or empty (the IsComplete guard on /form8949Transactions, the /form8949ShortTermNet idiom, because a CollectionSize or CollectionSum over an unanswered collection does not resolve). Rounded once here rather than per item, exactly as the two nets are. Line 2 adds columns (d), (e), (g) and (h); the module shipped only the column (h) total, so this is the column (d) half of the same line.

Fact.Name: The transactions printed as Form 8949 Part I rows 1 through 11
Fact.Description: The short-term view of /form8949Transactions, in the collection's order: the items Part I prints, filtered on ../isShortTerm. The printed Part I rows do NOT quantify over the unfiltered collection. dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv records Form 8949 as one of the four axes the register got wrong before that file existed, precisely because one unfiltered collection was printed into both Part I and Part II; an index into /form8949Transactions would print a long-term transaction into a short-term row. Part II gets the mirror filter when page 2 is swept. This is a print-shaped view and moves no dollar: /form8949ShortTermNet keeps summing ../shortTermGainOrLoss over the whole collection exactly as it does today.

Fact.Name: Basis was not reported to the IRS
Fact.Description: The Box B and Box H side of ../basisReportedToIrs: TRUE exactly when the information return did not show basis reported to the IRS. It exists because the box predicates are built with All over Bool paths and cannot negate inline.

Fact.Name: Basis was reported to the IRS, complete safe
Fact.Description: = ../writableBasisReportedToIrs when answered, else FALSE. A transaction the taxpayer never classified defaults to FALSE, which is the reporting adverse default: with no broker report and no basis reported to the IRS the transaction lands in Box C, the box that requires the taxpayer to report every column of detail rather than aggregate. This mirrors ../isLongTerm, which already defaults its own unanswered writable to FALSE so that no item falls out of both parts. A complete safe value matters here because this leaf ends up inside a Filter predicate: an incomplete predicate would make the box Bool that counts the filtered items incomplete, and the checkbox would print nothing rather than print false.

Fact.Name: This transaction is a Form 8949 Part II Box D transaction
Fact.Description: TRUE when all three parts of the Box D caption hold for this item: it is long-term (../isLongTerm), it was reported on a Form 1099-B (../reportedOnForm1099B), and the basis was reported to the IRS (../basisReportedToIrs). The long-term test is folded in here rather than taken from /form8949LongTermTransactions so that the return-level Box D fact can quantify over the writable collection and keep its IsComplete guard on a collection the graph can answer. Every operand is complete-safe, so this flag is too.

Fact.Name: This is a digital asset transaction, complete safe
Fact.Description: = ../writableIsDigitalAsset when answered, else FALSE. A transaction the taxpayer never classified defaults to FALSE, which is the reporting adverse default: with no broker report and no basis reported to the IRS the transaction lands in Box C, the box that requires the taxpayer to report every column of detail rather than aggregate. This mirrors ../isLongTerm, which already defaults its own unanswered writable to FALSE so that no item falls out of both parts. Fact.Name: This transaction belongs in Form 8949 Part I Box A
Fact.Description: TRUE exactly when the transaction is short-term, reported on a Form 1099-B, and the broker reported basis to the IRS, which is what the form's Box A label says. ../isShortTerm is one of the conjuncts on purpose: the six boxes partition the Part I population, so a long-term transaction of the same broker reporting shape must not satisfy this predicate. The holding-period conjunct is completeness-guarded: an unanswered ../isLongTerm leaves this predicate Incomplete until the row is classified. The six predicates are mutually exclusive whenever the intakes are answered consistently, that is whenever a transaction arrives on at most one of Form 1099-B and Form 1099-DA.

Fact.Name: This transaction belongs in Form 8949 Part I Box B
Fact.Description: TRUE exactly when the transaction is short-term, reported on a Form 1099-B, and the broker did not report basis to the IRS, which is what the form's Box B label says. ../isShortTerm is one of the conjuncts on purpose: the six boxes partition the Part I population, so a long-term transaction of the same broker reporting shape must not satisfy this predicate. The holding-period conjunct is completeness-guarded: an unanswered ../isLongTerm leaves this predicate Incomplete until the row is classified. The six predicates are mutually exclusive whenever the intakes are answered consistently, that is whenever a transaction arrives on at most one of Form 1099-B and Form 1099-DA.

Fact.Name: This transaction belongs in Form 8949 Part I Box C
Fact.Description: TRUE exactly when the transaction is short-term, not a digital asset transaction, and reported to the taxpayer on neither a Form 1099-B nor a Form 1099-DA, which is what the form's Box C label says. ../isShortTerm is one of the conjuncts on purpose: the six boxes partition the Part I population, so a long-term transaction of the same broker reporting shape must not satisfy this predicate. Fact.Name: This transaction belongs in Form 8949 Part I Box I
Fact.Description: TRUE exactly when the transaction is short-term, a digital asset transaction, and reported to the taxpayer on neither a Form 1099-DA nor a Form 1099-B, which is what the form's Box I label says. ../isShortTerm is one of the conjuncts on purpose: the six boxes partition the Part I population, so a long-term transaction of the same broker reporting shape must not satisfy this predicate. Fact.Name: This is not a digital asset transaction
Fact.Description: The Box C side of ../isDigitalAsset, the form's own "other than digital asset transactions". It exists because the box predicates are built with All over Bool paths and cannot negate inline.

Fact.Name: This transaction belongs on Form 8949 Part I (short-term)
Fact.Description: The Part I side of ../isLongTerm: TRUE exactly when the transaction is short-term. The holding-period answer is intentionally completeness-sensitive: an unanswered ../isLongTerm leaves this fact Incomplete rather than silently assigning the row to Part I. It exists to be the Filter predicate of /form8949ShortTermTransactions, the collection the Part I printed rows quantify over.

Fact.Name: Not reported on a Form 1099-B
Fact.Description: The Box C and Box I side of ../reportedOnForm1099B: TRUE exactly when no Form 1099-B reported this transaction. It exists because the box predicates are built with All over Bool paths and cannot negate inline.

Fact.Name: Not reported on a Form 1099-DA
Fact.Description: The Box C and Box I side of ../reportedOnForm1099DA: TRUE exactly when no Form 1099-DA reported this transaction. It exists because the box predicates are built with All over Bool paths and cannot negate inline.

Fact.Name: Reported on a Form 1099-B, complete safe
Fact.Description: = ../writableReportedOnForm1099B when answered, else FALSE. A transaction the taxpayer never classified defaults to FALSE, which is the reporting adverse default: with no broker report and no basis reported to the IRS the transaction lands in Box C, the box that requires the taxpayer to report every column of detail rather than aggregate.
