Fact.Name: This transaction's contribution to the Part I line 2 column (g) total
Fact.Description: ../adjustmentAmount when the item is short-term, else $0. The column (g) twin of the module's existing ../shortTermGainOrLoss: the two parts of Form 8949 are two different pages and IRC 1222 makes them two different numbers, so a long-term item contributes nothing to a Part I column total. Reads the complete-safe ../adjustmentAmount, not the writable, so a half-entered item contributes a computable $0 rather than making the whole column total unresolvable.

Fact.Name: This transaction's contribution to the Part I line 2 column (e) total
Fact.Description: ../costBasis when the item is short-term, else $0. The column (e) twin of the module's existing ../shortTermGainOrLoss: the two parts of Form 8949 are two different pages and IRC 1222 makes them two different numbers, so a long-term item contributes nothing to a Part I column total. Reads the complete-safe ../costBasis, not the writable, so a half-entered item contributes a computable $0 rather than making the whole column total unresolvable.

Fact.Name: This transaction's contribution to the Part I line 2 column (d) total
Fact.Description: ../proceeds when the item is short-term, else $0. The column (d) twin of the module's existing ../shortTermGainOrLoss: the two parts of Form 8949 are two different pages and IRC 1222 makes them two different numbers, so a long-term item contributes nothing to a Part I column total. Reads the complete-safe ../proceeds, not the writable, so a half-entered item contributes a computable $0. This carries a completeness guard on ../isLongTerm: an unclassified holding period leaves this contribution Incomplete instead of selecting the short-term fallback.

Fact.Name: The broker reported this transaction's basis to the IRS, writable
Fact.Description: Did the information return show that basis, usually cost, was reported to the IRS? This is the second axis of the Part I box sort: Box A and Box G are the basis reported cases, Box B and Box H the basis not reported cases. The graph has the taxpayer's own ../writableCostBasis but no record of what the broker told the IRS, and the two are not the same question. IRC 6045 (returns of brokers), the section that actually creates the Form 1099-B and Form 1099-DA reporting this box turns on, is not vendored under sources/, so this fact is anchored to the holding period section the Part I split rests on, exactly as the round 8 author anchored the Part I column intakes to IRC 1222 and IRC 1221. Form 1099-B box 12 (Check if basis reported to IRS).

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (a) — description of property, writable
Fact.Description: Column (a), the free text that identifies the asset sold; the form prints its own example, "100 sh. XYZ Co.". /form8949Transactions today carries the dollars (proceeds, basis, adjustment) and the holding-period flag but nothing that names the property, so a Part I row cannot be filled from the graph. Print-only until dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv declares the row `IRS8949 /form8949ShortTermTransactions rows 11`, which is what an indexed row token needs. Form 1099-B box 1a (Description of property).

Fact.Name: This transaction is a digital asset transaction, writable
Fact.Description: Is the property sold a digital asset? This is the only thing separating Box C from Box I: both are short-term transactions reported on neither Form 1099-B nor Form 1099-DA, and the form splits them on "other than digital asset transactions" (Box C, line 26) versus "digital asset transactions" (Box I, line 29). /disposedDigitalAssets is a return level Form 1040 attestation in a different module and says nothing about which transaction is which, so the flag has to live on the item.

Fact.Name: This transaction was reported on a Form 1099-B, writable
Fact.Description: Did the broker report this sale on a Form 1099-B or a substitute statement carrying the same information? Form 8949 tells the filer to settle this before checking any box: "Before you check Box A, B, C, G, H, or I below, see whether you received any Form(s) 1099-B, Form(s) 1099-DA, or substitute statement(s) from your broker." /form8949Transactions carries the dollars, the adjustment codes and the holding period flag, but nothing about how the transaction was reported, so Box A versus B versus C cannot be decided from the graph today. IRC 6045 (returns of brokers), the section that actually creates the Form 1099-B and Form 1099-DA reporting this box turns on, is not vendored under sources/, so this fact is anchored to the holding period section the Part I split rests on, exactly as the round 8 author anchored the Part I column intakes to IRC 1222 and IRC 1221.

Fact.Name: This transaction was reported on a Form 1099-DA, writable
Fact.Description: Did the broker report this digital asset sale on a Form 1099-DA or a substitute statement? The 1099-DA boxes (G, H and I) are the digital asset twins of the 1099-B boxes (A, B and C), and the form asks the filer to check for both information returns before choosing a box. Not in the graph in any form. IRC 6045 (returns of brokers), the section that actually creates the Form 1099-B and Form 1099-DA reporting this box turns on, is not vendored under sources/, so this fact is anchored to the holding period section the Part I split rests on, exactly as the round 8 author anchored the Part I column intakes to IRC 1222 and IRC 1221.

Fact.Name: The $0 a long-term transaction contributes to a Form 8949 Part I column total
Fact.Description: The named $0 constant the three Part I column contributions below select when an item is long-term. The supported templates have no zero literal inline in a Switch arm, so each module declares its own, as scheduleE does with /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor and form8960 with /form8960ZeroDollarFloor. Structural: it encodes the Part I / Part II split of a printed column, not a statutory dollar amount.

Fact.Name: At least one transaction belongs in Form 8949 Part I Box A
Fact.Description: The Part I Box A checkbox: TRUE when at least one transaction in /form8949Transactions is short-term, reported on a Form 1099-B, and the broker reported basis to the IRS. The Filter runs over the whole /form8949Transactions collection rather than over the staged /form8949ShortTermTransactions because a Filter predicate leaf resolves only through a collection the manifest already knows, and the short-term filter is itself a staged candidate; the difference is cosmetic, because /form8949Transactions/*/isForm8949BoxA already conjoins ../isShortTerm, so the two filters select the same items. The register renders exactly one page 1 copy of IRS8949, gated on /hasForm8949Transactions, so several of the six box Bools can be true at once while only one sheet prints; the multi copy per box render shape is carried as an obligation of kind gate on /hasForm8949Transactions.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 Part II, Box D is checked
Fact.Description: TRUE when /form8949Transactions is complete and at least one item is a Box D transaction: long-term, reported on Form 1099-B, basis reported to the IRS. The IsComplete guarded CollectionSize(Filter(...)) > 0 shape /hasForm8949Transactions already uses, so a return that never opens a Form 8949 section leaves the box blank rather than unresolvable. PRINT-ONLY UNTIL the graph grows the per box letter collections: the form says to check only one box and to file a separate page 2 for each letter that applies, and this configuration renders one page 2, so a return whose long-term items span D and E would check both. The obligation records that debt.

The Filter runs over the whole /form8949Transactions collection rather than over the staged /form8949ShortTermTransactions because a Filter predicate leaf resolves only through a collection the manifest already knows, and the short-term filter is itself a staged candidate; the difference is cosmetic, because /form8949Transactions/*/isForm8949BoxI already conjoins ../isShortTerm, so the two filters select the same items. Fact.Name: At least one Form 8949 transaction on this return is flagged as a digital asset
Fact.Description:
TRUE when /form8949Transactions is complete and at least one item carries ../isDigitalAsset. It is the DISPOSAL-side evidence that a "yes" to limb (b) of the Form 1040 digital-asset question has something behind it, read by income:/digitalAssetDispositionsAccountedFor and, through it, by the narrowed knockout income:/knockoutDigitalAssetYesWithNothingReported that replaced Not(income:/notDigitalAssets) in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut.
IT IS NOT A BOX FACT AND MUST NOT BE CONFUSED WITH ONE. The six shipping box Bools each conjoin a term/reporting shape as well: /hasForm8949BoxITransactions is short-term AND digital AND on neither information return, /hasForm8949BoxGTransactions and /hasForm8949BoxHTransactions are the two Form 1099-DA shapes, and Part II has the same three in J, K and L. A digital-asset transaction can therefore sit in any of six boxes, and an Any over the six box Bools would be a re-derivation of the flag rather than a reading of it. This Filter runs on ../isDigitalAsset itself, one term, so the answer is the same whatever box the item lands in and whether it is short-term or long-term.
SHAPE: the IsComplete-guarded CollectionSize(Filter(...)) greater than zero idiom /hasForm8949Transactions and the twelve box Bools already use, so a return that never opened a Form 8949 section resolves this Complete FALSE rather than leaving it unresolvable. That completeness is load-bearing: the knockout that reads it negates it, and an Incomplete leg there would make the whole refusal Incomplete on a return the flow calls complete. The Filter runs over the whole /form8949Transactions collection because a Filter predicate leaf resolves only through a collection the manifest already knows, the reason every box Bool gives.
MOVES NO DOLLAR AND PRINTS ON NOTHING: it is a filing gate only.

Fact.Name: This transaction belongs in Form 8949 Part II Box E
Fact.Description: TRUE exactly when the transaction is long-term, reported on a Form 1099-B, and the broker did not report basis to the IRS, which is what the form's Box E label says. ../isLongTerm is one of the conjuncts on purpose: the six Part II boxes partition the long-term population, so a short-term transaction of the same broker reporting shape must not satisfy this predicate. It is the Part II twin of the shipped Part I predicate /form8949Transactions/*/isForm8949BoxB. The holding-period conjunct is completeness-guarded: an unanswered ../isLongTerm leaves this predicate Incomplete until the row is classified. The six Part II predicates are mutually exclusive whenever the intakes are answered consistently, that is whenever a transaction arrives on at most one of Form 1099-B and Form 1099-DA.

Fact.Name: This transaction is reported on a Form 8949 with Box A or Box G checked

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 4
Fact.Description:
Schedule D line 4, the printed Part I other-forms line: the Form 4684 short-term casualty gain (form4684:/netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD) and the Form 8621 short-term capital component (form8621:/form8621ShortTermLoss, the short-term half of the section 1291 and section 1296 dispositions, negative when it is a loss). It is the short-term twin of /scheduleDLine11GainFromForm4797AndOtherForms and, unlike that print-only fact, it IS the term /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover sums. The printed cell is /scheduleDLine4ShortTermGainFromOtherFormsForPrint, which adds the filer's Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 remainder to these legs.
WHERE THE FORM 8621 AMOUNT PRINTS IS AN INTERPRETATION, and it is recorded here rather than assumed. The 2025 Instructions for Form 8621 send the capital component to "the Schedule D used for your tax return" and warn that "Portions of the net capital gain may have to be reported on different lines of Schedule D" without naming one; the 2025 Instructions for Schedule D name no PFIC line at all. This dictionary prints it on the Part I other-forms line because that is the only Part I cell that is not a Form 8949 total, a shortcut row, a Schedule K-1 row or the carryover, and because the long-term half already prints on the Part II other-forms line 11 for the same reason. The Forms 6252, 4684, 6781 and 8824 the printed caption lists are not exhaustive of what reaches the cell.
The Form 6252, 6781 and 8824 short-term legs the caption also names reach line 7 through the collapsed intake /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss and reach the printed cell through /writableScheduleDLine4OtherShortTermGains, never through this fact, so this fact carries two terms; both are complete-safe $0 on a return that opens neither form.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 4 as printed
Fact.Description:
Schedule D line 4 as it prints: the computed legs /scheduleDLine4ShortTermGainFromOtherForms (the Form 4684 short-term casualty gain and the Form 8621 short-term capital component) plus /scheduleDLine4OtherShortTermGainsOrZero, the Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 short-term remainder the filer supplies. The printed caption names all of them: "Short-term gain from Form 6252 and short-term gain or (loss) from Forms 4684, 6781, and 8824".
A PRINT COMPONENT AND NOTHING ELSE, the short-term twin of /scheduleDLine11GainFromForm4797AndOtherForms. Line 7 already reaches the Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 amounts through the collapsed intake /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss (on a return that itemises Form 8949 rows, through its remainder alias /nonForm8949ShortTermRemainder), so this fact is not wired into /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover; that total keeps reading the computed legs alone, and the Export records that this fact is deliberately unconsumed. Signed, with no floor: Forms 6781 and 8824 can produce a loss. ONE Round on the whole cell: the printed line is whole dollars and its legs are added with their cents first (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 9).

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 4 gains from Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete-safe wrapper of /writableScheduleDLine4OtherShortTermGains: the filer's entry when they made one, and 0 when they did not. It exists so the printed line 4 resolves on a return that answers none of these forms rather than staying Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 4 gains from Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824, filer entry
Fact.Description:
The part of Schedule D line 4 no fact in this dictionary computes: the short-term gain from Form 6252 (installment sale income), and the short-term gain or loss from Form 6781 (section 1256 contracts and straddles) and Form 8824 (like-kind exchanges). The other two legs of the printed line, the Form 4684 short-term casualty gain and the Form 8621 short-term capital component, DO have facts and are added beside this one on the printed line. No minimum of zero: Forms 6781 and 8824 can produce a loss.
This entry is print-only: line 7 reaches Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 through the collapsed /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss, so the same amounts belong in that figure as well, and this entry only puts them on the printed line 4 so Part I foots on the page. The Form 4684 and Form 8621 amounts are NOT entered here; they print on line 4 from their own facts. FORM 6252 AND FORM 8824 (2026-09-27): a Form 6252 sale or Form 8824 exchange entered on this return is carried to Schedule D line 4 or 11 by /scheduleDForm6252And8824ShortTermGainOrLoss and /scheduleDForm6252And8824LongTermGainOrLoss; do not include it here as well.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 11
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 11, the printed line: the Form 4797 Part I gain (form4797 /section1231LtcgPortion), the Form 4684 long-term casualty gain (form4684 /netLongTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD), the Form 2439 box 1a total over the notices included in this return (form2439 /form2439ScheduleDLine11LongTermCapitalGainOrZero) and the Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 legs the filer supplies. The Form 2439 leg is REAL in both places: /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover adds the same module fact to its line-15 minuend, and the collapsed intake /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss no longer carries box 1a (its Description says so), so box 1a is entered once, prints here once and reaches line 15 once. The Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 remainder in /scheduleDLine11OtherLongTermGainsOrZero stays PRINT ONLY, for the reason that applied to the whole line before this unit: line 15 still reaches those three forms through the collapsed intake, so promoting the remainder into the line 15 sum without removing that leg would double count. Plus the Form 8621 long-term capital component (form8621:/form8621LongTermGain): the QEF net capital gain of Form 8621 line 7c and the long-term half of the section 1291 and section 1296 dispositions. The 2025 Instructions for Form 8621 send line 7c to "the Schedule D used for your tax return" without naming a line and warn that portions may belong on different lines, so the Part II other-forms line is where this dictionary prints it. Unlike the Form 4797 and Form 4684 legs above, this one is NOT double counted by line 15: /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover adds form8621:/form8621LongTermGain itself and does not read this fact, so the printed cell and the printed total carry the amount exactly once each. ONE Round on the whole cell: the printed line is whole dollars and its legs are added with their cents first (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 9).

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 11 gains from Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824, complete safe
Fact.Description: The complete-safe wrapper of /writableScheduleDLine11OtherLongTermGains (Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824; the Form 2439 leg is form2439:/form2439ScheduleDLine11LongTermCapitalGainOrZero): the filer's entry when they made one, and 0 when they did not. It exists so the line 11 sum resolves on a return that answers none of these forms rather than staying Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 15 is a gain
Fact.Description: TRUE when Schedule D line 15, the net long-term capital gain or loss after the carryover, is more than zero. Strictly more than zero: a zero is not a gain, which is the reading /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet already records for the same phrase. Half of the printed line 17 question.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 16 is a gain
Fact.Description: TRUE when Schedule D line 16, lines 7 and 15 combined, is more than zero. Strictly more than zero, the same reading as its line 15 twin. The other half of the printed line 17 question, and the test the page 2 bullets under line 16 use to route the return.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 17 Yes: lines 15 and 16 are both gains
Fact.Description: The printed line 17 Yes box: lines 15 and 16 are both gains, so the return goes to line 18. It is the conjunction the printed question asks, and it is the same pair of comparisons /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet already conjoins with its line 18 and line 19 disjunction, now named on its own because line 17 prints it.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 17 No: lines 15 and 16 are not both gains
Fact.Description: The printed line 17 No box, the negation of /scheduleDLine17BothGains: the return skips lines 18 through 21 and goes to line 22.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1b, column (g), Adjustments to gain or loss from Form(s) 8949
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 1b, column (g), Adjustments to gain or loss from Form(s) 8949: the sum of that Form 8949 column over the transactions whose box is A or G (short-term). The IsComplete guard is on /form8949Transactions, the answerable collection, exactly as the module's existing Form 8949 column totals guard theirs, so a return that never opened a Form 8949 section resolves 0 rather than staying unresolvable. Rounded once on the total rather than per item, as those totals are.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 20 Yes: complete the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet
Fact.Description: The printed line 20 Yes box: the return reached line 20 because line 17 was Yes, and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet entry test is not met, so the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet figures Form 1040 line 16. Fact.Name: Disposed of an investment in a qualified opportunity fund, filer entry
Fact.Description: Schedule D page 1, the unnumbered question above Part I: did the filer dispose of any investment in a qualified opportunity fund during the tax year? A "Yes" here is what leads to /writableQofIncludibleGainShortTerm and /writableQofIncludibleGainLongTerm — this dictionary does not carry a qualified opportunity fund investment collection (Form 8997 Parts I and IV, the year-over-year QOF holdings, are multi-year state and remain unmodeled), only the current-year deferral and inclusion TOTALS a disposition or a new investment produces. /hasForm8949Transactions is the narrower question of whether a Form 8949 attaches at all, and a filer can attach Form 8949 for ordinary stock sales while holding no fund interest, so it cannot answer this box.

Fact.Name: Short-term capital gain deferred this year by investing in a QOF (Form 8949 code Z, short-term)
Fact.Description: The total SHORT-TERM eligible gain the filer elects to defer this year under IRC 1400Z-2(a)(1)(A) by investing in a qualified opportunity fund within the 180-day window, to the extent of the amount invested. On the printed Form 8949, the ORIGINAL sale that produced this gain is reported at its FULL, undiminished amount on its own row ("do not make any adjustments for the deferral in column (g)" on that row); the deferral itself is reported on a SEPARATE row with code "Z" in column (f) and this amount, negative, in column (g) — which is exactly what this fact's placement in /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend does: it does not touch the original sale's figure, it subtracts the deferred portion once, on its own line, matching the code-Z row's net effect on Schedule D line 7. THE CODE-Z ROW ITSELF IS NOT ALSO A /form8949Transactions ITEM: entering one there as well (proceeds/basis blank, this amount negative in column (g)) double-counts the deferral, because that collection's column (g) already reaches this line through /form8949ShortTermNet. This is also Form 8997 Part II, row 2, column (e) — "Amount of short-term deferred gain" — the aggregate this graph reads rather than modeling the underlying per-QOF-investment collection (Form 8997 Parts I-IV) that produces it. No maximum: the statute caps the excludible amount at the amount invested, which this attestation is trusted to already reflect, the same posture the module takes for every other worksheet-scalar attestation. Min $0, on the statute's own "gain... does not exceed" framing — there is no excess-deferral concept, only a smaller deferral. Unanswered is complete-safe $0, so a return that never elects a QOF deferral is value-identical to one before this fact existed.

Fact.Name: Short-term QOF deferred gain (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /qofInvestmentsDeferredGainShortTerm when the return lists its QOF investments one by one, else /writableQofDeferredGainShortTerm when answered, else $0. THE LIST GOVERNS when it exists: a return that enters its code-Z rows and leaves the return-level scalar blank would otherwise defer nothing at all. A scalar that is answered and disagrees with a non-empty list is refused, not resolved - see /knockoutQofDeferralScalarDisagreesWithInvestmentList. When the scalar fallback is used, its declared Min $0 is enforced explicitly because XML limits are not resolution floors. The recorded-investment arm remains authoritative.

Fact.Name: Long-term capital gain deferred this year by investing in a QOF (Form 8949 code Z, long-term)
Fact.Description: The long-term twin of /writableQofDeferredGainShortTerm: the total LONG-TERM eligible gain deferred this year under IRC 1400Z2(a)(1)(A). Enters /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend as a subtrahend the same way, and is Form 8997 Part II, row 2, column (f). The code-Z row itself is NOT ALSO a /form8949Transactions item — see the short-term twin's Description. Min $0; unanswered is complete-safe $0.

Fact.Name: Long-term QOF deferred gain (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /qofInvestmentsDeferredGainLongTerm when the return lists its QOF investments one by one, else /writableQofDeferredGainLongTerm when answered, else $0. THE LIST GOVERNS when it exists: a return that enters its code-Z rows and leaves the return-level scalar blank would otherwise defer nothing at all. A scalar that is answered and disagrees with a non-empty list is refused, not resolved - see /knockoutQofDeferralScalarDisagreesWithInvestmentList.

Fact.Name: Previously deferred short-term QOF gain now includible (Form 8949 code Y, short-term)
Fact.Description: The total SHORT-TERM previously-deferred gain that becomes includible this year because an inclusion event occurred — the QOF investment was sold, exchanged, or otherwise disposed of (IRC 1400Z2(b)(1)(A)), which for a TY2025 individual return is the only inclusion trigger this graph models; the statute's other trigger, the December 31, 2026 mandatory-inclusion date, cannot occur within TY2025. On the printed Form 8949, the QOF investment's own current-year sale is reported on its own row (columns (b) through (e) completed normally); the previously-deferred amount becoming includible is reported as a POSITIVE code-"Y" adjustment in column (g) of that same row — an ADDITION distinct from whatever gain or loss the QOF investment's own current-year sale itself produced, which is why this fact is an ADDEND at /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend rather than a substitute for the sale's own figure. THE PREVIOUSLY-DEFERRED AMOUNT ITSELF IS NOT ENTERED IN /form8949Transactions: if the QOF investment's own current-year sale is entered there (proceeds/basis/dates as an ordinary item, column (g) LEFT BLANK), that collection reaches this line through /form8949ShortTermNet already — only the code-Y ADJUSTMENT belongs on this writable, never in that item's own adjustmentAmount, or the inclusion counts twice. This is also Form 8997 Part III, row 2, column (e) — "Amount of previously deferred short-term gain now included in taxable income." The amount includible is capped by IRC 1400Z2(b)(2)(A) at the excess of the lesser of (the deferred gain or the investment's fair market value at inclusion) over the taxpayer's basis in the investment — a computation this graph does not perform (it would require tracking the investment's own basis, including the 5-year/7-year holding-period basis step-ups Form 8997 Part III's special gain codes G/H disclose), so this is an ATTESTED total, the filer's own computed answer, not derived. No maximum for that reason. Min $0, matching the statute's own floor (paragraph (2)(A)'s excess is never negative in the ordinary case; a negative would mean no gain is includible, i.e. $0 here). Unanswered is complete-safe $0, so a return with no QOF inclusion event is value-identical to one before this fact existed.

Fact.Name: Short-term QOF includible gain (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /qofInclusionDispositionsGainShortTerm when the return lists its QOF dispositions one by one, else /writableQofIncludibleGainShortTerm when answered, else $0. The list governs when it exists; a scalar that disagrees with a non-empty list is refused by /knockoutQofInclusionScalarDisagreesWithDispositionList rather than added to it.

Fact.Name: Previously deferred long-term QOF gain now includible (Form 8949 code Y, long-term)
Fact.Description: The long-term twin of /writableQofIncludibleGainShortTerm: the total previously DEFERRED LONG-TERM gain becoming includible this year under IRC 1400Z2(b). Enters /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend as an addend the same way, and is Form 8997 Part III, row 2, column (f). The previously-deferred amount is NOT ALSO entered in /form8949Transactions — see the short-term twin's Description. Min $0; unanswered is complete-safe $0.

Fact.Name: Long-term QOF includible gain (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /qofInclusionDispositionsGainLongTerm when the return lists its QOF dispositions one by one, else /writableQofIncludibleGainLongTerm when answered, else $0. The list governs when it exists; a scalar that disagrees with a non-empty list is refused by /knockoutQofInclusionScalarDisagreesWithDispositionList rather than added to it.

Fact.Name: Qualified opportunity fund investments made this year
Fact.Description: One item per QOF investment whose eligible gain the filer elects to defer this year - which is one printed code-Z row of Form 8949 each. Investments in different funds, or in the same fund on different dates, are separate items; eligible gains of the same character invested on the same date into the same fund may be grouped into one. OPTIONAL. A return may answer the return-level deferral scalars instead and list nothing here, which is what every return before this collection did. An ABSENT or EMPTY collection is not a list: /hasQofInvestmentDetail is Complete FALSE for both, and the scalars keep Schedule D lines 7 and 15 exactly as they were.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (a) on the code-Z row - the EIN of the qualified opportunity fund
Fact.Description: The employer identification number of the fund this eligible gain was invested in. Column (a) of the code-Z row carries ONLY this number - not a description of the property, which belongs to the original sale's own row.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (b) on the code-Z row - the date invested in the fund
Fact.Description: The day the filer invested in the fund, which column (b) of the code-Z row carries. It is also what makes two investments in the same fund two rows rather than one. NOT VALIDATED HERE against the 180-day window that IRC 1400Z2(a)(1)(A) requires between the realized gain and the investment: the realization date of the deferred gain is not modelled, so the window is the filer's attestation, as it is for the amount.

Fact.Name: Is the gain deferred by this investment long-term?
Fact.Description: TRUE when the eligible gain deferred by this investment is LONG-TERM and its code-Z row goes in Part II, FALSE when it is short-term and the row goes in Part I. The instructions put the row in "Part I with box C or box I checked or Part II with box F or" box L checked "depending on whether the gain being deferred is" short or long term, and the character of the eligible gain survives the investment. NO DEFAULT. An unanswered character leaves this investment's contribution INCOMPLETE and the deferral with it: the two terms reach different Schedule D lines, and guessing one moves money on the printed return.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (g) on the code-Z row - the eligible gain deferred by this investment
Fact.Description: The eligible gain this investment defers, entered as a POSITIVE amount. It is what column (g) of the code-Z row prints as a negative number in parentheses; the sign belongs to the printed row, not to the answer. The statute caps the deferral at the amount invested in the fund, which this attestation is trusted to already reflect - the same posture the module takes for the return-level scalar. The Limit below is NOT enforced on resolution, so a mistyped negative is floored in ../qofInvestmentDeferredGainFloored instead.

Fact.Name: This investment's deferred gain, floored at zero
Fact.Description: ../writableQofInvestmentDeferredGain, never below $0. The Writable's own Limit Min is not enforced on the resolution path, and a negative deferral would be SUBTRACTED from Schedule D line 7 backwards - it would raise the net gain rather than lower it. The floor is here rather than in the total so a single mistyped row cannot move the return in either direction. INCOMPLETE while the amount is unanswered: an investment that has been started but not priced must not contribute $0.

Fact.Name: This investment's contribution to the short-term deferral
Fact.Description: ../qofInvestmentDeferredGainFloored when the deferred gain is short-term, else $0. Read through IsComplete on the character, so an unanswered Part leaves BOTH contributions incomplete rather than placing the row in Part I by default.

Fact.Name: This investment's contribution to the long-term deferral
Fact.Description: The mirror of its short-term twin, and the two are exhaustive and disjoint by construction.

Fact.Name: The return lists its QOF investments one by one
Fact.Description: TRUE when /qofInvestments is answered and holds at least one item. FALSE for an UNANSWERED collection and FALSE for an ANSWERED EMPTY one - the two are different states of the graph and the same answer here, because neither is a list of investments. The IsComplete guard is what buys the Complete FALSE: a bare CollectionSize over an unanswered collection does not resolve.

Fact.Name: Short-term QOF deferral, totalled from the investment list
Fact.Description: The sum of the short-term contributions of every listed investment, $0 when the return lists none. INCOMPLETE when a listed investment has no amount or no character - the list is then a half-answered list, and a half-answered list must not resolve to a number that reaches Schedule D line 7.

Fact.Name: Long-term QOF deferral, totalled from the investment list
Fact.Description: The long-term twin of /qofInvestmentsDeferredGainShortTerm.

Fact.Name: Refusal: a return-level QOF deferral scalar disagrees with the investment list
Fact.Description: The return lists at least one QOF investment AND an answered return-level deferral scalar does not equal its total from that list. The list governs both Schedule D legs whenever it is non-empty, so a scalar is never added - but a scalar that disagrees with the list means one of the two entries is wrong and this dictionary cannot tell which, so the return is refused rather than filed on the list alone. A scalar equal to its list total is harmless. Complete-safe FALSE with no list (the scalars then carry both legs by themselves, unchecked, exactly as before) and FALSE for an unanswered scalar; each leg is guarded IsComplete-first on its scalar, after the list test.

Fact.Name: Qualified opportunity fund dispositions with previously deferred gain included this year
Fact.Description: One item per QOF investment sold or exchanged this year whose previously deferred gain is reported on its own Form 8949 code-Y row. The EIN and sale date identify the printed row; the character follows the gain that was deferred; and the amount is the filer's attested IRC 1400Z-2(b)(2)(A) result. The collection is optional: an absent or answered-empty list leaves the return-level inclusion scalars in control.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (a) on the code-Y row — EIN of the QOF investment sold
Fact.Description: The employer identification number of the QOF investment sold or exchanged. It is the only value printed in column (a) of the code-Y row.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (c) on the code-Y row — date the QOF investment was sold
Fact.Description: The date the QOF investment was sold or exchanged, transcribed for the ordinary Form 8949 columns (b) through (e) that accompany the code-Y adjustment.

Fact.Name: Whether this code-Y QOF inclusion is long-term
Fact.Description: TRUE when the previously deferred gain belongs in Form 8949 Part II (box F or L), FALSE when it belongs in Part I (box C or I). The instructions require the recognized gain to keep the same short- or long-term character as the gain originally deferred. No default: an unanswered character cannot choose which Schedule D line receives the amount.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (g) on the code-Y row — previously deferred gain now included
Fact.Description: The positive amount of previously deferred gain the filer reports for this QOF disposition. It is the attested result of the IRC 1400Z-2(b)(2)(A) lesser-of/FMV/basis computation, including any holding-period basis step-ups; this graph does not hold the multi-year state needed to derive it. The printed code-Y row supplies the positive sign. Min $0; the floor is enforced in the derived per-item fact because a Writable Limit is not enforced during resolution.

Fact.Name: This QOF disposition's included gain, floored at zero
Fact.Description: The entered code-Y amount, never below $0. An unanswered amount remains Incomplete: a started disposition must not silently contribute zero to taxable income.

Fact.Name: This QOF disposition's short-term included gain
Fact.Description: The floored code-Y amount when the item's character is answered FALSE, else $0. An unanswered character leaves this contribution Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This QOF disposition's long-term included gain
Fact.Description: The mirror of the short-term contribution; the two are exhaustive and disjoint once the item's character is answered.

Fact.Name: The return lists QOF dispositions with code-Y inclusion amounts one by one
Fact.Description: TRUE only for an answered, non-empty /qofInclusionDispositions collection. Both an unanswered and an answered-empty collection are Complete FALSE so the legacy scalar route remains available.

Fact.Name: Short-term QOF inclusion, totalled from the disposition list
Fact.Description: The sum of each listed code-Y disposition's short-term included gain. A started item with an unanswered amount or character leaves the total Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Long-term QOF inclusion, totalled from the disposition list
Fact.Description: The long-term twin of /qofInclusionDispositionsGainShortTerm.

Fact.Name: Refusal: a QOF inclusion scalar disagrees with the disposition list
Fact.Description: When the return lists at least one QOF disposition, an answered return-level inclusion scalar that differs from the corresponding list total is contradictory. The list governs rather than adding the scalar, but this graph cannot decide which of two entries is correct, so it refuses the return. No list means Complete FALSE and the scalar route remains unchanged.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 11 gains from Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824, filer entry
Fact.Description:
The part of Schedule D line 11 no fact in this dictionary computes: the long-term gain from Form 6252 (installment sale income), and the long-term gain or loss from Form 6781 (section 1256 contracts and straddles) and Form 8824 (like-kind exchanges). The other three legs of the printed line, the Form 4797 Part I gain, the Form 4684 long-term casualty gain and the Form 2439 box 1a total, DO have facts and are added beside this one. No minimum of zero: Forms 6781 and 8824 can produce a loss.
FORM 2439 BOX 1a IS NOT ENTERED HERE. It is carried per notice by form2439:/form2439Forms and reaches this printed line and line 15 through form2439:/form2439ScheduleDLine11LongTermCapitalGainOrZero. A filer who lists a notice and also adds its box 1a to this entry prints line 11 twice over; because this entry also carries three other forms, the graph cannot check it against the notice list the way it checks the pure Form 2439 scalars (see /knockoutForm2439NoticeTotalsDisagreeWithScheduleDEntries), so the exclusion is BY CONSTRUCTION and stated to the application. This entry is print-only: line 15 reaches Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824 through the collapsed /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss, as before. FORM 6252 AND FORM 8824 (2026-09-27): a Form 6252 sale or Form 8824 exchange entered on this return is carried to Schedule D line 4 or 11 by /scheduleDForm6252And8824ShortTermGainOrLoss and /scheduleDForm6252And8824LongTermGainOrLoss; do not include it here as well.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a column (h) as a term of line 7 (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableScheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss when the filer used the line 1a shortcut row (all Form 1099-B/1099-DA transactions with basis reported, no adjustments, entered as one line instead of Form 8949), else $0. The printed line 7 is "Combine lines 1a through 6 in column (h)", so this is added at /shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend beside /netShortTermGainOrLoss. This writable, /writableScheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss, is the SOLE channel for line 1a: it must not also be entered into /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss, which by its own Description covers only lines 4 and 5. Complete-safe 0 on every return that does not use the row, which is every committed scenario. A four-way Switch: a nonzero /writableScheduleDLine1aAdjustments makes the row INCOMPLETE (the row is by definition "no adjustments"); with column (d) or (e) answered (/scheduleDLine1aComponentsStarted) the value is the COMPUTED /scheduleDLine1aComputedGainOrLoss, requiring both and requiring any entered (h) to agree after rounding, else INCOMPLETE; (h) alone is the legacy net-only channel; no row at all is $0. Still the SOLE channel to line 7 beside /netShortTermGainOrLoss.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 8a column (h) as a term of line 15 (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableScheduleDLine8aGainOrLoss when the filer used the line 8a shortcut row (all Form 1099-B/1099-DA transactions with basis reported, no adjustments, entered as one line instead of Form 8949), else $0. The printed line 15 is "Combine lines 8a through 14 in column (h)", so this is added at /longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover's minuend beside /netLongTermGainOrLoss. This writable, /writableScheduleDLine8aGainOrLoss, is the SOLE channel for line 8a: it must not also be entered into /writableNetLongTermGainOrLoss, which by its own Description covers only lines 8b, 9, 10 and 12. Complete-safe 0 on every return that does not use the row, which is every committed scenario. A four-way Switch: a nonzero /writableScheduleDLine8aAdjustments makes the row INCOMPLETE (the row is by definition "no adjustments"); with column (d) or (e) answered (/scheduleDLine8aComponentsStarted) the value is the COMPUTED /scheduleDLine8aComputedGainOrLoss, requiring both and requiring any entered (h) to agree after rounding, else INCOMPLETE; (h) alone is the legacy net-only channel; no row at all is $0. Still the SOLE channel to line 15 beside /netLongTermGainOrLoss.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a column (g), Adjustments to gain or loss from Form(s) 8949, filer entry
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 1a, column (g), Adjustments to gain or loss from Form(s) 8949: the aggregate of every short-term transaction reported on a Form 1099-B or Form 1099-DA showing basis reported to the IRS and needing no adjustment, which the filer may report here INSTEAD of listing on Form 8949. The graph's /form8949Transactions collection is by construction the transactions that ARE listed on Form 8949, so this row has no input here at all and is the filer's own entry. No minimum of zero: column (h) and column (g) can both be negative. Print-only: nothing in this dictionary computes with column (g) of this row beyond what column (h), /writableScheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss, already carries to Schedule D line 7. A filer who reports every transaction on Form 8949 leaves this row blank and goes to line 1b, which is what an unanswered intake prints. THE printed cell is SHADED (the row is by definition "no adjustments"), so this is no longer bound in the register (PERMANENT GAP); $0 or blank is harmless, a nonzero answer leaves /scheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss INCOMPLETE - the transaction belongs on Form 8949.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a column (e), Cost (or other basis), filer entry
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 1a, column (e), Cost (or other basis): the aggregate of every short-term transaction reported on a Form 1099-B or Form 1099-DA showing basis reported to the IRS and needing no adjustment, which the filer may report here INSTEAD of listing on Form 8949. The graph's /form8949Transactions collection is by construction the transactions that ARE listed on Form 8949, so this row has no input here at all and is the filer's own entry. No minimum of zero: column (h) and column (g) can both be negative. A filer who reports every transaction on Form 8949 leaves this row blank and goes to line 1b, which is what an unanswered intake prints. Answering column (d) or (e) starts the row's own arithmetic (/scheduleDLine1aComponentsStarted): both are then required and column (h) is COMPUTED as (d) minus (e), rounded once (/scheduleDLine1aComputedGainOrLoss).

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a column (h), Gain or (loss), filer entry
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 1a, column (h), Gain or (loss): the aggregate of every short-term transaction reported on a Form 1099-B or Form 1099-DA showing basis reported to the IRS and needing no adjustment, which the filer may report here INSTEAD of listing on Form 8949. The graph's /form8949Transactions collection is by construction the transactions that ARE listed on Form 8949, so this row has no input here at all and is the filer's own entry. No minimum of zero: column (h) and column (g) can both be negative. Reaches Schedule D line 7 through /scheduleDLine1aGainOrLoss, which is the SOLE channel for line 1a — this amount must NOT also be folded into /writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss (see that fact's Description), or line 7 counts it twice. A filer who reports every transaction on Form 8949 leaves this row blank and goes to line 1b, which is what an unanswered intake prints. WITH column (d)/(e) answered this is a CONSISTENCY CHECK only - it must equal the computed (h) after whole-dollar rounding and is never ADDED to it; with (d)/(e) absent it remains the legacy net-only channel to line 7. The printed (h) cell now binds /scheduleDLine1aGainOrLossForPrint.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a column (d), Proceeds (sales price), filer entry
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 1a, column (d), Proceeds (sales price): the aggregate of every short-term transaction reported on a Form 1099-B or Form 1099-DA showing basis reported to the IRS and needing no adjustment, which the filer may report here INSTEAD of listing on Form 8949. The graph's /form8949Transactions collection is by construction the transactions that ARE listed on Form 8949, so this row has no input here at all and is the filer's own entry. A filer who reports every transaction on Form 8949 leaves this row blank and goes to line 1b, which is what an unanswered intake prints. Answering column (d) or (e) starts the row's own arithmetic (/scheduleDLine1aComponentsStarted): both are then required and column (h) is COMPUTED as (d) minus (e), rounded once (/scheduleDLine1aComputedGainOrLoss).

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 8a column (g), Adjustments to gain or loss from Form(s) 8949, filer entry
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 8a, column (g), Adjustments to gain or loss from Form(s) 8949: the aggregate of every long-term transaction reported on a Form 1099-B or Form 1099-DA showing basis reported to the IRS and needing no adjustment, which the filer may report here INSTEAD of listing on Form 8949. The graph's /form8949Transactions collection is by construction the transactions that ARE listed on Form 8949, so this row has no input here at all and is the filer's own entry. No minimum of zero: column (h) and column (g) can both be negative. A filer who reports every transaction on Form 8949 leaves this row blank and goes to line 8b, which is what an unanswered intake prints. Fact.Name: Schedule D line 8a column (e), Cost (or other basis), filer entry
Fact.Description: Schedule D line 8a, column (e), Cost (or other basis): the aggregate of every long-term transaction reported on a Form 1099-B or Form 1099-DA showing basis reported to the IRS and needing no adjustment, which the filer may report here INSTEAD of listing on Form 8949. Fact.Description: Schedule D line 8a, column (d), Proceeds (sales price): the aggregate of every long-term transaction reported on a Form 1099-B or Form 1099-DA showing basis reported to the IRS and needing no adjustment, which the filer may report here INSTEAD of listing on Form 8949. Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (b) — date acquired, writable
Fact.Description: Column (b), "Date acquired (Mo., day, yr.)": the day the taxpayer acquired the property. It is the opening end of the holding period the Part I/Part II split turns on: when both this date and ../writableDateSold are answered, ../isLongTerm computes the split from them (../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates) rather than relying on the attested ../writableIsLongTerm. Left unanswered for a "VARIOUS"-dated block of stock or digital assets acquired on several dates — enter "VARIOUS" on the printed row instead of a date, per the instructions — in which case ../isLongTerm falls back to the attestation. A Day, not a String. Form 1099-B box 1b (Date acquired).

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (c) — date sold or disposed of, writable
Fact.Description: Column (c), "Date sold or disposed of (Mo., day, yr.)": the day of the disposition that realizes the column (h) gain or loss, and the closing end of the holding period. Feeds ../isLongTerm's computed split (../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates) together with ../writableDateAcquired when both are answered. A Day, not a String. Form 1099-B box 1c (Date sold or disposed).

Fact.Name: This Form 8949 transaction is an ESPP disqualifying disposition
Fact.Description: Optional filer attestation that the transaction is a disqualifying disposition of employee stock purchased through an employee stock purchase plan.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 ESPP disqualifying disposition belongs to the primary filer
Fact.Description: On a married-filing-jointly return, identify whether this employee stock purchase plan disqualifying disposition belongs to the primary filer. Leave this question unanswered on a single-filer return: the transaction is assigned to the primary filer by the filing status. ASKED WHEN: this row is an ESPP disqualifying disposition and the return is MFJ. UNANSWERED: the positive ordinary-income amount remains Incomplete rather than being silently put into either spouse's earned-income base. This is a per-transaction ownership answer, not a second ordinary-income amount; the Schedule D total and Form 8949 basis correction remain unchanged.

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income already in Form W-2 box 1 for this transaction
Fact.Description: On a return with more than one ESPP disqualifying disposition, the portion of this row's ordinary income already included in Form W-2 box 1. A single-disposition return may use the return-level income:/writableEsppDisqualifyingOrdinaryIncomeAlreadyInFormW2Box1 answer instead. ASKED WHEN: more than one disqualifying disposition is present. UNANSWERED: the per-transaction line 1h amount remains Incomplete rather than allocating one household W-2 answer to several sales. Dollar, minimum $0; the computed body caps it at this row's ordinary income.

Fact.Name: ESPP exercise-date fair market value for shares sold
Fact.Description: Fair market value at exercise for shares in this ESPP disqualifying disposition. Optional and non-negative.

Fact.Name: ESPP purchase price for shares sold
Fact.Description: Purchase price actually paid for the shares in this ESPP disposition, qualifying or disqualifying: Form 3922 box 5 (price paid per share) times the shares sold. Optional and non-negative.

Fact.Name: This Form 8949 transaction is an ESPP qualifying disposition of stock bought at a discount
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Is this sale of stock you bought through an employee stock purchase plan, sold after you met the plan's holding period (more than 2 years after the option was granted and more than 1 year after the shares were transferred to you)? Answer yes only when the option price was set below the stock's value on the grant date, which is when the corporation sends you Form 3922. ASKED WHEN: the row is a sale of employee stock purchase plan stock. A disqualifying disposition (holding period NOT met) is the sibling question ../writableEsppDisqualifyingDisposition; the two answers exclude each other, and a row answered yes to both keeps its ordinary income and column (h) Incomplete rather than picking one. UNANSWERED OR NO: the row contributes no compensation and column (g) is untouched, so every return that never answers it resolves as before. A DISPOSITION BY DEATH is outside this question: section 423(c) also taxes the discount on the decedent's final return, which this intake does not model.

Fact.Name: ESPP grant-date fair market value for the shares sold
Fact.Description: SCREEN. The value of the shares in this sale on the date the option was granted: Form 3922 box 3 (value per share on the grant date) times the number of shares sold. ASKED WHEN: ../writableEsppQualifyingDisposition is yes. Dollar, minimum $0; the consuming body floors a negative answer.

Fact.Name: ESPP option price as of the grant date for the shares sold
Fact.Description: SCREEN. The option price for the shares in this sale, measured on the grant date: Form 3922 box 8 (the exercise price per share determined as if the option had been exercised on the grant date) times the number of shares sold. When box 8 is blank the price was fixed on the grant date, and it is the box 5 price actually paid. This is NOT always the price paid: a plan that prices at a percentage of the lower of the grant-date and exercise-date values pays less than this whenever the stock fell. ASKED WHEN: ../writableEsppQualifyingDisposition is yes. Dollar, minimum $0; the consuming body floors a negative answer.

Fact.Name: ESPP qualifying disposition compensation (IRC 423(c))
Fact.Description: The compensation a qualifying disposition of discounted employee stock purchase plan stock carries: the lesser of (1) the sale value over the price paid and (2) the grant-date value over the grant-date option price, floored at $0. The sale value is this row's proceeds, column (d): Pub. 525 figures its example from the selling price and says a sale at a loss has no ordinary income, which is what the $0 floor of measure (1) gives. The price paid is ../writableEsppPurchasePriceForSharesSold, shared with the disqualifying arm. UNANSWERED OR NO: complete-safe $0. YES WITH A MISSING AMOUNT: Incomplete. YES TOGETHER WITH A YES ON ../writableEsppDisqualifyingDisposition: Incomplete, deliberately; the inner Switch has no catch-all so the contradiction runs off the end.

Fact.Name: ESPP compensation on this Form 8949 row, either arm
Fact.Description: The employee stock purchase plan compensation this row carries: the disqualifying-disposition exercise spread (../esppDisqualifyingOrdinaryIncome) plus the qualifying-disposition discount (../esppQualifyingOrdinaryIncome). At most one is nonzero on a finished row, and a row answered as both is Incomplete through the qualifying arm. This is the one per-row quantity every downstream consumer reads: the column (g) basis correction, the Form 1040 line 1h share and the per-filer split. Both arms raise basis by the amount included and both are reported as wages, so one reader serves both.

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income
Fact.Description: For an answered disqualifying disposition, the ordinary-income portion is the greater of zero and exercise-date fair market value less purchase price. An unanswered classification is complete-safe zero; an answered classification with a missing required value remains incomplete.

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income not already in Form W-2 box 1 for this transaction
Fact.Description: The portion of this transaction's ESPP ordinary income that belongs on Form 1040 line 1h. With one transaction, the existing return-level box-1 answer is the whole answer; with multiple transactions, each row must answer its own box-1 amount. The amount is floored at zero and capped at this row's ordinary income.

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income for the primary filer
Fact.Description: The ordinary-income portion of this disqualifying disposition attributed to the primary filer. A non-MFJ return assigns its own transaction to the primary filer; on MFJ, the per-transaction ownership answer decides the spouse. A positive disqualifying disposition with an unanswered MFJ ownership answer is intentionally Incomplete.

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income for the secondary filer
Fact.Description: The ordinary-income portion of this disqualifying disposition attributed to the secondary filer. It is zero on a non-MFJ return; on MFJ it is the ordinary-income portion when the per-transaction ownership answer is complete and false. A positive disposition with an unanswered MFJ ownership answer remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: ESPP adjusted basis for a disqualifying disposition
Fact.Description: Purchase price plus the ordinary-income portion of the disqualifying disposition. Unclassified or unanswered transactions contribute zero.

Fact.Name: ESPP disqualifying disposition capital gain or loss
Fact.Description: Proceeds less the adjusted basis for an ESPP disqualifying disposition.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 column (g) — the ESPP disqualifying-disposition basis correction
Fact.Description: The ESPP compensation on this row (../esppOrdinaryIncome: the ordinary-income portion of a disqualifying disposition, or the IRC 423(c) discount of a qualifying one, whose basis section 423(c) raises by the same amount), carried into column (g) as a NEGATIVE number, which is what makes column (h) the capital gain Pub. 525 states. WHY COLUMN (g) AND NOT COLUMN (e). The compensation element is a basis increase, and a broker's Form 1099-B does not reflect it: the instructions say to "Increase your" "basis by any amount you included in income upon grant or" "exercise of the option." The printed form then says where the increase goes when the broker reported the basis — column (e) keeps the reported figure and column (g) carries the correction — and the instructions' own worksheet enters a correct basis LARGER than the reported one in column (g) "as a negative number (in parentheses)". This module already routes every basis correction that way (see ../writableCostBasis). ZERO FOR EVERY RETURN THAT IS NOT ONE. ../esppDisqualifyingOrdinaryIncome is complete-safe $0 with the classification unanswered or answered false, so this is $0 and column (g) is untouched on every existing return. It is INCOMPLETE exactly when that fact is — an answered classification whose exercise value or purchase price is missing — so an unfinished disqualifying disposition leaves column (h) incomplete instead of manufacturing the unadjusted gain. BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT IN ADDITION. A row that answers the ESPP classification must leave the compensation element OUT of ../writableCostBasis and OUT of ../writableAdjustmentAmount: column (e) carries the basis as the broker reported it (the option price) and this fact is the whole of the code-B correction for that ordinary income. Entering it by hand as well counts it twice — node case scheduleD/s351-espp-manual-code-b-double-counts measures exactly that and is the reason the application must not offer both entries on one row. THE ORDINARY-INCOME SIDE IS NOT HERE. Pub. 525 puts the same amount on the wages line, and no fact in this dictionary reads /esppDisqualifyingOrdinaryIncomeTotal yet; that consumer belongs to the wages module, not to Schedule D.

Fact.Name: Total ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income
Fact.Description: Guarded sum of the per-row ESPP compensation (../esppOrdinaryIncome) across Form 8949 transactions: the disqualifying-disposition exercise spread AND the IRC 423(c) qualifying-disposition discount, both of which are wages. The path keeps its historical "Disqualifying" name because the income module reads it; the quantity is both arms. An unanswered or empty transaction collection contributes zero.

Fact.Name: Total ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income for the primary filer
Fact.Description: Sum of the per-transaction ESPP ordinary-income portions assigned to the primary filer. A non-MFJ disposition is assigned to the primary filer; an MFJ disposition requires its ownership answer before a positive amount can resolve.

Fact.Name: Total ESPP disqualifying disposition ordinary income for the secondary filer
Fact.Description: Sum of the per-transaction ESPP ordinary-income portions assigned to the secondary filer. It is complete-safe zero on a non-MFJ return; an MFJ positive disposition requires its ownership answer.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-B VOID box
Fact.Description: Form 1099-B: the VOID checkbox in the form's header, printed on Copy A and Copy 1 only (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099b--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the VOID box checked on this Form 1099-B?" (yes/no), on every Form 8949 transaction item that came from a Form 1099-B; never required. Help text: A payer checks VOID only on a Copy A it did not mean to file, so the IRS scanner skips it; a correction is never marked VOID. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — this Form 8949 row's own columns are the facts the return computes from. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-B register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-B CORRECTED box
Fact.Description: Form 1099-B: the CORRECTED checkbox in the form's header, printed on every copy (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099b--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the CORRECTED box checked on this Form 1099-B?" (yes/no), on every Form 8949 transaction item that came from a Form 1099-B; never required. Help text: A checked CORRECTED means this form replaces one the broker already sent; enter the corrected figures, not the originals. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — this Form 8949 row's own columns are the facts the return computes from. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-B register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-B payer's name and address
Fact.Description: Form 1099-B: the PAYER'S name, street address, city or town, state or province, country, ZIP or foreign postal code, and telephone no. block, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099b--2025.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Name and address of the broker or barter exchange shown on this Form 1099-B" (free text), on every Form 8949 transaction item that came from a Form 1099-B; never required. Help text: The payer on a Form 1099-B is the broker or barter exchange that reported the transaction. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — this Form 8949 row's own columns are the facts the return computes from. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-B register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-B payer's TIN
Fact.Description: Form 1099-B: the PAYER'S TIN box, as printed; a broker or barter exchange is a business, so the number printed is an employer identification number (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099b--2025.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Payer's TIN shown on this Form 1099-B" (nine digits), on every Form 8949 transaction item that came from a Form 1099-B; never required. Validation: EIN. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — this Form 8949 row's own columns are the facts the return computes from. Fact.Name: Form 1099-B applicable checkbox on Form 8949
Fact.Description: Form 1099-B: the "Applicable checkbox on Form 8949" entry the broker prints in the form's title block: the Form 8949 box letter this transaction belongs in (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099b--2025.pdf, page 2; recipient instruction at lines 173-176, "Indicates where to report this transaction on Form 8949 and Schedule D (Form 1040), and which checkbox is applicable"). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Applicable checkbox on Form 8949, as printed on this Form 1099-B" (one capital letter), on every Form 8949 transaction item that came from a Form 1099-B; never required. Help text: One letter, as the broker printed it. This dictionary derives the Form 8949 box itself from ../isLongTerm and ../basisReportedToIrs (../isForm8949BoxA and its siblings); this box is the broker's own statement of it, transcribed, and neither overrides the other. Validation: one capital letter (Match [A-Z], MaxLength 1). The form's recipient instruction names no letters. The vendored instructions give the set: a Form 1099-B transaction takes "box A or box B in Part I or box D or box E in Part II" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 4), within Form 8949's full box set "(A, B, C, G, H, or I)" for Part I and "(D, E, F, J, K, or L)" for Part II (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8949.pdf, pages 3-4). The Match accepts any single capital letter rather than only A, B, D or E, because the payer-side Instructions for Form 1099-B, which govern what a broker may print in this box, are not vendored, and a transcription writable must not refuse a letter the broker printed. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — this Form 8949 row's own columns are the facts the return computes from. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-B register.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-B's box 4 federal income tax withheld, or zero
Fact.Description: The answered Form 1099-B box 4 backup withholding on this Form 8949 row, with cents intact; zero when box 4 is unanswered, zero for a negative answer (the Min $0 limit on the writable is not enforced when a fact resolves, so the floor is here), and zero on a row marked as reported on a Form 1099-DA (../reportedOnForm1099DA), which came from no Form 1099-B: its broker's box 4 is entered on the Form 1099-DA and reaches line 25b through /form1099DaFederalIncomeTaxWithheld, so it is not counted twice. No per-document rounding: /form1099BFederalIncomeTaxWithheld sums these and Form 1040 line 25b rounds its total once.

Fact.Name: Total Form 1099-B box 4 federal income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Sum of Form 1099-B box 4 backup withholding over every Form 8949 transaction row on the return, with cents intact: an addend of the Form 1040 line 25b total, taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding, which rounds once. No filer filter, as the Form 1099-NEC and Form 1099-MISC totals: a Form 8949 row carries no owner, and the return's Schedule D reports every row it lists. No Form 8958 line 11 allocation sibling: the graph does not allocate the capital gain or loss these rows report either (Form 8958 line 6 is filer-supplied and print-only here), so the withholding and the income stay together on this return. An empty or unopened collection contributes zero.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 uses an IRS single-amount reporting exception
Fact.Description: True only when a specific Form 8949 instruction permits the known net gain to be entered in column (d), or the known loss magnitude in column (e), with the other amount column left blank. This is not an assertion that the cost basis of an ordinary sale is unknown. Supply a nonnegative amount in the applicable column, select the appropriate reporting box and holding period, and do not duplicate an amount already fed by another form. Only this explicit mode permits the opposite amount column to contribute zero when blank. Pure column-(h)-only reporting is not implemented by this mode. The service must ask this question and retain the reason; an absent answer means ordinary two-amount reporting.

Fact.Name: The row explicitly uses single-amount reporting
Fact.Description: The specific one-amount exception applies only after an affirmative answer. Otherwise ordinary proceeds and basis evidence is required.

Fact.Name: Single-amount reporting has a coherent known amount
Fact.Description: At least one of columns (d) and (e) is answered with a nonnegative known net amount, and the other is blank or zero. Two positive amounts belong to ordinary reporting instead. A stated zero net amount is permitted; two missing amounts are not. This tests arithmetic consistency, not eligibility for the legal exception.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 adjustment codes have been entered
Fact.Description: True for an answered nonempty column-(f) string. An absent or empty string means no code. This is a presence test, not a parser or a determination of the tax treatment. The service must validate uppercase permitted codes, alphabetical order and the absence of whitespace or separators.

Fact.Name: Form 8949 monetary inputs are complete and coherent
Fact.Description: The proceeds, basis and signed adjustment used by column (h) are complete. In the explicit single-amount mode the adjustment must be zero because the entered amount is already the known net gain or loss. Holding-period classification, reporting-box validation and full filing eligibility are separate requirements. False is a diagnostic, not a BlockSubmissionOnTrue refusal.

Fact.Name: Ordinary acquisition and disposition dates are chronological
Fact.Description: When both ordinary dates are supplied, the disposition date is on or after the acquisition date. A reversed pair is inconsistent rather than short-term. Same-day disposition is allowed. The inherited-property override retains its existing attested section 1223(9) conditions. Special tacking, gift, short-sale and nonbusiness-bad-debt rules are not derived by this ordinary-date check.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a has entered evidence
Fact.Description: True when any proceeds, basis, legacy gain/loss or legacy adjustment cell is answered. This is an input-presence predicate; a break-even transaction still counts. The service must not seed these optional scalar inputs merely to initialize an unused row.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a amount columns have been started
Fact.Description: True when either column (d) or column (e) is entered. Once either is present both are required; an old column-(h) answer cannot hide a missing companion amount.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a gain or loss from proceeds less basis
Fact.Description: The signed difference of entered proceeds and cost or other basis, rounded once for the reported line. No adjustment is permitted in this shortcut row. Eligibility also requires the relevant broker-reported basis and no other required corrections; those document-level conditions remain an intake responsibility.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 1a column (h) print value
Fact.Description: The same validated amount used in the capital-gain arithmetic, but no value when the row is unused. A partial or contradictory row stays Incomplete instead of printing the stale independent h input. Its accompanying d/e cells remain bound to their entered amounts.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 8a has entered evidence
Fact.Description: True when any proceeds, basis, legacy gain/loss or legacy adjustment cell is answered. This is an input-presence predicate; a break-even transaction still counts. The service must not seed these optional scalar inputs merely to initialize an unused row.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 8a amount columns have been started
Fact.Description: True when either column (d) or column (e) is entered. Once either is present both are required; an old column-(h) answer cannot hide a missing companion amount.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 8a gain or loss from proceeds less basis
Fact.Description: The signed difference of entered proceeds and cost or other basis, rounded once for the reported line. No adjustment is permitted in this shortcut row. Eligibility also requires the relevant broker-reported basis and no other required corrections; those document-level conditions remain an intake responsibility.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 8a column (h) print value
Fact.Description: The same validated amount used in the capital-gain arithmetic, but no value when the row is unused. A partial or contradictory row stays Incomplete instead of printing the stale independent h input. Its accompanying d/e cells remain bound to their entered amounts.

Fact.Name: Schedule D line 13 capital gain distributions
Fact.Description: The parent return capital-gain distributions plus the Form 8814 line-10 amounts already included by the existing line-15 computation. This materializes their common printed line so the form and arithmetic use one quantity. It does not recompute Form 8814 eligibility, its special-rate components or section 1202 treatment, and does not turn an ordinary distribution-only return into a Schedule D filer. ONE Round on the printed line: the box 2a amounts are added with their cents and only the total is rounded (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 9), so the line stays whole dollars whether or not the Form 1099-DIV module rounds its own sum.

Fact.Name: A Form 8949 transaction was entered on this item (not a document-only Form 1099-B)
Fact.Description: TRUE when any Form 8949 column of this item has been answered: a description, either date, proceeds, cost or other basis, an adjustment amount, an adjustment code, the Part I/Part II attestation, the inherited-property attestation, or the single-amount reporting election. FALSE when none of them is — the item is then a Form 1099-B DOCUMENT carrying no capital transaction, which the intake shape allows: a Form 1099-B that reports only section 1256 contracts (boxes 8 to 11) "has boxes 1a to 1e blank and boxes 8 to 11 filled, and it is still one item on /form8949Transactions" (the collection's own header note). Such an item contributes $0 to every Form 8949 column and sorts as it always has, exactly what node case d052-form1099b-section-1256-only pins. The gate is deliberately WIDE on the transaction side: one answered column is enough to make the row a transaction, and from then on a missing proceeds or basis stays INCOMPLETE (../proceeds, ../costBasis) rather than becoming $0 — node cases form8949-item-partly-entered-stays-incomplete and sdtk-description-only-item-stays-incomplete pin that side. This exists so the missing-input correction does not make the committed document-only contract unfilable.

Fact.Name: Refusal: a Schedule D Form 2439 scalar disagrees with the Form 2439 notice list
Fact.Description: The return lists at least one Form 2439 notice (form2439:/hasForm2439Notices) AND at least one of the two legacy return-level scalars is answered and does not equal its per-notice total: /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm2439 against form2439:/form2439IncludedUnrecapturedSection1250Gain (box 1b), or /writableCollectiblesGainFromForm2439 against form2439:/form2439IncludedCollectiblesGain (box 1d). The list governs both worksheet legs whenever it is non-empty, so a scalar is never added, but a scalar that disagrees with the list means one of the two entries is wrong and this dictionary cannot tell which, so the return is refused rather than filed on the list alone. A scalar equal to its list total is harmless. Complete-safe: FALSE with no notice list (the scalars then carry the legs by themselves, unchecked, as before) and FALSE for an unanswered scalar. Each leg is guarded IsComplete-first on its scalar, after the list test, so an unanswered collection or scalar never leaves this Incomplete; a live notice with no resolvable year makes the included totals Incomplete and this fact with them, the same ruling-6 block the worksheet legs already carry. THE BOX 1a SCALAR IS NOT CHECKED HERE: /writableScheduleDLine11OtherLongTermGains also carries Forms 6252, 6781 and 8824, so no equality holds; its Form 2439 exclusion is by construction and declared.
